path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 P.S. Children›Chapter 28. Federal Credit Unions›PA ST 11 P.S. § 2242. Shares held in the name of a minor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 P.S. Children › Chapter 28. Federal Credit Unions › PA ST 11 P.S. § 2242. Shares held in the name of a minor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 P.S. § 2242. Shares held in the name of a minor (2023)
content:
Any such Federal credit union, having issued shares standing on its books in the name
   of any minor not less than twelve years of age, may pay the dividends or earnings
   thereon, as well as the withdrawal value of such shares, to such minor, without the
   assent of his parent or guardian.  The receipt, acquittance, or other action required by the Federal credit union to
   be taken by the minor shall be binding upon such minor with like effect as if such
   minor were of full age and shall be a valid release to the Federal credit union.  The parent or guardian of such minor shall not, in his capacity as parent or guardian,
   have the power to attach or in any manner transfer any shares issued to or standing
   in the name of such minor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 P.S. Children›Chapter 32. Medical Consent Act›PA ST 11 P.S. § 2512. Legislative intent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 P.S. Children › Chapter 32. Medical Consent Act › PA ST 11 P.S. § 2512. Legislative intent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 P.S. § 2512. Legislative intent (2023)
content:
It is the intent of the General Assembly to provide a mechanism similar to a power
   of attorney whereby parents may confer the power to consent to medical and mental
   health treatment of their children upon a relative or family friend in order to enable
   those who are temporarily unable to care for the needs of their children to ensure
   that the medical and mental health needs of the children are met without terminating
   or limiting in any way the legal rights of the parents.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 P.S. Children›Chapter 28. Federal Credit Unions›PA ST 11 P.S. § 2241. Joint accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 P.S. Children › Chapter 28. Federal Credit Unions › PA ST 11 P.S. § 2241. Joint accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 P.S. § 2241. Joint accounts (2023)
content:
Whenever shares of a Federal credit union existing under the Act of Congress approved
   June 26, 1934, c. 750, 48 Stat. 1216, its amendments and supplements, known as the
   Federal Credit Union Act,1shall be issued in the names of two or more persons as joint tenants with right of
   survivorship and one or more of such persons is a minor, and such shares shall have
   been subscribed for under an arrangement with the Federal credit union whereby the
   dividends or earnings thereon, or the withdrawal value thereof, may be paid upon receipt,
   acquittance or other action, as the case may be, of either or any of such persons,
   the Federal credit union may pay such dividends or earnings or withdrawal value upon
   such receipt, acquittance, or other action, as the case may be, of either or any of
   such minors who shall be not less than sixteen years of age, pursuant to the arrangement
   provided for in this section, notwithstanding the fact that one or more of the other
   persons may be dead and the Federal credit union has notice thereof;  and such receipt,
   acquittance or other action shall be binding upon such minor with like effect as if
   such minor were of full age and shall be a valid release to the Federal credit union.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 P.S. Children›Chapter 32. Medical Consent Act›PA ST 11 P.S. § 2513. Medical and mental health care consent
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 P.S. Children › Chapter 32. Medical Consent Act › PA ST 11 P.S. § 2513. Medical and mental health care consent
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 P.S. § 2513. Medical and mental health care consent (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A parent, legal guardian or legal custodian of a minor may confer upon an adult person
      who is a relative or family friend the power to consent to medical, surgical, dental,
      developmental, mental health or other treatment to be rendered to the minor under
      the supervision of or upon the advice of a physician, nurse, school nurse, dentist,
      mental health or other health care professional licensed to practice in this Commonwealth
      and to exercise any existing parental rights to obtain records and information with
      regard to the health care services and insurance unless the minor is in the custody
      of a county child and youth agency or there is currently in effect a prior order of
      a court in any jurisdiction which would prohibit the parent, legal guardian or legal
      custodian from exercising the power that the parent, legal guardian or legal custodian
      seeks to confer.  When a parent's rights have not been terminated or voluntarily relinquished, nothing
      in this subsection shall divest a parent of the power to consent to his children's
      medical or mental health treatment.  The authorization may also include the right to act as the minor's legal representative
      for the purposes of receiving informational materials regarding vaccines under section
      2126 of the Public Health Service Act (58 Stat. 682,42 U.S.C. § 300aa-26).  Conferral of powers authorized by this subsection shall not be used to compel the
      production or release of records or information to which the parent, legal guardian
      or legal custodian would not themselves be entitled to review, receive or authorize
      release to others.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 P.S. Children›Chapter 28. Federal Credit Unions›PA ST 11 P.S. § 2243. Shares held as trustee
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 P.S. Children › Chapter 28. Federal Credit Unions › PA ST 11 P.S. § 2243. Shares held as trustee
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 P.S. § 2243. Shares held as trustee (2023)
content:
Whenever shares of such a Federal credit union shall be issued to any person, describing
   himself, in subscribing for such shares, as trustee for any person or persons, and
   no other notice of the existence and terms of a valid trust than such description
   shall have been given to the Federal credit union, the dividends or earnings on such
   shares, as well as the withdrawal value of such shares, shall, in the event of the
   death of the person so described as trustee, be paid to the person or persons for
   whose benefit the shares were stated to have been subscribed if, at the time of payment,
   such beneficiary is not less than sixteen years of age.  Payment may be made to any such beneficiary who is not less than sixteen years of
   age under the same conditions as if such shares had been originally subscribed for
   by him.  If there are two or more beneficiaries named on any such shares, the Federal credit
   union shall, in the absence of written notice to the contrary, make payment to such
   of the beneficiaries as may survive the trustee, in equal portions.  The receipt or acquittance of any such beneficiary or beneficiaries for payments,
   made in accordance with this section, shall be a full, complete and valid release
   of the Federal credit union from any further liability for the amounts so paid.

      appropriate activities and experiences.  A child with a disability or special needs in an out-of-home placement shall have
      the same access to age-appropriate or developmentally appropriate activities and experiences
      as the child's nondisabled peers, even if reasonable accommodations are required.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10204. Resolution certification and form (2023)
content:
The governing body of a municipal corporation that adopts an incorporation resolution
   shall certify the incorporation resolution to the county board of elections of each
   proper county.  The county board of elections shall, at the general or municipal election in the
   manner required by the Pennsylvania Election Code, submit a referendum question to
   the registered voters of the municipal corporation that has certified an incorporation
   resolution.

   be voting on a referendum question shall be given by the secretary or other person
   designated by the municipal corporation.  The notice required under this section shall be published once a week for four successive
   weeks in a newspaper of general circulation in the municipal corporation in which
   the referendum question will be submitted to the registered voters.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10302. Hearing and decree (2023)
content:
(a) Date and publication.--Upon presentation to the court of the petition and resolution under section 10301
      (relating to resolution and petition), the court shall set a day for a hearing on
      the question of the change in the corporate title of the city and shall direct that
      notice of the hearing be published once a week for three weeks in a newspaper of general
      circulation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 102. Procedures for Incorporation›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10207. Letters patent and boundaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 102. Procedures for Incorporation › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10207. Letters patent and boundaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10207. Letters patent and boundaries (2023)
content:
If the returns of an election under section 10204.1 (relating to notice of election)
   show that a majority of registered voters in a municipal corporation voted “yes” on
   the referendum question, within 60 days after the election, the governing body of
   the municipal corporation shall furnish to the Secretary of the Commonwealth the necessary
   information with respect to the boundaries of the new city, and the Governor shall
   issue letters patent, under the Great Seal of the Commonwealth, reciting the facts,
   defining the boundaries of the city and constituting the city as a body corporate
   and politic by the name of the “City of․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․․.”

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 102. Procedures for Incorporation›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10206. Vote against incorporating as city
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 102. Procedures for Incorporation › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10206. Vote against incorporating as city
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10206. Vote against incorporating as city (2023)
content:
If the returns of an election under section 10204.1 (relating to notice of election)
   show that a majority of registered voters in a municipal corporation voted “no” on
   the referendum question, further proceedings may not occur, and another election on
   the referendum question may not be held in the municipal corporation until the third
   ensuing general or municipal election.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10401. General power of council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10401. General power of council (2023)
content:
(a) Power.--In addition to reapportionment of wards under 53 Pa.C.S. Ch. 9 (relating to municipal
      reapportionment) andsection 11 of Article IX of the Constitution of Pennsylvania, a council may, with or without a petition as provided under section 10401.1 (relating
      to petition of registered voters) and subject to approval by the registered voters
      as provided under section 10407 (relating to voting procedures), create a new ward,
      divide a ward or wards or detach part of a ward and attach it to another ward, in
      accordance with this chapter.

content:
(a) Existing government.--The government of the municipal corporation shall continue in full force and operation
      until the first Monday of January next succeeding the municipal election under section
      10702 (relating to first elections in newly created cities).  On the first Monday of January next succeeding the municipal election under section
      10702, the officers of the city chosen at the municipal election shall begin their
      terms of service, and the city government shall be organized under this part.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 102. Procedures for Incorporation›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10210. Existing liabilities, debts and claims

content:
If a municipal corporation is incorporated as a city in accordance with this part,

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 103. Change of Corporate Title›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10303. Recording decree
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 103. Change of Corporate Title › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10303. Recording decree
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10303. Recording decree (2023)
content:
A change in the corporate title of a city that is ordered in accordance with section
   10302(c) (relating to hearing and decree) may not take effect until a certified copy
   of the decree of court is filed in the office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth
   and is recorded in the office of the recorder of deeds of the county in which the
   city is located.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 103. Change of Corporate Title›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10304. Existing rights and liabilities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 103. Change of Corporate Title › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10304. Existing rights and liabilities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10304. Existing rights and liabilities (2023)
content: A change in the corporate title of a city shall not affect any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10405. Notice of election and review of report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10405. Notice of election and review of report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10405. Notice of election and review of report (2023)
content:
(a) Publication.--A city must publish a notice of election in a newspaper of general circulation at
      least 15 days prior to the date that the question of approving the creation, division
      or detachment of a ward is to be presented at the specified general or municipal election.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10401.1. Petition of registered voters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10401.1. Petition of registered voters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10401.1. Petition of registered voters (2023)
content:
(a) Initiation of proceedings.--Registered voters may petition council to initiate proceedings under section 10401
      (relating to general power of council) to create new wards, divide a ward or wards
      or detach part of a ward and attach it to another ward as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10403.1. Expenses of commissioners
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10403.1. Expenses of commissioners
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10403.1. Expenses of commissioners (2023)
content:
Council must make an appropriation for reasonable expenses incurred by commissioners
   for service under this chapter.  Each commissioner shall submit for approval an itemized account of the commissioner's
   expenses to the city controller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10407. Voting procedures
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10407. Voting procedures
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10407. Voting procedures (2023)
content:
(a) Publication.--The county board of elections must tabulate and publish the results of the referendum
      in a newspaper of general circulation within 30 days of the election.  A certified copy of the results shall be placed on record with the minutes of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10406. Election laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10406. Election laws
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10406. Election laws (2023)
content:
Each matter relating to the election at which the question of approving the creation,
   division or detachment of a ward or is to be presented to the voters shall be governed
   by the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 108. Vacancies in Office›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10801. Council and office of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 108. Vacancies in Office › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10801. Council and office of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10801. Council and office of mayor (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Within 30 days of a vacancy in the office of mayor or other member of council or if
      an elected mayor or council member has failed to qualify under section 10701 (relating
      to elected officers, term, reelection and vacancy) prior to taking office, council
      must, by a majority of council's remaining members, appoint a qualified individual
      to fill the vacant office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10404. Election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10404. Election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10404. Election (2023)
content:
(a) Certification.--If, based upon the report under section 10403.2 (relating to report), council decides
      to proceed, council shall certify to the county board of elections the question of
      the creation, division or detachment of the ward to be submitted to the registered
      voters of each ward which are the subject of the report at the general or municipal
      election occurring not less than 90 days after the report was approved by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 107. Elected Officers and Elections›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10702. First elections in newly created cities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 107. Elected Officers and Elections › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10702. First elections in newly created cities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10702. First elections in newly created cities (2023)
content:
(a) Election.--At the first municipal election occurring at least 90 days after the date of the letters
      patent issued by the Governor incorporating the city, the registered voters of the
      city shall elect city officials as provided under section 10701(a)(1) (relating to
      elected officers, term, reelection and vacancy).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10409. Pennsylvania Election Code
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10409. Pennsylvania Election Code
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10409. Pennsylvania Election Code (2023)
content:
Nothing under this chapter shall be construed as affecting the powers and duties of
   the court of common pleas or the county board of elections and restrictions on alteration
   of election districts as provided under Article V of the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

content: (a) Elected officer and term.--

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 107. Elected Officers and Elections › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10703. Nominations and elections
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10703. Nominations and elections (2023)
content:
Each matter relating to a nomination of a candidate and election of a city officer
   shall be governed by the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10902. Number, duties and compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10902. Number, duties and compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10902. Number, duties and compensation (2023)
content:
(a) Prescription.--Except as otherwise provided under this chapter, council may prescribe, by ordinance,
      the number, duties and compensation of the officers and employees of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10903. Salary, compensation and emoluments of officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10903. Salary, compensation and emoluments of officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10903. Salary, compensation and emoluments of officers (2023)
content:
(a) Prohibition.--A city may not increase or diminish the salary, compensation or emoluments of an elected
      officer after the officer's election.  A change in salary, compensation or emoluments of an elected office shall take effect
      at the beginning of the next term of the member of council or other elected official.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 107. Elected Officers and Elections›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10704. Certificates of election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 107. Elected Officers and Elections › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10704. Certificates of election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10704. Certificates of election (2023)
content:
After the election of city officers under this chapter, the county board of elections
   must issue and the officer-elect must procure a certificate of election.  The officer-elect must present the certificate of election to council on the date
   and time provided under law for council's organization.  The certificate must be filed with the city archives, and the certificate's presentation
   must be noted in the minutes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10408. Change of ward lines by council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 104. Creation and Division of Wards › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10408. Change of ward lines by council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10408. Change of ward lines by council (2023)
content:
If council determines during proceedings for the division or creation of a ward that
   any of the boundaries or divisions are uncertain, council must determine the relocation
   of the line to conform as nearly as possible to the previously determined boundary
   lines so that each ward in the city is composed of compact and contiguous territory
   as nearly equal in population as practicable as officially and finally reported in
   the most recent Federal decennial or special census.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 108. Vacancies in Office›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10802. Controller and treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 108. Vacancies in Office › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10802. Controller and treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10802. Controller and treasurer (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Within 30 days after a vacancy occurs in the office of city controller or in the office
      of city treasurer or if an elected city controller or city treasurer has failed to
      qualify under section 10701 (relating to elected officers, term, reelection and vacancy)
      prior to taking office, council must appoint a qualified individual to fill the vacant
      office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10904. Offices to be held until qualification of successors

content:
(a) Successor.--An officer of a city, who has been elected or appointed and has qualified under this
      chapter, shall hold office until the officer's successor meets all of the following:

content:
(a) Delivered.--All money, accounts, property, documents or effects belonging to the city in the possession
      of an officer of the city shall be either:

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10917. Powers of subpoena and compelling testimony (2023)
content:
(a) Applicability.--This section shall apply to any of the following which are specifically empowered

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10905. Oath of office, violation of oath and penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10905. Oath of office, violation of oath and penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10905. Oath of office, violation of oath and penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Oath required.--Each officer of the city, whether elected or appointed, shall, before entering upon
      the officer's respective duties, take and subscribe an oath or affirmation of office
      pursuant to53 Pa.C.S. § 1141(relating to form of oaths of office).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11002. Vesting of legislative power
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11002. Vesting of legislative power
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11002. Vesting of legislative power (2023)
content:
The legislative power of every city shall be vested in a council composed of the mayor
   and council members.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10918. Consolidation or integration of fire and police personnel prohibited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10918. Consolidation or integration of fire and police personnel prohibited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10918. Consolidation or integration of fire and police personnel prohibited (2023)
content:
A city may not consolidate, integrate or reorganize the paid members of the fire force
   and the paid members of the police force into one bureau or organization.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10906. Bond to be given by officers and agents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10906. Bond to be given by officers and agents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10906. Bond to be given by officers and agents (2023)
content:
(a) Bond.--In addition to the requirements for bonding that may be imposed by this chapter or
      any other law, council may require from each elected or appointed officer and agent
      of the city a lawful bond with corporate surety for the faithful performance of his
      or her duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10908. Officers not to become surety on bonds given to city and penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 109. City Officers and Employees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10908. Officers not to become surety on bonds given to city and penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 10908. Officers not to become surety on bonds given to city and penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Surety.--A city officer or member of council may not become the surety on a bond or obligation
      given to the city by an agent or contractor for the faithful performance of a trust,
      agency or contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016. Salaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016. Salaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016. Salaries (2023)
content:
(a) Salary.--Except as provided in subsection (b), a council member shall receive an annual salary
      for the member's service during the member's term.  The salary shall be fixed by ordinance and payable in regular installments.  Council may, by an ordinance fixing the salaries, provide for the assessment and
      retention from the salaries of reasonable fines for absence from regular or special
      meetings of council or committees of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11015. Attendance of witnesses and production of books before council or committee of council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11015. Attendance of witnesses and production of books before council or committee of council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11015. Attendance of witnesses and production of books before council or committee of council (2023)
content:
(a) Subpoenas.--Council may compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books, papers
      and other evidence at a meeting of the body or a committee of council.  A subpoena signed by the mayor or the chairperson of the committee may be issued
      in a pending case of inquiry or investigation.  The subpoena may be served and executed in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11004. Oath of council members, quorum and rules

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11004. Oath of council members, quorum and rules (2023)
content:
(a) Oath.--The members of council shall take the oath of office provided for in section 10905
      (relating to oath of office, violation of oath and penalty).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.2. Voting, no veto and vote necessary to enact ordinances or adopt resolutions

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11003. Organization of council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11003. Organization of council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11003. Organization of council (2023)
content:
(a) Organization.--On the first Monday of the January following the regular municipal election, the members
      of council shall assemble at the usual place of meeting for the purpose of organizing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.1. Ordinances and resolutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.1. Ordinances and resolutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.1. Ordinances and resolutions (2023)
content: (a) Ordinances.--With regard to ordinances, the following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.7. Payments not authorized by law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.7. Payments not authorized by law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.7. Payments not authorized by law (2023)
content:
An ordinance may not be enacted and a resolution may not be adopted providing for
   the payment of money by the city without previous authority of law.  An officer executing a document authorizing payment, making a payment or passing
   a voucher for a payment not authorized by law commits a misdemeanor.  The officer shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than
   $5,000 and to imprisonment for not more than one year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016.1. Appointment of city clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016.1. Appointment of city clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016.1. Appointment of city clerk (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Council shall appoint a city clerk, whose compensation shall be fixed by ordinance,
      who meets all the following criteria:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.3. Journal of proceedings, recording and withholding of vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.3. Journal of proceedings, recording and withholding of vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.3. Journal of proceedings, recording and withholding of vote (2023)
content:
(a) Journal.--Council shall keep a journal of the proceedings.  The journal shall be in the possession of the city clerk and shall, at all times,
      be open to public inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.6. Reading of proposed ordinances and final enactment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.6. Reading of proposed ordinances and final enactment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.6. Reading of proposed ordinances and final enactment (2023)
content:
(a) Reading.--The title of every proposed ordinance shall be read at least twice, once when introduced
      and again before final enactment by council.  Amendments or other changes to the proposed ordinance shall be read in their entirety.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.9. Publication of proposed ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.9. Publication of proposed ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.9. Publication of proposed ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) Publication required.--A proposed ordinance, except as otherwise provided in this chapter, shall be published
      in a newspaper of general circulation not more than 60 days nor fewer than seven days
      prior to enactment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.5. Proposed ordinances and titles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.5. Proposed ordinances and titles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.5. Proposed ordinances and titles (2023)
content:
(a) Format.--A proposed ordinance shall be presented to council in written form as a bill and shall
      be numbered sequentially for the calendar year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.4. Signing and attesting ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.4. Signing and attesting ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.4. Signing and attesting ordinances (2023)
content:
A legislative act of council shall be by ordinance.  An ordinance enacted by council shall be signed by the mayor and attested by the
   city clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.14. Maps, plans or drawings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.14. Maps, plans or drawings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.14. Maps, plans or drawings (2023)
content:
(a) Adoption.--Except as otherwise provided under the Municipalities Planning Code, if maps, plans
      or drawings are to be adopted as part of an ordinance, council, instead of publishing
      the maps, plans or drawings as part of the ordinance may make reference to, in publishing
      the ordinance or a summary of the ordinance, the location where the maps, plans or
      drawings are on file and may be examined.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.8. Time of taking effect of ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.8. Time of taking effect of ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.8. Time of taking effect of ordinances (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise provided by law, an ordinance, except those pertaining to the subjects
   set forth in section 11050(b) (relating to time ordinances go into effect), shall
   take effect after:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.13. Standard or nationally recognized codes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.13. Standard or nationally recognized codes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.13. Standard or nationally recognized codes (2023)
content:
(a) Authority to enact.--In the same manner as other ordinances, and except as otherwise provided in this chapter
      or the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act,1council may enact, by reference to a standard or nationally recognized code, all
      or a portion of the standard or nationally recognized code as an ordinance of the
      city.  Three copies of the proposed standard or nationally recognized code, portion of
      the code or amendment to the code shall be filed in the office of the city clerk at
      least 10 days before council considers the proposed ordinance.  Upon enactment, a copy shall be kept with the ordinance book and available for public
      use, inspection and examination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.11. Records of ordinances maintained by city clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.11. Records of ordinances maintained by city clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.11. Records of ordinances maintained by city clerk (2023)
content:
(a) Records.--Within one month after enactment, each ordinance shall be certified and recorded by
      the city clerk in a book provided by the city which shall, at all times, be open to
      the inspection of the public.  Within one month after adoption, each resolution pertaining to a tax levy shall
      be certified and recorded by the city clerk in a book provided by the city which shall,
      at all times, be open to the inspection of the public.  A standard or nationally recognized code or a portion of the standard or nationally
      recognized code enacted by reference need not be recorded in or attached to the ordinance
      book but shall be deemed to have been legally recorded if the ordinance by which the
      code was enacted by reference is recorded, with an accompanying notation stating where
      the full text of the code is filed.  A failure to record within the time provided shall not be deemed a defect in the
      process of the enactment or adoption of the ordinance or of the resolution that pertains
      to a tax levy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.17. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.17. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.17. Penalty (2023)
content:
A person who violates an ordinance enacted under the authority of this chapter for
   which no penalty is specified commits a summary offense and, upon conviction, shall
   be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than $1,000 or to imprisonment for not more
   than 90 days, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.16. Enforcement of ordinances, recovery and payment of fines and penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.16. Enforcement of ordinances, recovery and payment of fines and penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.16. Enforcement of ordinances, recovery and payment of fines and penalties (2023)
content:
(a) Enforcement.--An action, prosecution, complaint or proceeding for the violation of an ordinance
      of the city and for the fine, penalty and forfeiture imposed shall be instituted in
      the corporate name of the city and be conducted in the manner prescribed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11032. Signing and oath
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11032. Signing and oath
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11032. Signing and oath (2023)
content:
(a) Petition.--A petition for the submission of a proposed ordinance shall be signed in the city
      clerk's office.  The petition shall be retained in the city clerk's office at all times for a period
      of 15 days.  Each signer shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.12. Proof and evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.12. Proof and evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.12. Proof and evidence (2023)
content:
(a) Proof.--An ordinance, resolution, motion or other proceeding of council may be proved by the
      certificate of the city clerk under the corporate seal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.15. Codification of ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.15. Codification of ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.15. Codification of ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) Preparation authorized.--Council may prepare a consolidation or codification of the general body of city ordinances
      or the ordinances on a particular subject.  Council may adopt the consolidation or codification as an ordinance of the city
      in the same manner prescribed for the adoption of an ordinance, except as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.10. Filing of proposed ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.10. Filing of proposed ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.10. Filing of proposed ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) Place of filing.--If the full text is not published, an attested copy of the proposed ordinance shall
      be filed when the summary of the ordinance is published in the county law library
      or other county office designated by the county commissioners.  The county commissioners may impose a fee no greater than necessary to cover the
      actual costs of storing the proposed ordinances.  Filing with the county may be completed by the submission of an electronic copy
      of the ordinance through a method available, in the sole discretion of the county,
      to permit receipt by the office storing municipal ordinances.  Upon request by the city, the county shall notify the city of the method by which
      electronic copies may be submitted.  The county may store the ordinance electronically, provided that the public is able
      to access the electronically stored city ordinances during regular business hours
      at the office or at a remote location.  The city shall retain a printed copy of the e-mail and ordinance as transmitted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11034. Submission to council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11034. Submission to council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11034. Submission to council (2023)
content:
If the petition is certified to contain signatures as required in section 11033(a)(2)
   (relating to number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk), the
   city clerk shall submit the petition to council without delay.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11031. Petition and notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11031. Petition and notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11031. Petition and notice (2023)
content:
If the city clerk receives a written request for the preparation of a petition for
   the submission of a proposed ordinance to council by at least 100 qualified electors
   of the city and the request is accompanied by a copy of the proposed ordinance, within
   10 days of receipt the city clerk shall do each of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11033. Number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11033. Number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11033. Number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk (2023)
content:
(a) Signatures.--Within 10 days after the period of time for signing the petition has elapsed, the
      city clerk shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11030. Initiation of proposed ordinances by petition and exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11030. Initiation of proposed ordinances by petition and exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11030. Initiation of proposed ordinances by petition and exceptions (2023)
content:
(a) Submission.--Except as provided in subsection (b), a proposed ordinance may be submitted to council
      by a petition signed by the electors of a city in accordance with this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11037. Effect of majority vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11037. Effect of majority vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11037. Effect of majority vote (2023)
content:
If the majority of the qualified electors voting on the proposed ordinance vote in
   favor of the ordinance, the ordinance shall become a valid and binding ordinance of
   the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11035. Actions by council and notices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11035. Actions by council and notices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11035. Actions by council and notices (2023)
content:
If the petition accompanying the proposed ordinance is signed by electors of the city
   as required in section 11033(a)(2) (relating to number of signatures, examination
   and certificate by city clerk), council shall do one of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11038. No repeal within two years
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11038. No repeal within two years
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11038. No repeal within two years (2023)
content:
An ordinance proposed by petition, whether enacted by council or adopted by a vote
   of the electors, shall not be repealed or amended within two years of the effective
   date except by a vote of the electors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11041. Publication of proposed ordinance, repeal or amendment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11041. Publication of proposed ordinance, repeal or amendment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11041. Publication of proposed ordinance, repeal or amendment (2023)
content:
Whenever a proposed ordinance is to be submitted to the electors of the city at an
   election or an ordinance is submitted by council for repeal or amendment, notice of
   the election and text of the question to be submitted to the electors shall be published
   in the same manner as publication is required in section 1201 of the Pennsylvania
   Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11039. Number of proposed ordinances to be submitted and elections limited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11039. Number of proposed ordinances to be submitted and elections limited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11039. Number of proposed ordinances to be submitted and elections limited (2023)
content:
Any number of proposed ordinances may be voted upon at the same election, in accordance
   with the provisions of this subchapter.  Proposed ordinances on the same subject matter shall not be submitted by petition
   more frequently than once every three years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11036. Form of ballot on submission to vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11036. Form of ballot on submission to vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11036. Form of ballot on submission to vote (2023)
content:
The question to be submitted to the electors on the proposed ordinance shall be framed
   to state the nature of the proposed ordinance, followed by the words “yes” and “no”.  The question shall be placed on the ballot which shall be counted, returned and
   computed in accordance with section 11062 (relating to computing and filing returns)
   and the election laws of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11050. Time ordinances go into effect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11050. Time ordinances go into effect
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11050. Time ordinances go into effect (2023)
content:
(a) Timing.--Except as provided in subsection (b), an ordinance enacted by council may not go into
      effect before 10 days from the time of the ordinance's final enactment by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11051. Petition and reconsideration of ordinance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11051. Petition and reconsideration of ordinance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11051. Petition and reconsideration of ordinance (2023)
content:
With the exception of an ordinance dealing with the subjects set forth in section
   11050(b) (relating to time ordinances go into effect), an ordinance shall be suspended
   from going into operation and shall be reconsidered by council if all of the following
   occur:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11040. Submission for repeal by council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11040. Submission for repeal by council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11040. Submission for repeal by council (2023)
content:
Council may submit a proposition for the repeal or amendment of an ordinance to be
   voted upon at a succeeding municipal, general or primary election occurring at least
   90 days after council's submission of the proposition.  Should the submitted proposition receive a majority of the votes cast on the proposition
   at the election, the ordinance shall be repealed or amended accordingly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11052. Preparation of petition by city clerk and notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11052. Preparation of petition by city clerk and notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11052. Preparation of petition by city clerk and notice (2023)
content:
(a) Petition.--A petition under section 11051 (relating to petition and reconsideration of ordinance)
      shall be prepared by the city clerk immediately upon receipt by the clerk of the written
      request of 100 qualified electors of the city asking that the petition be prepared.  Upon preparation of the petition, the clerk shall give notice by publication in
      a newspaper of general circulation:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11056. Ascertainment of number of signers and report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11056. Ascertainment of number of signers and report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11056. Ascertainment of number of signers and report (2023)
content:
After presentation of the petition to council, the city clerk shall ascertain whether
   or not the referendum petition is signed by a number of registered electors equal
   to 20% of all the votes cast for all candidates for mayor at the last preceding municipal
   election at which a mayor was elected.  Council may allow the clerk additional help for that purpose.  After the clerk has made the examination, the clerk shall report the result to council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11063. Effect of vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11063. Effect of vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11063. Effect of vote (2023)
content:
If a majority of the electors vote in favor of the ordinance, the ordinance shall
   take effect when the results of the election are certified by council.  If a majority of the electors vote against the ordinance, the ordinance shall be
   nullified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11054. Signatures, oath and time of signing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11054. Signatures, oath and time of signing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11054. Signatures, oath and time of signing (2023)
content:
(a) Signers.--Each signer of a petition under section 11051 (relating to petition and reconsideration
      of ordinance) shall also do all the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11053. Additional petitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11053. Additional petitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11053. Additional petitions (2023)
content:
(a) Petitions.--In order to facilitate the signing of the petition, the city clerk shall make at least
      two additional similar petitions for signing by the qualified electors.  Signing an additional similar petition shall have the same force and effect as signing
      the original petition.  The city clerk is authorized to employ at least two individuals to take charge of
      the additional petitions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11059. Effect of petition and submission to electors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11059. Effect of petition and submission to electors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11059. Effect of petition and submission to electors (2023)
content:
(a) Petition lacking signatures.--If it appears that the petition under this subchapter has not been signed by the required
      number of electors, no action shall be taken.  The ordinance shall be taken to be in full force from the time or times it would
      have gone into effect had there been no petition against the ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11060. Certification to county board of elections, ballots or ballot labels and expense of elections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11060. Certification to county board of elections, ballots or ballot labels and expense of elections
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11060. Certification to county board of elections, ballots or ballot labels and expense of elections (2023)
content:
(a) Certification.--The city clerk, after consultation with the city solicitor, shall certify to the county
      board of elections a copy of the ordinance and the proceedings of council directing
      the referendum vote.  The county board of elections shall cause the question to be printed for use in
      the election districts of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11055. Presentation of petition to council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11055. Presentation of petition to council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11055. Presentation of petition to council (2023)
content:
At the expiration of 10 days, the petition shall be filed with council and presented
   by the city clerk at council's next meeting.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11061. Form of ballot or ballot label
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11061. Form of ballot or ballot label
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11061. Form of ballot or ballot label (2023)
content:
The ballot used when voting on the ordinance shall contain a question stating the
   nature of the referred ordinance followed by the words “yes” and “no” and shall be
   conducted in the manner as provided in the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11062. Computing and filing returns
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11062. Computing and filing returns
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11062. Computing and filing returns (2023)
content:
(a) Computing.--An officer holding an election shall keep a tally sheet and make a return of votes
      on the referendum question in the same manner as a tally sheet is kept and a return
      is made in an election of officers and the submission of other questions as provided
      by the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 110. Council›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11064. Publication of ordinance before election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 110. Council › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11064. Publication of ordinance before election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11064. Publication of ordinance before election (2023)
content:
Before any referendum is held on any ordinance in accordance with this subchapter,
   the city shall provide notice of the ordinance by publishing a copy of the ordinance
   in a newspaper of general circulation.  Publication in accordance with this section shall be in addition to the publication
   requirements of the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11001. Qualifications of council members (2023)
content: (a) Requirements.--A council member shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11002. Vesting of legislative power
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11002. Vesting of legislative power
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11002. Vesting of legislative power (2023)
content:
The legislative power of every city shall be vested in a council composed of the mayor
   and council members.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11015. Attendance of witnesses and production of books before council or committee of council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11015. Attendance of witnesses and production of books before council or committee of council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11015. Attendance of witnesses and production of books before council or committee of council (2023)
content:
(a) Subpoenas.--Council may compel the attendance of witnesses and the production of books, papers
      and other evidence at a meeting of the body or a committee of council.  A subpoena signed by the mayor or the chairperson of the committee may be issued
      in a pending case of inquiry or investigation.  The subpoena may be served and executed in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11003. Organization of council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11003. Organization of council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11003. Organization of council (2023)
content:
(a) Organization.--On the first Monday of the January following the regular municipal election, the members
      of council shall assemble at the usual place of meeting for the purpose of organizing.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11005. Meetings of council, notice and participation by telecommunication device
