citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11005. Meetings of council, notice and participation by telecommunication device (2023)
content: (a) Meetings.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016.1. Appointment of city clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016.1. Appointment of city clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016.1. Appointment of city clerk (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Council shall appoint a city clerk, whose compensation shall be fixed by ordinance,
      who meets all the following criteria:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016. Salaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016. Salaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11016. Salaries (2023)
content:
(a) Salary.--Except as provided in subsection (b), a council member shall receive an annual salary
      for the member's service during the member's term.  The salary shall be fixed by ordinance and payable in regular installments.  Council may, by an ordinance fixing the salaries, provide for the assessment and
      retention from the salaries of reasonable fines for absence from regular or special
      meetings of council or committees of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.3. Journal of proceedings, recording and withholding of vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.3. Journal of proceedings, recording and withholding of vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.3. Journal of proceedings, recording and withholding of vote (2023)
content:
(a) Journal.--Council shall keep a journal of the proceedings.  The journal shall be in the possession of the city clerk and shall, at all times,
      be open to public inspection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. General Provisions›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11004. Oath of council members, quorum and rules
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. General Provisions › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11004. Oath of council members, quorum and rules
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11004. Oath of council members, quorum and rules (2023)
content:
(a) Oath.--The members of council shall take the oath of office provided for in section 10905
      (relating to oath of office, violation of oath and penalty).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.1. Ordinances and resolutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.1. Ordinances and resolutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.1. Ordinances and resolutions (2023)
content: (a) Ordinances.--With regard to ordinances, the following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.2. Voting, no veto and vote necessary to enact ordinances or adopt resolutions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.2. Voting, no veto and vote necessary to enact ordinances or adopt resolutions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.2. Voting, no veto and vote necessary to enact ordinances or adopt resolutions (2023)
content:
(a) Voting generally.--Members of council present or participating via a telecommunication device shall vote
      on each question before council, except:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.6. Reading of proposed ordinances and final enactment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.6. Reading of proposed ordinances and final enactment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.6. Reading of proposed ordinances and final enactment (2023)
content:
(a) Reading.--The title of every proposed ordinance shall be read at least twice, once when introduced
      and again before final enactment by council.  Amendments or other changes to the proposed ordinance shall be read in their entirety.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.10. Filing of proposed ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.10. Filing of proposed ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.10. Filing of proposed ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) Place of filing.--If the full text is not published, an attested copy of the proposed ordinance shall
      be filed when the summary of the ordinance is published in the county law library
      or other county office designated by the county commissioners.  The county commissioners may impose a fee no greater than necessary to cover the
      actual costs of storing the proposed ordinances.  Filing with the county may be completed by the submission of an electronic copy
      of the ordinance through a method available, in the sole discretion of the county,
      to permit receipt by the office storing municipal ordinances.  Upon request by the city, the county shall notify the city of the method by which
      electronic copies may be submitted.  The county may store the ordinance electronically, provided that the public is able
      to access the electronically stored city ordinances during regular business hours
      at the office or at a remote location.  The city shall retain a printed copy of the e-mail and ordinance as transmitted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.5. Proposed ordinances and titles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.5. Proposed ordinances and titles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.5. Proposed ordinances and titles (2023)
content:
(a) Format.--A proposed ordinance shall be presented to council in written form as a bill and shall
      be numbered sequentially for the calendar year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.7. Payments not authorized by law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.7. Payments not authorized by law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.7. Payments not authorized by law (2023)
content:
An ordinance may not be enacted and a resolution may not be adopted providing for
   the payment of money by the city without previous authority of law.  An officer executing a document authorizing payment, making a payment or passing
   a voucher for a payment not authorized by law commits a misdemeanor.  The officer shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than
   $5,000 and to imprisonment for not more than one year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.4. Signing and attesting ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.4. Signing and attesting ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.4. Signing and attesting ordinances (2023)
content:
A legislative act of council shall be by ordinance.  An ordinance enacted by council shall be signed by the mayor and attested by the
   city clerk.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.8. Time of taking effect of ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.8. Time of taking effect of ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.8. Time of taking effect of ordinances (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise provided by law, an ordinance, except those pertaining to the subjects
   set forth in section 11050(b) (relating to time ordinances go into effect), shall
   take effect after:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.9. Publication of proposed ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.9. Publication of proposed ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.9. Publication of proposed ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) Publication required.--A proposed ordinance, except as otherwise provided in this chapter, shall be published
      in a newspaper of general circulation not more than 60 days nor fewer than seven days
      prior to enactment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.16. Enforcement of ordinances, recovery and payment of fines and penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.16. Enforcement of ordinances, recovery and payment of fines and penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.16. Enforcement of ordinances, recovery and payment of fines and penalties (2023)
content:
(a) Enforcement.--An action, prosecution, complaint or proceeding for the violation of an ordinance
      of the city and for the fine, penalty and forfeiture imposed shall be instituted in
      the corporate name of the city and be conducted in the manner prescribed by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.13. Standard or nationally recognized codes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.13. Standard or nationally recognized codes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.13. Standard or nationally recognized codes (2023)
content:
(a) Authority to enact.--In the same manner as other ordinances, and except as otherwise provided in this chapter
      or the Pennsylvania Construction Code Act,1council may enact, by reference to a standard or nationally recognized code, all
      or a portion of the standard or nationally recognized code as an ordinance of the
      city.  Three copies of the proposed standard or nationally recognized code, portion of
      the code or amendment to the code shall be filed in the office of the city clerk at
      least 10 days before council considers the proposed ordinance.  Upon enactment, a copy shall be kept with the ordinance book and available for public
      use, inspection and examination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.14. Maps, plans or drawings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.14. Maps, plans or drawings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.14. Maps, plans or drawings (2023)
content:
(a) Adoption.--Except as otherwise provided under the Municipalities Planning Code, if maps, plans
      or drawings are to be adopted as part of an ordinance, council, instead of publishing
      the maps, plans or drawings as part of the ordinance may make reference to, in publishing
      the ordinance or a summary of the ordinance, the location where the maps, plans or
      drawings are on file and may be examined.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.11. Records of ordinances maintained by city clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.11. Records of ordinances maintained by city clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.11. Records of ordinances maintained by city clerk (2023)
content:
(a) Records.--Within one month after enactment, each ordinance shall be certified and recorded by
      the city clerk in a book provided by the city which shall, at all times, be open to
      the inspection of the public.  Within one month after adoption, each resolution pertaining to a tax levy shall
      be certified and recorded by the city clerk in a book provided by the city which shall,
      at all times, be open to the inspection of the public.  A standard or nationally recognized code or a portion of the standard or nationally
      recognized code enacted by reference need not be recorded in or attached to the ordinance
      book but shall be deemed to have been legally recorded if the ordinance by which the
      code was enacted by reference is recorded, with an accompanying notation stating where
      the full text of the code is filed.  A failure to record within the time provided shall not be deemed a defect in the
      process of the enactment or adoption of the ordinance or of the resolution that pertains
      to a tax levy.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.12. Proof and evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.12. Proof and evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.12. Proof and evidence (2023)
content:
(a) Proof.--An ordinance, resolution, motion or other proceeding of council may be proved by the
      certificate of the city clerk under the corporate seal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11030. Initiation of proposed ordinances by petition and exceptions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11030. Initiation of proposed ordinances by petition and exceptions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11030. Initiation of proposed ordinances by petition and exceptions (2023)
content:
(a) Submission.--Except as provided in subsection (b), a proposed ordinance may be submitted to council
      by a petition signed by the electors of a city in accordance with this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11031. Petition and notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11031. Petition and notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11031. Petition and notice (2023)
content:
If the city clerk receives a written request for the preparation of a petition for
   the submission of a proposed ordinance to council by at least 100 qualified electors
   of the city and the request is accompanied by a copy of the proposed ordinance, within
   10 days of receipt the city clerk shall do each of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11033. Number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11033. Number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11033. Number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk (2023)
content:
(a) Signatures.--Within 10 days after the period of time for signing the petition has elapsed, the
      city clerk shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11032. Signing and oath
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11032. Signing and oath
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11032. Signing and oath (2023)
content:
(a) Petition.--A petition for the submission of a proposed ordinance shall be signed in the city
      clerk's office.  The petition shall be retained in the city clerk's office at all times for a period
      of 15 days.  Each signer shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11035. Actions by council and notices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11035. Actions by council and notices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11035. Actions by council and notices (2023)
content:
If the petition accompanying the proposed ordinance is signed by electors of the city
   as required in section 11033(a)(2) (relating to number of signatures, examination
   and certificate by city clerk), council shall do one of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.17. Penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.17. Penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.17. Penalty (2023)
content:
A person who violates an ordinance enacted under the authority of this chapter for
   which no penalty is specified commits a summary offense and, upon conviction, shall
   be sentenced to pay a fine of not more than $1,000 or to imprisonment for not more
   than 90 days, or both.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11037. Effect of majority vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11037. Effect of majority vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11037. Effect of majority vote (2023)
content:
If the majority of the qualified electors voting on the proposed ordinance vote in
   favor of the ordinance, the ordinance shall become a valid and binding ordinance of
   the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A.1. Ordinances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.15. Codification of ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A.1. Ordinances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.15. Codification of ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11018.15. Codification of ordinances (2023)
content:
(a) Preparation authorized.--Council may prepare a consolidation or codification of the general body of city ordinances
      or the ordinances on a particular subject.  Council may adopt the consolidation or codification as an ordinance of the city
      in the same manner prescribed for the adoption of an ordinance, except as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11040. Submission for repeal by council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11040. Submission for repeal by council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11040. Submission for repeal by council (2023)
content:
Council may submit a proposition for the repeal or amendment of an ordinance to be
   voted upon at a succeeding municipal, general or primary election occurring at least
   90 days after council's submission of the proposition.  Should the submitted proposition receive a majority of the votes cast on the proposition
   at the election, the ordinance shall be repealed or amended accordingly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11034. Submission to council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11034. Submission to council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11034. Submission to council (2023)
content:
If the petition is certified to contain signatures as required in section 11033(a)(2)
   (relating to number of signatures, examination and certificate by city clerk), the
   city clerk shall submit the petition to council without delay.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11039. Number of proposed ordinances to be submitted and elections limited
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11039. Number of proposed ordinances to be submitted and elections limited
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11039. Number of proposed ordinances to be submitted and elections limited (2023)
content:
Any number of proposed ordinances may be voted upon at the same election, in accordance
   with the provisions of this subchapter.  Proposed ordinances on the same subject matter shall not be submitted by petition
   more frequently than once every three years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11036. Form of ballot on submission to vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11036. Form of ballot on submission to vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11036. Form of ballot on submission to vote (2023)
content:
The question to be submitted to the electors on the proposed ordinance shall be framed
   to state the nature of the proposed ordinance, followed by the words “yes” and “no”.  The question shall be placed on the ballot which shall be counted, returned and
   computed in accordance with section 11062 (relating to computing and filing returns)
   and the election laws of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11041. Publication of proposed ordinance, repeal or amendment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11041. Publication of proposed ordinance, repeal or amendment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11041. Publication of proposed ordinance, repeal or amendment (2023)
content:
Whenever a proposed ordinance is to be submitted to the electors of the city at an
   election or an ordinance is submitted by council for repeal or amendment, notice of
   the election and text of the question to be submitted to the electors shall be published
   in the same manner as publication is required in section 1201 of the Pennsylvania
   Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11050. Time ordinances go into effect
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11050. Time ordinances go into effect
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11050. Time ordinances go into effect (2023)
content:
(a) Timing.--Except as provided in subsection (b), an ordinance enacted by council may not go into
      effect before 10 days from the time of the ordinance's final enactment by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11052. Preparation of petition by city clerk and notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11052. Preparation of petition by city clerk and notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11052. Preparation of petition by city clerk and notice (2023)
content:
(a) Petition.--A petition under section 11051 (relating to petition and reconsideration of ordinance)
      shall be prepared by the city clerk immediately upon receipt by the clerk of the written
      request of 100 qualified electors of the city asking that the petition be prepared.  Upon preparation of the petition, the clerk shall give notice by publication in
      a newspaper of general circulation:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11055. Presentation of petition to council
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11055. Presentation of petition to council
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11055. Presentation of petition to council (2023)
content:
At the expiration of 10 days, the petition shall be filed with council and presented
   by the city clerk at council's next meeting.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11059. Effect of petition and submission to electors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11059. Effect of petition and submission to electors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11059. Effect of petition and submission to electors (2023)
content:
(a) Petition lacking signatures.--If it appears that the petition under this subchapter has not been signed by the required
      number of electors, no action shall be taken.  The ordinance shall be taken to be in full force from the time or times it would
      have gone into effect had there been no petition against the ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11060. Certification to county board of elections, ballots or ballot labels and expense of elections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11060. Certification to county board of elections, ballots or ballot labels and expense of elections
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11060. Certification to county board of elections, ballots or ballot labels and expense of elections (2023)
content:
(a) Certification.--The city clerk, after consultation with the city solicitor, shall certify to the county
      board of elections a copy of the ordinance and the proceedings of council directing
      the referendum vote.  The county board of elections shall cause the question to be printed for use in
      the election districts of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11056. Ascertainment of number of signers and report
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11056. Ascertainment of number of signers and report
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11056. Ascertainment of number of signers and report (2023)
content:
After presentation of the petition to council, the city clerk shall ascertain whether
   or not the referendum petition is signed by a number of registered electors equal
   to 20% of all the votes cast for all candidates for mayor at the last preceding municipal
   election at which a mayor was elected.  Council may allow the clerk additional help for that purpose.  After the clerk has made the examination, the clerk shall report the result to council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11038. No repeal within two years
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Initiating Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11038. No repeal within two years
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11038. No repeal within two years (2023)
content:
An ordinance proposed by petition, whether enacted by council or adopted by a vote
   of the electors, shall not be repealed or amended within two years of the effective
   date except by a vote of the electors.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11063. Effect of vote
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11063. Effect of vote
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11063. Effect of vote (2023)
content:
If a majority of the electors vote in favor of the ordinance, the ordinance shall
   take effect when the results of the election are certified by council.  If a majority of the electors vote against the ordinance, the ordinance shall be
   nullified.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11051. Petition and reconsideration of ordinance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11051. Petition and reconsideration of ordinance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11051. Petition and reconsideration of ordinance (2023)
content:
With the exception of an ordinance dealing with the subjects set forth in section
   11050(b) (relating to time ordinances go into effect), an ordinance shall be suspended
   from going into operation and shall be reconsidered by council if all of the following
   occur:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11061. Form of ballot or ballot label
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11061. Form of ballot or ballot label
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11061. Form of ballot or ballot label (2023)
content:
The ballot used when voting on the ordinance shall contain a question stating the
   nature of the referred ordinance followed by the words “yes” and “no” and shall be
   conducted in the manner as provided in the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11053. Additional petitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11053. Additional petitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11053. Additional petitions (2023)
content:
(a) Petitions.--In order to facilitate the signing of the petition, the city clerk shall make at least
      two additional similar petitions for signing by the qualified electors.  Signing an additional similar petition shall have the same force and effect as signing
      the original petition.  The city clerk is authorized to employ at least two individuals to take charge of
      the additional petitions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11064. Publication of ordinance before election
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11064. Publication of ordinance before election
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11064. Publication of ordinance before election (2023)
content:
Before any referendum is held on any ordinance in accordance with this subchapter,
   the city shall provide notice of the ordinance by publishing a copy of the ordinance
   in a newspaper of general circulation.  Publication in accordance with this section shall be in addition to the publication
   requirements of the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 111. Executive Department›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11105. Quarterly reports from department directors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 111. Executive Department › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11105. Quarterly reports from department directors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11105. Quarterly reports from department directors (2023)
content:
(a) Report.--At the close of each quarter of the fiscal year, a department director shall prepare
      and submit to the director of the department of accounts and finance, if a department
      of accounts and finance is established by ordinance, or to the business administrator
      or other official designated by council, a comprehensive and detailed report of all
      expenditures and operations of the director's department during the quarter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11054. Signatures, oath and time of signing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11054. Signatures, oath and time of signing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11054. Signatures, oath and time of signing (2023)
content:
(a) Signers.--Each signer of a petition under section 11051 (relating to petition and reconsideration
      of ordinance) shall also do all the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 111. Executive Department›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11101. Executive departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 111. Executive Department › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11101. Executive departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11101. Executive departments (2023)
content:
The city may enact an ordinance establishing departments to implement administrative
   functions of the city.  If the city fails to adopt an ordinance, powers and duties of the city shall be
   allocated and assigned among the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 111. Executive Department›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11103. Designation of department directors
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 111. Executive Department › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11103. Designation of department directors
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11103. Designation of department directors (2023)
content: (a) Duties of mayor.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11062. Computing and filing returns
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Reconsidering Ordinances by Electors › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11062. Computing and filing returns
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11062. Computing and filing returns (2023)
content:
(a) Computing.--An officer holding an election shall keep a tally sheet and make a return of votes
      on the referendum question in the same manner as a tally sheet is kept and a return
      is made in an election of officers and the submission of other questions as provided
      by the Pennsylvania Election Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 111. Executive Department›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11104. Department directors responsible for city property and supplies and reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 111. Executive Department › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11104. Department directors responsible for city property and supplies and reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11104. Department directors responsible for city property and supplies and reports (2023)
content:
A department director shall be responsible for the property and supplies of the city
   within the director's department.  The department director shall prepare and maintain a perpetual inventory of the
   property and supplies for which the department director is responsible and, from time
   to time during the fiscal year, file the inventory with the city clerk or other official
   designated by council.  The city clerk or other designated official with whom the inventory is filed shall,
   upon request, transmit a copy of the inventory to the chief fiscal officer and council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11203. Execution of laws, powers of sheriff conferred and emergency powers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11203. Execution of laws, powers of sheriff conferred and emergency powers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11203. Execution of laws, powers of sheriff conferred and emergency powers (2023)
content:
(a) Execution.--The mayor shall execute and enforce the ordinances of the city and all general laws
      applicable to the ordinances.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11206. City government reports
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11206. City government reports
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11206. City government reports (2023)
content:
The mayor may request a report from a city official or department director containing
   information pertaining to administrative functions under the control and management
   of the city official or department director.  The mayor may submit a report pertaining to all matters of city government to council
   as the mayor deems necessary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11204. Official seal of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11204. Official seal of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11204. Official seal of mayor (2023)
content:
Council shall provide an official seal for the mayor in a form, as reasonably requested
   by the mayor, which shall not be changed during the mayor's term of office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11202. Inauguration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11202. Inauguration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11202. Inauguration (2023)
content:
The mayor shall be the chief executive of the city.  The mayor shall be inaugurated and take the oath of office in accordance with sections
   10904 (relating to offices to be held until qualification of successors) and 10905
   (relating to oath of office, violation of oath and penalty) on the first Monday of
   January after the regular municipal election.  If the first Monday is a legal holiday, the mayor shall be inaugurated and take
   the oath the first day after that day or as soon after that day as possible.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11201. Qualifications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11201. Qualifications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11201. Qualifications (2023)
content: The qualifications for office of mayor shall be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 111. Executive Department›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11102. Determination of powers and duties of departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 111. Executive Department › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11102. Determination of powers and duties of departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11102. Determination of powers and duties of departments (2023)
content: Council may, by ordinance, do all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11205. Supervision of conduct of city officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11205. Supervision of conduct of city officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11205. Supervision of conduct of city officers (2023)
content:
(a) Supervision.--The mayor shall supervise the conduct of all city officers, examine the grounds of
      all reasonable complaints against them and cause all of their violations or neglect
      of duty to be promptly punished or reported for correction as council may direct.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112A. City Administrator›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A01. Office of city administrator
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112A. City Administrator › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A01. Office of city administrator
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A01. Office of city administrator (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--Council may enact an ordinance by a majority vote of all the members of council establishing
      the office of city administrator.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11209. Powers and duties of acting mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11209. Powers and duties of acting mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11209. Powers and duties of acting mayor (2023)
content:
(a) Absence or inability to act.--During the absence of the mayor or the inability of the mayor to act, the vice president
      of council shall be the acting mayor who shall exercise all the rights and powers
      of the mayor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11208. Salary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11208. Salary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11208. Salary (2023)
content: (a) Payment.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112. Mayor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11207. Acknowledgments and oaths
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112. Mayor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11207. Acknowledgments and oaths
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11207. Acknowledgments and oaths (2023)
content:
The mayor may take acknowledgments of any instruments in writing pertaining to the
   business of the city, solemnize marriages and administer oaths and affirmations as
   to city business and shall attest all the mayor's acts with the mayor's official seal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11401. Qualifications
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11401. Qualifications
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11401. Qualifications (2023)
content: The qualifications for the office of city treasurer shall be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112A. City Administrator›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A05. Powers and duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112A. City Administrator › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A05. Powers and duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A05. Powers and duties (2023)
content:
(a) Powers and duties generally.--Council may, by ordinance, vest in the city administrator powers and duties relating
      to the general management of city business and to the enforcement of city ordinances
      and regulations.  Nothing in this section shall be construed to diminish the powers granted to other
      city officers by law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112A. City Administrator›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A02. Appointment of city administrator
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112A. City Administrator › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A02. Appointment of city administrator
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A02. Appointment of city administrator (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--In a city that has established an office of city administrator, council shall appoint
      an individual, partnership, limited partnership, an association or professional corporation
      to be city administrator.  The appointment of a city administrator shall be by a majority vote of all the members
      of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112A. City Administrator›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A00. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112A. City Administrator › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A00. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A00. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.1. City treasurer to be tax collector
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.1. City treasurer to be tax collector
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.1. City treasurer to be tax collector (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by the act of December 31, 1965 (P.L. 1257, No. 511),1known as The Local Tax Enabling Act, the city treasurer, by virtue of the city treasurer's
   office, shall be the collector of the city, county, school and institution district
   taxes assessed or levied in the city by the proper authorities in the city.  As tax collector, the city treasurer shall maintain and keep an office which may
   be the same as that of the city treasurer for the purpose of receiving taxes during
   regular business hours.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.2. Delivery of duplicates of taxes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.2. Delivery of duplicates of taxes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.2. Delivery of duplicates of taxes (2023)
content: (a) Duplicate delivery.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112A. City Administrator›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A03. Employment or professional services agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112A. City Administrator › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A03. Employment or professional services agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A03. Employment or professional services agreement (2023)
content:
(a) Agreement.--Council may enter into an employment or professional services agreement with the city
      administrator.  The agreement may set forth the terms and conditions of employment.  The agreement shall remain in effect for a specified period terminating not later
      than two years after the effective date of the agreement or the date of the organizational
      meeting of council after the next municipal election, whichever is earlier.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402. Bond, insurance and salary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402. Bond, insurance and salary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402. Bond, insurance and salary (2023)
content:
(a) Conditioning.--The city treasurer shall provide lawful fidelity bond, covering the full term of office,
      for the faithful performance of official duties, including duties as tax collector
      of city, county, institution district and school taxes.  In addition to being subject to other conditions as council may direct, the bond
      of the city treasurer shall be conditioned upon the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11403. Receipt and payment of money
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11403. Receipt and payment of money
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11403. Receipt and payment of money (2023)
content:
(a) Payments.--The city treasurer shall receive all money payable to the city from the sources as
      council may assign.  Upon request, the city treasurer shall issue a receipt to an individual making the
      payment.  The city treasurer shall pay all documents authorizing payment duly countersigned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11405. Restrictions on money paid out
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11405. Restrictions on money paid out
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11405. Restrictions on money paid out (2023)
content:
Money may not be paid out of the city treasury unless the money has been previously
   approved, duly authorized and appropriated by council for its intended purposes as
   explicitly mentioned in the document authorizing payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11406. Depositories of city funds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11406. Depositories of city funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11406. Depositories of city funds (2023)
content:
(a) Depositories.--The city treasurer shall keep public funds in banks or financial depositories as directed
      by council and under the restrictions and safeguards as provided by council.  The city treasurer shall verify the city treasurer's accounts as requested by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 112A. City Administrator›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A04. Residency and elective city office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 112A. City Administrator › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A04. Residency and elective city office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 112A04. Residency and elective city office (2023)
content:
(a) Residence of city administrator who is an individual.--At the time an individual is appointed to fill the office of city administrator, the
      appointee does not have to be a resident of the city.  After appointment, a city administrator who is an individual may reside outside
      the city only with the approval of council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11407. Delivery of city property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11407. Delivery of city property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11407. Delivery of city property (2023)
content:
The city treasurer shall, upon leaving office, deliver to the city or to the city
   treasurer's duly qualified successor all money, accounts, property or effects in the
   city treasurer's possession belonging to the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.3. Tax liens and liability for false returns
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.3. Tax liens and liability for false returns
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11402.3. Tax liens and liability for false returns (2023)
content:
(a) Tax liens.--Upon the settlement of the duplicates of city, county, institution district and school
      taxes which by law are made a lien on real estate, the city treasurer as tax collector
      shall make out schedules of the city, county, school or institution district taxes
      uncollected upon the duplicates, including a brief description of the properties against
      which the taxes are assessed for the purpose of entering a lien or selling the properties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11408. Appointment of deputy city treasurer and employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11408. Appointment of deputy city treasurer and employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11408. Appointment of deputy city treasurer and employees (2023)
content: (a) Appointments.--The city treasurer may appoint the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 115. City Engineer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11504. Certifying commencement and completion of municipal improvements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 115. City Engineer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11504. Certifying commencement and completion of municipal improvements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11504. Certifying commencement and completion of municipal improvements (2023)
content:
(a) Certification.--Within a reasonable time after the completion of any municipal improvement, the cost
      and expense of which, in whole or in part, is to be paid by the abutting property
      owner, the city engineer or employees designated by the city engineer shall:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 115. City Engineer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11501. Appointment of city engineer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 115. City Engineer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11501. Appointment of city engineer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11501. Appointment of city engineer (2023)
content:
Council shall provide for the manner of appointment and compensation of the city engineer.  The city engineer shall be a registered professional engineer in this Commonwealth
   and shall serve at the pleasure of council.  Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit council from designating
   an engineering firm of registered professional engineers from performing the duties
   and functions of the city engineer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 115. City Engineer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11502. Control of engineering matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 115. City Engineer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11502. Control of engineering matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11502. Control of engineering matters (2023)
content:
The city engineer shall have the supervision, direction and control of the engineering
   matters of the city.  Unless authorized by council, a department of the city may not employ or retain
   any additional engineers.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 114. City Treasurer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11404. Method of keeping accounts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 114. City Treasurer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11404. Method of keeping accounts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11404. Method of keeping accounts (2023)
content:
The accounts of the city treasurer shall clearly exhibit all the items of receipts
   and expenditures of the city, the sources from which the money is received and the
   objects for which the expenditures are disbursed.  The city treasurer shall keep separate and distinct accounts of the receipts and
   expenditures of the city, including the sinking fund, each department providing a
   utility service and each special fund.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11607. Satisfaction of liens due city
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 116. City Solicitor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11607. Satisfaction of liens due city
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11607. Satisfaction of liens due city (2023)
content:
Upon the payment of any lien or other debt of record due to the city to a city employee,
   city official or any other person authorized to receive the payment, the person who
   received the payment shall, as soon as practicable, notify the city solicitor.  The city solicitor or the solicitor's designee, as soon as practicable, shall cause
   the satisfaction to be entered upon the proper record of the lien or debt of record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11610. Special counsel
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 116. City Solicitor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11610. Special counsel
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11610. Special counsel (2023)
content:
Council may retain special counsel for particular proceedings or matters of the city
   and shall provide for the compensation of special counsel by resolution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 115. City Engineer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11503. Duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 115. City Engineer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11503. Duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11503. Duties (2023)
content:
As authorized by council, engineering work undertaken by the city shall be performed
   or supervised by the city engineer or by another registered professional engineer
   employed by the city for a particular purpose.  The duties of the city engineer may include all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11603. Duties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 116. City Solicitor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11603. Duties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11603. Duties (2023)
content: The city solicitor shall have the following duties:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704. Powers and duties of city controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704. Powers and duties of city controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704. Powers and duties of city controller (2023)
content:
(a) Payment authorization.--The city controller shall countersign all documents authorizing the payment of money
      from the city treasury, if satisfied of the legality of the payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11701. Qualifications, bond and compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11701. Qualifications, bond and compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11701. Qualifications, bond and compensation (2023)
content: (a) Qualifications.--The qualifications for the position of city controller shall be as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.2. Temporary deputy controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.2. Temporary deputy controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.2. Temporary deputy controller (2023)
content:
In case of the sickness, absence or inability of a city controller to perform the
   city controller's duties, if no deputy controller has been appointed by the city controller,
   council may appoint a temporary deputy controller to serve during the sickness, absence
   or inability of the city controller or until the city controller shall appoint a deputy
   controller.  A deputy controller shall be bonded and receive the compensation fixed by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.1. Deputy controller and employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.1. Deputy controller and employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.1. Deputy controller and employees (2023)
content:
The city controller may appoint a deputy controller and may select individuals to
   serve as assistants and employees in the city controller's office.  The number of assistants and employees permitted, if any, shall be fixed by council.  Assistants and employees in the city controller's office shall, in all other respects,
   be considered employees of the city.  The deputy controller, assistants and employees appointed under this section shall
   be bonded and their compensation shall be fixed by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.3. Continuation of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.3. Continuation of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.3. Continuation of office (2023)
content:
The appointment of an independent auditor in accordance with Subchapter B (relating
   to independent auditor) shall not abolish the office of city controller.  The elected controller shall continue to exercise the powers retained for the controller
   in this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11609. Assistant solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 116. City Solicitor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11609. Assistant solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11609. Assistant solicitor (2023)
content:
Council may appoint one or more assistant city solicitors to assist the city solicitor
   in the performance of all duties and shall provide for the compensation of assistant
   solicitors by resolution.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11601. Appointment of city solicitor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 116. City Solicitor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11601. Appointment of city solicitor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11601. Appointment of city solicitor (2023)
content:
Council shall provide, by ordinance, for the manner of appointment and compensation
   of the city solicitor, which may be a law firm.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter B. Independent Auditor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.12. Powers and duties of independent auditor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter B. Independent Auditor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.12. Powers and duties of independent auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.12. Powers and duties of independent auditor (2023)
content:
(a) Annual audit.--The independent auditor shall conduct an annual audit of all accounts of city officers,
      departments and offices which collect, receive and disburse public money or are authorized
      with the management, control or custody of public money on which the independent auditor
      is required to report under this subchapter.  The annual audit, as directed by council, shall also include any accounts subject
      to examination by the city controller under Subchapter A (relating to city controller).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 115. City Engineer›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11505. Entering upon property for surveys
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 115. City Engineer › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11505. Entering upon property for surveys
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11505. Entering upon property for surveys (2023)
content:
For the purposes of carrying out authorized surveys, laying out streets or other engineering
   work of the city, the city engineer or other persons engaged in city engineering work
   may enter upon any property occupied by any person within the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor›Subchapter B. Independent Auditor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.11. Appointment of independent auditor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 117. City Controller and Independent Auditor › Subchapter B. Independent Auditor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.11. Appointment of independent auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.11. Appointment of independent auditor (2023)
content:
Council shall provide, by resolution, for the appointment of an independent auditor.  The independent auditor may be a certified public accountant or a firm of certified
   public accountants.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11604. Written opinions to be furnished

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11604. Written opinions to be furnished (2023)
content:
(a) Opinions.--Subject to regulation by council in accordance with subsection (b), the city solicitor
      shall submit a written opinion on questions of law submitted by any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 116. City Solicitor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11602. Direction of legal matters
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 116. City Solicitor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11602. Direction of legal matters
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11602. Direction of legal matters (2023)
content:
The city solicitor shall have the direction and control of the legal matters of the
   city.  Unless authorized by council, a department of the city may not employ or retain
   any additional counsel in any matter or cause.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.1. Deputy controller and employees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.1. Deputy controller and employees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.1. Deputy controller and employees (2023)
content:
The city controller may appoint a deputy controller and may select individuals to
   serve as assistants and employees in the city controller's office.  The number of assistants and employees permitted, if any, shall be fixed by council.  Assistants and employees in the city controller's office shall, in all other respects,
   be considered employees of the city.  The deputy controller, assistants and employees appointed under this section shall
   be bonded and their compensation shall be fixed by council.

content: (a) Audit report.--

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Independent Auditor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.11. Appointment of independent auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.11. Appointment of independent auditor (2023)
content:
Council shall provide, by resolution, for the appointment of an independent auditor.  The independent auditor may be a certified public accountant or a firm of certified
   public accountants.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704. Powers and duties of city controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704. Powers and duties of city controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704. Powers and duties of city controller (2023)
content:
(a) Payment authorization.--The city controller shall countersign all documents authorizing the payment of money
      from the city treasury, if satisfied of the legality of the payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Independent Auditor›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.12. Powers and duties of independent auditor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Independent Auditor › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.12. Powers and duties of independent auditor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.12. Powers and duties of independent auditor (2023)
content:
(a) Annual audit.--The independent auditor shall conduct an annual audit of all accounts of city officers,
      departments and offices which collect, receive and disburse public money or are authorized
      with the management, control or custody of public money on which the independent auditor
      is required to report under this subchapter.  The annual audit, as directed by council, shall also include any accounts subject
      to examination by the city controller under Subchapter A (relating to city controller).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11801. Fiscal year
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11801. Fiscal year
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11801. Fiscal year (2023)
content: The fiscal year of each city shall begin on January 1 and end on December 31.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11802. Powers and duties of chief fiscal officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11802. Powers and duties of chief fiscal officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11802. Powers and duties of chief fiscal officer (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Council shall appoint a chief fiscal officer.  In filling the position of chief fiscal officer, council may appoint the director
      of the department of accounts and finance or the city administrator if one is an individual
      appointed under Chapter 111 (relating to the executive department) or 112A (relating
      to city administrator).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11804. Regulations concerning appropriation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11804. Regulations concerning appropriation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11804. Regulations concerning appropriation (2023)
content: (a) Debt.--Debt may not be incurred by any department of the city except in accordance with law.

content: (a) Audit report.--

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11805. Countersigning documents, money available and evidence required (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The chief fiscal officer shall countersign all documents, in the form approved by
      council, authorizing payment from the city treasury.

content:
The chief fiscal officer or other official or employee of the city designated by council
