path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.3. Continuation of office
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.3. Continuation of office
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.3. Continuation of office (2023)
content:
The appointment of an independent auditor in accordance with Subchapter B (relating
   to independent auditor) shall not abolish the office of city controller.  The elected controller shall continue to exercise the powers retained for the controller
   in this subchapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter A. City Controller›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.2. Temporary deputy controller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter A. City Controller › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.2. Temporary deputy controller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11704.2. Temporary deputy controller (2023)
content:
In case of the sickness, absence or inability of a city controller to perform the
   city controller's duties, if no deputy controller has been appointed by the city controller,
   council may appoint a temporary deputy controller to serve during the sickness, absence
   or inability of the city controller or until the city controller shall appoint a deputy
   controller.  A deputy controller shall be bonded and receive the compensation fixed by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11807. Supervision of accounts of departments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11807. Supervision of accounts of departments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11807. Supervision of accounts of departments (2023)
content:
The chief fiscal officer shall have the supervision and control of the accounts of
   all of the departments and may require at any time a statement in writing of all money
   or property of the city under any department's control.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11809. Annual budget, presentation to council, notice, revision and adoption
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11809. Annual budget, presentation to council, notice, revision and adoption
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11809. Annual budget, presentation to council, notice, revision and adoption (2023)
content:
(a) Introduction.--Each year at the last stated meeting in November, the chief fiscal officer shall,
      on behalf of council, present to council for introduction a proposed budget ordinance.  The proposed budget ordinance shall show the estimated receipts, expenditures and
      liabilities for the ensuing year, with the balance of unexpended appropriations and
      all other information of value as a basis for fixing the levy and tax rate for the
      next fiscal year.  Council shall, upon introducing the proposed budget ordinance, fix a date for adoption,
      which shall be not later than December 31 of that year.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11804.1. Investment of city money (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Council shall have power to provide the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11803. Deputy chief fiscal officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11803. Deputy chief fiscal officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11803. Deputy chief fiscal officer (2023)
content:
(a) Appointment.--Council may authorize the chief fiscal officer to appoint, subject to the approval
      of council, a deputy chief fiscal officer whose compensation shall be fixed by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11808. Suggestions for improvement of city finances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11808. Suggestions for improvement of city finances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11808. Suggestions for improvement of city finances (2023)
content:
The chief fiscal officer may, and when council directs shall, suggest plans to council
   for the management and improvement of the city finances.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11811. Appropriations, tax rate and limitations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11811. Appropriations, tax rate and limitations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11811. Appropriations, tax rate and limitations (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--When all estimates for the receipts, liabilities and expenditures for the ensuing
      year are made, council shall proceed to make the annual appropriations and shall fix
      the tax rate at the figure that will, in combination with all other estimated receipts
      of the city, fully meet and cover the aggregate amount of the estimates of liabilities
      and expenditures for the ensuing year.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901. Power to make and regulate contracts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901. Power to make and regulate contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901. Power to make and regulate contracts (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Each city may execute contracts for the purpose of carrying out the provisions of
      this part and the laws of this Commonwealth.  In addition to and consistent with the requirements of this chapter, council shall,
      by ordinance, provide for and regulate the procedures for the award of all contracts,
      including the purchase of supplies and materials.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11810. Amending budget and notice
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11810. Amending budget and notice
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11810. Amending budget and notice (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--During the month of January following the expiration of a past fiscal year, in furthering
      its fiduciary responsibility, council may amend the budget and the levy and tax rate
      to conform to its amended budget ordinance.  A period of 10 days' public inspection at the city clerk's office of the proposed
      amended budget ordinance, after notice by the city clerk to that effect is published
      in a newspaper of general circulation as provided in section 10109 (relating to publication
      of notices), shall intervene between council's introduction of the proposed amended
      budget ordinance and its enactment.  Any amended budget ordinance must be enacted by council on or before February 15.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11814. Annual reports to council on insurance and bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11814. Annual reports to council on insurance and bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11814. Annual reports to council on insurance and bonds (2023)
content:
The chief fiscal officer shall prepare or cause to be prepared and submit to council,
   as council shall direct, a complete and itemized report of all policies of insurance
   contracted by the city for the information and consideration of council.  The chief fiscal officer shall prepare a report, as council shall direct, of all
   bonds given for the protection of the city in whole or in part.

content: In accordance with 53 Pa.C.S. Pt. VII Subpt. B1(relating to indebtedness and borrowing), cities may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.1. Contracts or purchases in excess of base amount of $18,500
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.1. Contracts or purchases in excess of base amount of $18,500
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.1. Contracts or purchases in excess of base amount of $18,500 (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in section 11901.4(b) (relating to contracts or purchases not requiring
      advertising or bidding), all contracts or purchases in excess of the base amount of
      $18,500, subject to adjustment under section 11903.1 (relating to adjustments to base
      amount based on Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers), shall be subject to
      advertising and competitive bidding as provided in this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11813. Committee to prepare uniform forms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11813. Committee to prepare uniform forms
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11813. Committee to prepare uniform forms (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The uniform financial report forms under this chapter shall be prepared by a committee
      consisting of four representatives of the Pennsylvania Municipal League and the Secretary
      of Community and Economic Development, or the secretary's agent or designee who shall
      be an individual trained in the field of municipal finance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.8. Prohibitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.8. Prohibitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.8. Prohibitions (2023)
content:
No individual, consultant, firm or corporation contracting with a city for purposes
   of rendering personal or professional services to the city shall share with any city
   officer or employee, and no city officer or employee shall accept, any portion of
   the compensation or fees paid by the city for the contracted services provided to
   the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11812. Annual reports, publication, filing report with Department of Community and Economic Development and penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 118. Accounts and Finances › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11812. Annual reports, publication, filing report with Department of Community and Economic Development and penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11812. Annual reports, publication, filing report with Department of Community and Economic Development and penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Annual report.--The chief fiscal officer shall make a report, verified by oath or affirmation to council
      at a stated meeting in April of each year, of the public accounts of the city and
      of the trusts in its care for the preceding fiscal year, exhibiting all of the expenditures
      of the accounts, respectively, and the sources from which the revenue and funds are
      derived and in what measures the revenue and funds have been disbursed.  Each account shall be accompanied by a statement detailing all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.2. Contracts or purchases not in excess of base amount of $18,500
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.2. Contracts or purchases not in excess of base amount of $18,500
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.2. Contracts or purchases not in excess of base amount of $18,500 (2023)
content:
With regard to all contracts or purchases not in excess of the base amount of $18,500,
   subject to adjustment under section 11903.1 (relating to adjustments to base amount
   based on Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers), the following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.7. Compliance with other laws
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.7. Compliance with other laws
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.7. Compliance with other laws (2023)
content:
Every contract subject to this chapter shall comply, as applicable, with the provisions
   of the act of August 15, 1961 (P.L. 987, No. 442),1known as the Pennsylvania Prevailing Wage Act, the act of December 20, 1967 (P.L.
   869, No. 385),2known as the Public Works Contractors' Bond Law of 1967, the act of January 23, 1974
   (P.L. 9, No. 4),3referred to as the Public Contract Bid Withdrawal Law, the act of March 3, 1978 (P.L.
   6, No. 3),4known as the Steel Products Procurement Act, the act of February 17, 1994 (P.L. 73,
   No. 7),5known as the Contractor and Subcontractor Payment Act, and 62 Pa.C.S. Chs. 37 Subch.
   B6(relating to motor vehicles), 39 (relating to contracts for public works) and 45
   (relating to antibid-rigging).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.9. Lowest responsible bidder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.9. Lowest responsible bidder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.9. Lowest responsible bidder (2023)
content:
For purposes of this chapter, the lowest responsible bidder need not be the bidder
   submitting the lowest dollar amount bid.  The city may also consider the quality of goods or services supplied, ease of repair,
   compatibility with other city equipment or services, responsiveness, past performance
   of the bidder and any other reasonable factors specified in the advertisement for
   bids.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.4. Contracts or purchases not requiring advertising or bidding
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.4. Contracts or purchases not requiring advertising or bidding
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.4. Contracts or purchases not requiring advertising or bidding (2023)
content:
(a) Not in excess of base amount.--City contracts or purchases, if not in excess of the base amount of $18,500, subject
      to adjustment under section 11903.1 (relating to adjustments to base amount based
      on Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers), shall not require advertising or
      bidding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11906. Designation of appropriations, certification in excess of appropriation and contracts for governmental services for more than one year
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11906. Designation of appropriations, certification in excess of appropriation and contracts for governmental services for more than one year
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11906. Designation of appropriations, certification in excess of appropriation and contracts for governmental services for more than one year (2023)
content:
With regard to any contract, council may direct the city administrator, chief fiscal
   officer or other designated official or employee to furnish information concerning
   the availability of appropriated money to satisfy required payments under the contract.  Nothing in this section shall prevent the making of contracts for governmental services
   for a period exceeding one year, but any contract shall be executed only for the amounts
   agreed to be paid for the services to be rendered in succeeding fiscal years.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.3. Determining amount of contract
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.3. Determining amount of contract
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.3. Determining amount of contract (2023)
content:
The amount of the contract shall be the entire amount which the city pays to the successful
   bidder or the successful bidder's assigns in order to obtain the services or property,
   or both, and shall not be construed to mean only the amount which is paid to acquire
   title or to receive any other particular benefit or benefits of the whole bargain.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11902. Evasion of advertising requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11902. Evasion of advertising requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11902. Evasion of advertising requirements (2023)
content: The following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.6. Bid, performance and payment security
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.6. Bid, performance and payment security
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.6. Bid, performance and payment security (2023)
content: (a) Bid security.--The following shall apply to bid security:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11910. Acceptance by contractor of Workers' Compensation Act
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11910. Acceptance by contractor of Workers' Compensation Act
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11910. Acceptance by contractor of Workers' Compensation Act (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--All contracts executed by any city which involve the construction or performance of
      any work involving the employment of labor shall contain a provision that the contractor
      shall accept and file with the city, proof of compliance with or exemption from the
      act of June 2, 1915 (P.L. 736, No. 338),1known as the Workers' Compensation Act, insofar as the work covered by the contract
      is concerned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.5. Receipt, opening, award or rejection of bids
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.5. Receipt, opening, award or rejection of bids
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11901.5. Receipt, opening, award or rejection of bids (2023)
content:
(a) Advertisement.--If advertisement and bidding are required, the advertisement shall specify the time
      and place bids will be received and the time and place for the opening of bids.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11912. Architects and engineers in employ of city, prohibitions from bidding on public works and penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11912. Architects and engineers in employ of city, prohibitions from bidding on public works and penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11912. Architects and engineers in employ of city, prohibitions from bidding on public works and penalty (2023)
content:
(a) Bidding.--It shall be unlawful for any architect or engineer in the employ of any city to bid
      on any public work of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11911. Contracts for improvements and assignment of assessments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11911. Contracts for improvements and assignment of assessments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11911. Contracts for improvements and assignment of assessments (2023)
content:
Where the whole or any part of the cost of an improvement is to be paid by assessments
   upon the property abutting or benefited, the city may enter into an agreement with
   the contractor pursuant to which the contractor shall take an assignment of the assessments
   in payment of the amount due under the terms of the contract, and the city shall not
   be otherwise liable under the contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11909. Separate bids for plumbing, heating, ventilating and electrical work, elevators and escalators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11909. Separate bids for plumbing, heating, ventilating and electrical work, elevators and escalators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11909. Separate bids for plumbing, heating, ventilating and electrical work, elevators and escalators (2023)
content: The following shall apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11908.1. Purchase contracts for petroleum products, fire company and participation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11908.1. Purchase contracts for petroleum products, fire company and participation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11908.1. Purchase contracts for petroleum products, fire company and participation (2023)
content:
Council of each city shall have power to permit, subject to any terms and conditions
   as the city may impose, any fire company, rescue company and ambulance company in
   the city to participate in purchase contracts for petroleum products entered into
   by the city.  Fire company, rescue company and ambulance company participation in purchase contracts
   for petroleum products shall be subject to the condition that all prices shall be
   FOB.  If permitted by council, a fire company, rescue company or ambulance company may
   participate in designated petroleum product contracts entered into by the city, subject
   to the fire company, rescue company or ambulance company:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11903.1. Adjustments to base amount based on Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11903.1. Adjustments to base amount based on Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11903.1. Adjustments to base amount based on Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (2023)
content:
Adjustments to the base amounts specified under sections 11901.1 (relating to contracts
   or purchases in excess of base amount of $18,500), 11902 (relating to evasion of advertising
   requirements) and 11909 (relating to separate bids for plumbing, heating, ventilating
   and electrical work, elevators and escalators) shall be made as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12005. Powers of police officers to arrest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12005. Powers of police officers to arrest
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12005. Powers of police officers to arrest (2023)
content:
Police officers shall be ex-officio constables of the city and shall enforce the laws
   of this Commonwealth or otherwise perform the functions of their office in accordance
   with42 Pa.C.S. §§ 8952(relating to primary municipal police jurisdiction) and 8953 (relating to Statewide
   municipal police jurisdiction) and upon property owned or controlled by the city or
   by a municipal authority created by the city.  A police officer may, without warrant and upon view, arrest and commit for hearing
   any and all individuals:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 119. Contracts›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11916. Contracts with passenger or transportation companies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 119. Contracts › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11916. Contracts with passenger or transportation companies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 11916. Contracts with passenger or transportation companies (2023)
content:
Except as may be prohibited by 66 Pa.C.S. Pt. I (relating to public utility code)
   or Federal or other State regulation of transportation or commerce, a city may, as
   it deems necessary for the public benefit and convenience, contract with a person
   owning a public transportation service, railroad company, street railway, motor power
   company or passenger or transportation company.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12008. Extra compensation prohibited, exception and penalty
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12008. Extra compensation prohibited, exception and penalty
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12008. Extra compensation prohibited, exception and penalty (2023)
content:
No police officer shall ask, demand or receive any compensation or reward for the
   police officer's services other than compensation provided by ordinance, except rewards
   offered for the arrest of persons accused of crimes committed outside of the city
   in which the police officer is employed.  A police officer violating any of the provisions of this section commits a misdemeanor
   of the third degree and shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to pay a fine or imprisonment,
   or both, to be followed by dismissal from office.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12009. Compensation or insurance for volunteer police officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12009. Compensation or insurance for volunteer police officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12009. Compensation or insurance for volunteer police officer (2023)
content:
Each city may make necessary appropriations to provide compensation or insurance for
   volunteer police officers injured or killed while engaged in the performance of duties
   as may be assigned to them in the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12101. Organization of fire bureau, maintenance and apparatus
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12101. Organization of fire bureau, maintenance and apparatus
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12101. Organization of fire bureau, maintenance and apparatus (2023)
content: With regard to a city fire bureau, council shall have the authority to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12001. Appointment, number, rank, compensation and qualifications of police officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12001. Appointment, number, rank, compensation and qualifications of police officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12001. Appointment, number, rank, compensation and qualifications of police officers (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council shall fix, by ordinance, the number, grades and compensation of the members
      of the city police force, who shall, except as provided in section 12002 (relating
      to designation of chief), be appointed in accordance with the civil service provisions
      of this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12003. Extra police officers and compensation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12003. Extra police officers and compensation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12003. Extra police officers and compensation (2023)
content:
The mayor may appoint extra police officers, whenever it is necessary in the judgment
   of the mayor for the public safety or to preserve order, to serve for a period designated
   by council, not to exceed 30 days and whose compensation shall be fixed by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12006. Service of process, fees and payment into treasury
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12006. Service of process, fees and payment into treasury
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12006. Service of process, fees and payment into treasury (2023)
content:
Police officers shall have authority to serve and to execute criminal process or processes
   issued for the violation of city ordinances and shall charge the same fees and costs
   as pertain by law to the constables of the city for similar services, but the fees
   and costs shall be paid into the city treasury monthly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12010. School crossing guards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12010. School crossing guards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12010. School crossing guards (2023)
content:
(a) Request.--Upon request of the board of school directors of the school district in which a city
      is located, council may appoint school crossing guards who shall control and direct
      traffic at or near schools.  They shall serve at the pleasure of council, except as provided for in subsection
      (b).  The compensation of the school crossing guards, if any, shall be fixed by council
      and shall be jointly paid by council and the board of school directors, in a ratio
      to be determined by council and the board of school directors.  If council and the board of school directors are unable to determine the ratio of
      compensation of the school crossing guards to be paid by council and the board, each
      shall pay one-half of the compensation of the school crossing guards.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12002. Designation of chief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12002. Designation of chief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12002. Designation of chief (2023)
content:
The chief of police shall be designated by the mayor from within the ranks and may
   be demoted without cause in the same manner, but not to any rank lower than the rank
   which was held at the time of designation as chief of police.  In the event that no qualified officer from within the ranks has applied for the
   designation, the chief of police shall be designated by the mayor from outside the
   ranks.  The officers, other than the chief of police, shall be designated in accordance
   with Chapter 144 (relating to civil service).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12101.1. Appointment and demotion of fire chief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12101.1. Appointment and demotion of fire chief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12101.1. Appointment and demotion of fire chief (2023)
content:
The mayor, by and with approval and consent of council, shall appoint the fire chief
   who may be demoted without cause but not to any rank lower than the rank which the
   fire chief held within the fire bureau at the time of designation as fire chief.  In the event that no qualified employee of the fire bureau has applied for the appointment,
   the fire chief shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with approval and consent of
   council, from outside the ranks.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12106. Investigation of cause of fire and power of mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12106. Investigation of cause of fire and power of mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12106. Investigation of cause of fire and power of mayor (2023)
content:
The mayor of any city may issue a subpoena in the name of the Commonwealth to an individual
   requiring the attendance of the individual before the mayor or the fire marshal at
   the time and place as may be named in the subpoena, then and there to testify, under
   oath or affirmation, which the fire marshal in the absence of the mayor is empowered
   to administer, as to:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12103. Platoon system and hours of service
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12103. Platoon system and hours of service
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12103. Platoon system and hours of service (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The director of the department having charge of the fire bureau in a city may divide
      the officers and members of companies of the uniformed fire force in the employ of
      the city, and any other firefighters and drivers regularly employed and paid by the
      city, except the chief engineer and assistant chiefs, and those employed subject to
      call, into shifts, bodies or platoons to perform service during the hours as the director
      shall fix.  In cases of riot, serious conflagration, times of war, public celebrations or other
      emergency, the fire chief or officer in charge at any fire shall have the power to
      assign all the members of the fire force to continuous duty or to continue any member
      of the fire force on duty, if necessary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12102. Paid fire bureau, election of officers and companies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12102. Paid fire bureau, election of officers and companies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12102. Paid fire bureau, election of officers and companies (2023)
content:
When a paid fire bureau is organized by any city, council, except as provided by section
   12101.1 (relating to appointment and demotion of fire chief), may provide for the
   election or appointment of the officers and companies belonging to the fire bureau
   by ordinance in accordance with civil service provisions, where applicable.  The minimum annual starting salary or compensation to be paid to officers and firefighters
   by any city shall be established by council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 120. Police Force›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12007. Supervision by mayor
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 120. Police Force › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12007. Supervision by mayor
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12007. Supervision by mayor (2023)
content:
The chief of police shall obey the orders of the mayor and make report to the mayor,
   which shall be presented monthly by the mayor to council.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12104. Fire marshal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12104. Fire marshal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12104. Fire marshal (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A city may, by ordinance, provide for the creation of the office of fire marshal who
      shall be appointed by the mayor, by and with the approval and consent of council,
      biennially.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12108. Compensation insurance for injured volunteer firefighters or special fire police
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12108. Compensation insurance for injured volunteer firefighters or special fire police
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12108. Compensation insurance for injured volunteer firefighters or special fire police (2023)
content:
A city may make appropriations to secure insurance or compensation for volunteer firefighters
   killed or injured while engaged in the performance of their duties or as special fire
   police.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12105. Obstructing fire marshal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12105. Obstructing fire marshal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12105. Obstructing fire marshal (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--It shall be unlawful for any person to obstruct or prevent or attempt to obstruct
      or prevent the fire marshal in the discharge of the fire marshal's duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12204. Operators to furnish maps and contents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12204. Operators to furnish maps and contents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12204. Operators to furnish maps and contents (2023)
content:
The owner, operator or superintendent of a coal mine or colliery within the limits
   of the city, in whole or in part, shall, at the request of council, make or cause
   to be made and furnished to the city engineer an accurate map or plan of the workings
   or excavations of each coal mine or colliery within the limits of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12207. Penalty for surface support violations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12207. Penalty for surface support violations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12207. Penalty for surface support violations (2023)
content:
An individual, corporation or association violating the provisions of this chapter
   concerning surface support of streets and places within the city commits a misdemeanor
   and shall, upon conviction, be sentenced to pay a fine not to exceed $1,000 or imprisonment
   for a period not to exceed 90 days, or both.  Each day in which the violation continues shall constitute an additional and separate
   offense.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12107. Fire chief ex-officio fire marshal
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12107. Fire chief ex-officio fire marshal
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12107. Fire chief ex-officio fire marshal (2023)
content:
The fire chief of a city shall be ex-officio fire marshal if the office is not separately
   filled pursuant to ordinance in the city, and, in that case, all the powers and duties
   given to or imposed upon the fire marshal under this chapter shall be enjoyed and
   exercised by the fire chief.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 121. Fire Bureau›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12109. Salary of nonunion city fire officers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 121. Fire Bureau › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12109. Salary of nonunion city fire officers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12109. Salary of nonunion city fire officers (2023)
content:
A fire chief or head of a fire department of a city who has been removed from bargaining
   units under the act of June 24, 1968 (P.L. 237, No. 111),1referred to as the Policemen and Firemen Collective Bargaining Act, by rulings of
   the Pennsylvania Labor Relations Board shall receive not less than the same dollar
   increase, including fringe benefits but excluding overtime and holiday pay, as received
   by the highest-ranking fire officer participating in the bargaining unit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12209. Enactment of ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12209. Enactment of ordinances

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12206. Certain surface supports not to be removed
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 122. Surveys and Surface Support in Coal Mining Areas › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12206. Certain surface supports not to be removed
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12206. Certain surface supports not to be removed (2023)
content:
It shall be unlawful for an individual, partnership, association or corporation to
   dig, mine, remove or carry away the coal, rock, earth or other minerals or materials
   forming the natural support of the surface beneath the streets and places of a city
   to an extent and in a manner as to remove the necessary support of the surface, without
   having first placed or constructed an artificial permanent support sufficient to uphold
   and preserve the stability of the surfaces of the streets and places.

      the request of council, pursuant to section 12204 (relating to operators to furnish
      maps and contents) shall be updated at the direction of the mine owner, operator or
      superintendent.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12302. Members of appointed boards of health (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council shall appoint five members to a board of health created by ordinance.  Appointed members shall serve without compensation.  Except in the case of an appointed member who is a licensed or certified health

      of health must be residents of the city.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12301. Board of health (2023)
content:
A city shall have a board of health.  Council may, by ordinance, create a board of health or council shall be the board
   of health.  If council is the board of health, members of council shall receive no additional
   compensation for serving on the board.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Public Nuisances Detrimental to Public Health›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12321. Abatement of public nuisances by designated department
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Public Nuisances Detrimental to Public Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12321. Abatement of public nuisances by designated department
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12321. Abatement of public nuisances by designated department (2023)
content:
(a) Duty to report.--If, in accordance with this subchapter, the board of health determines that a public
      nuisance exists, it shall report its determination, along with any request for summary
      abatement, to the department designated by council in section 127A02 (relating to
      report and investigation of public nuisance).

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12335. Filling of vacancies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12335. Filling of vacancies (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Council may appoint successors for vacancies on the board of health that occur:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12337. No compensation for members
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12337. No compensation for members
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12337. No compensation for members (2023)
content:
The members of the board of health under this subchapter shall serve without compensation
   from the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter B. Public Nuisances Detrimental to Public Health›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12320. Determination of public nuisances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter B. Public Nuisances Detrimental to Public Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12320. Determination of public nuisances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12320. Determination of public nuisances (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A condition or usage in a city, whether public or private, determined by the board
      of health to be detrimental to the public health shall constitute a public nuisance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12333. Health officer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12333. Health officer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12333. Health officer (2023)
content:
Pursuant to section 12305(b) (relating to health officer), council may appoint the
   manager or chief administrator of a nonprofit corporation as the principal health
   officer of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12338. Applicability of subchapter
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12338. Applicability of subchapter
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12338. Applicability of subchapter (2023)
content:
This subchapter shall be effective only under the circumstances set forth in section
   12330 (relating to board of directors of corporation to be appointed members of board
   of health).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12334. Secretary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter C. Corporations Acting as Boards of Health › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12334. Secretary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12334. Secretary (2023)
content:
The secretary of the board of directors of the nonprofit corporation under this subchapter
   may serve as secretary of the board of health.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Subchapter D. Penalty › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12340. Penalty

content: Any person who:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12404. Creation of reserve funds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12404. Creation of reserve funds (2023)
content: (a) Capital reserve fund.--

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12402. Powers of cities (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A city is declared to be a body corporate and politic, shall have perpetual succession
      and may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12403. Payment of debts and expenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12403. Payment of debts and expenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12403. Payment of debts and expenses (2023)
content:
Council may provide for the payment of the debts and expenses of the city and appropriate
   money for the payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12402.1. City property and affairs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12402.1. City property and affairs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12402.1. City property and affairs (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In exercising its discretion to make decisions that further the public interest under
      terms it deems most beneficial to the city, council may, subject to any restrictions,
      limitations or exceptions stated in this chapter:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12405. Hiring of employees and salaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12405. Hiring of employees and salaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12405. Hiring of employees and salaries (2023)
content:
Council may provide for and regulate the manner of hiring and discharging employees
   and the fixing of their salaries or compensation, consistent with applicable Federal
   and State law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12407. Lockups
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12407. Lockups
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12407. Lockups (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council may provide for lockup facilities as deemed necessary for the detention and
      confinement of individuals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12413. Regulation of division fences, party walls and foundations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12413. Regulation of division fences, party walls and foundations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12413. Regulation of division fences, party walls and foundations (2023)
content: (a) Authority.--

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12412. Fireworks and inflammable articles (2023)
content: In conformity with Federal and State laws and regulations, council may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12406. Creation of necessary offices or boards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12406. Creation of necessary offices or boards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12406. Creation of necessary offices or boards (2023)
content:
In addition to the city departments established in accordance with Chapter 111 (relating
   to the executive department), council may create any city office, public board, bureau
   or commission, which it may deem necessary for the good of government and interests
   of the city, and, with regard to an office or membership on a board, bureau or commission,
   unless otherwise provided by this part, council may make appointments and regulate
   and prescribe the terms, duties and compensation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12410. Regulation of pets and feral animals
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12410. Regulation of pets and feral animals
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12410. Regulation of pets and feral animals (2023)
content:
Council may, by ordinance, prohibit and regulate the running at large of dogs, cats,
   other pets and feral animals.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12411. Inspection and regulation of fireplaces and chimneys and smoke regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12411. Inspection and regulation of fireplaces and chimneys and smoke regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12411. Inspection and regulation of fireplaces and chimneys and smoke regulations (2023)
content:
In conformity with Federal and State laws and regulations, council may regulate and
   inspect fireplaces, chimneys and other sources of smoke and fly ash to control the
   production and emission of unnecessary smoke and fly ash.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12409. Accumulation of ashes, garbage, solid waste and refuse materials
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12409. Accumulation of ashes, garbage, solid waste and refuse materials
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12409. Accumulation of ashes, garbage, solid waste and refuse materials (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council in the manner authorized by the act of July 7, 1980 (P.L. 380, No. 97),1known as the Solid Waste Management Act, and the act of July 28, 1988 (P.L. 556,
      No. 101),2known as the Municipal Waste Planning, Recycling and Waste Reduction Act, may prohibit
      accumulations of ashes, garbage, solid waste and other refuse materials upon private
      property, including the imposition and collection of reasonable fees and charges for
      the collection, removal and disposal.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12415. Regulation of encroachments
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12415. Regulation of encroachments
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12415. Regulation of encroachments (2023)
content:
In compliance with applicable State laws and city ordinances, council may provide
   for the regulation of all encroachments in, under or upon sidewalks or other portions
   of streets in the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12417. Numbering of buildings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12417. Numbering of buildings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12417. Numbering of buildings (2023)
content: Council may require and regulate the numbering of buildings and lots.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12414. Nuisances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12414. Nuisances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12414. Nuisances (2023)
content:
Council may prohibit and abate public nuisances in accordance with Subchapter B of
   Chapter 1231(relating to public nuisances detrimental to public health).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12418. Transportation stands
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12418. Transportation stands
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12418. Transportation stands (2023)
content:
Council may establish stands for taxis, buses, automobiles and other vehicles for
   hire and enforce the observance and use of the stands.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12419. Police force
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12419. Police force
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12419. Police force (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council may establish and maintain a police force and define the duties of the force
      in accordance with Chapter 120 (relating to police force).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12408. Marketplaces
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12408. Marketplaces
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12408. Marketplaces (2023)
content: Council may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12416. Shade trees
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12416. Shade trees
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12416. Shade trees (2023)
content: (a) Power to regulate.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12424. Racing and dangerous practices
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12424. Racing and dangerous practices
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12424. Racing and dangerous practices (2023)
content:
With regard to streets and public places in the city, council may regulate or prohibit
   racing or fast driving of vehicles and all games, practices or amusements likely to
   result in danger or damage to any individual or property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12422. Prevent riots
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12422. Prevent riots
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12422. Prevent riots (2023)
content:
Council may prevent and restrain riots, noises, disturbances or disorderly assemblies
   in any street, house or place in the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12421. Rewards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12421. Rewards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12421. Rewards (2023)
content:
Council may offer rewards for the arrest and conviction of individuals guilty of capital
   or other crimes within the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12427. Aid to historical societies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12427. Aid to historical societies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12427. Aid to historical societies (2023)
content:
Council may make annual appropriations for the support and maintenance of the principal
   historical society located in the city, which shall be incorporated under the laws
   of this Commonwealth, and shall maintain permanent quarters for the society and keep
   them open to the public.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12425. Bathing, recreational swimming establishments and boathouses and bathhouses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12425. Bathing, recreational swimming establishments and boathouses and bathhouses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12425. Bathing, recreational swimming establishments and boathouses and bathhouses (2023)
content:
To the extent permitted by the act of June 23, 1931 (P.L. 899, No. 299),1known as the Public Bathing Law, council may regulate the time and place of bathing
   in rivers and other public water in and adjoining the city and may construct, maintain
   and manage municipal boathouses, bathhouses and recreational swimming establishments.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12420. Police regulations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12420. Police regulations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12420. Police regulations (2023)
content:
Council may establish and enforce suitable police regulations for the protection of
   individuals and property.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12429. Ambulances and rescue and lifesaving services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12429. Ambulances and rescue and lifesaving services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12429. Ambulances and rescue and lifesaving services (2023)
content: Council may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12426. Musical entertainment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12426. Musical entertainment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12426. Musical entertainment (2023)
content:
Council may appropriate money to defray the expenses of musical entertainment held
   under the auspices of the city and for the purpose of having music in any public park
   or place.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12436. Historical property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12436. Historical property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12436. Historical property (2023)
content:
Council may acquire, by purchase or gift, repair, supervise, operate and maintain
   landmarks and other historical properties that are either eligible for listing or
   listed in the National Register of Historic Places or certified by the Pennsylvania
   Historical and Museum Commission as having historical significance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12423. Regulate discharge of guns and deadly weapons
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12423. Regulate discharge of guns and deadly weapons
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12423. Regulate discharge of guns and deadly weapons (2023)
content:
To the extent permitted by Federal and other State law, council may regulate, prohibit
   and prevent the discharge of guns and prevent the carrying of concealed deadly weapons.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12428. Establishment of institutions to collect educational collections
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12428. Establishment of institutions to collect educational collections
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12428. Establishment of institutions to collect educational collections (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council may establish institutions authorized to collect and hold certain scientific,
      educational and economic collections, the object of each being the instruction of
      the public concerning commerce, manufacturing, mining and agriculture.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12434. Municipal authorities and cooperation with other political subdivisions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12434. Municipal authorities and cooperation with other political subdivisions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12434. Municipal authorities and cooperation with other political subdivisions (2023)
content:
(a) Municipal authorities.--Council may, by ordinance, individually or in cooperation with other municipalities
      or school districts, form municipal authorities as authorized under 53 Pa.C.S. Ch.
      56 (relating to municipal authorities).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12433. Official expenses on city business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12433. Official expenses on city business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12433. Official expenses on city business (2023)
content:
Council may make appropriations for the reasonable expenses of city officials incurred
   in the conduct of city business.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12439. Appropriations for industrial development
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12439. Appropriations for industrial development
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12439. Appropriations for industrial development (2023)
content:
Council may make appropriations to an industrial development organization as defined
   in section 2301 of the act of June 29, 1996 (P.L. 434, No. 67),1known as the Job Enhancement Act, when the city is located within the area for which
   the industrial development organization has been authorized to make application to
   and receive grants from the Department of Community and Economic Development for the
   purposes specified in Chapter 23 of the Job Enhancement Act.2

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12430. Insurance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12430. Insurance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12430. Insurance (2023)
content:
(a) Contracts authorized.--Council, in its discretion or as required by law or a collective bargaining agreement,
      may make contracts of insurance and contracts for annuities or pensions, including
