path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12431. Parking lots
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12431. Parking lots
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12431. Parking lots (2023)
content:
Council may acquire, by lease, purchase or condemnation proceedings, land that in
   its judgment may be necessary and desirable for the purpose of establishing and maintaining
   lots for the sole purpose of parking motor vehicles.  Council may regulate the use of the land, including the posting of signs, and may
   establish or designate areas exclusively reserved for parking by individuals with
   disabilities.  Regulation of parking lots shall be consistent with 75 Pa.C.S. (relating to vehicles)
   and the act of October 27, 1955 (P.L. 744, No. 222),1known as the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12432. Disorderly conduct
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12432. Disorderly conduct
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12432. Disorderly conduct (2023)
content:
Council may, by ordinance, prohibit disorderly conduct within the limits of the city
   and provide for the imposition of penalties in accordance with this part.  If an ordinance is enacted, it shall define disorderly conduct in a manner substantially
   similar to the provisions of18 Pa.C.S. § 5503(relating to disorderly conduct).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12441. Appropriations for urban common carrier mass transportation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12441. Appropriations for urban common carrier mass transportation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12441. Appropriations for urban common carrier mass transportation (2023)
content:
Council may make appropriations for urban common carrier mass transportation from
   current revenues and make annual contributions to county departments of transportation
   or to urban common carrier mass transportation authorities to assist the departments
   or the authorities to meet costs of operation, maintenance, capital improvements and
   debt service and to enter into long-term agreements providing for the payment of the
   contributions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12435. Local self-government
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12435. Local self-government
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12435. Local self-government (2023)
content:
Council shall have the power to enact, make, adopt, modify, repeal and enforce, in
   accordance with this part, ordinances, resolutions, rules and regulations not inconsistent
   with or restrained by the Constitution of Pennsylvania and laws of this Commonwealth
   that are either of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12438. Junk dealers and junk yards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12438. Junk dealers and junk yards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12438. Junk dealers and junk yards (2023)
content:
Council may regulate and license junk dealers and the establishment and maintenance
   of junk yards and scrap yards, including automobile junk or grave yards.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12437. Appropriations for handling, storage and distribution of surplus foods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12437. Appropriations for handling, storage and distribution of surplus foods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12437. Appropriations for handling, storage and distribution of surplus foods (2023)
content:
(a) Appropriations.--Council may appropriate from city funds money for the handling, storage and distribution
      of surplus foods obtained through a Federal, State or local agency.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12440. Nondebt revenue bonds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12440. Nondebt revenue bonds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12440. Nondebt revenue bonds (2023)
content:
Consistent with and without limitation of any power conferred or duty imposed by 53
   Pa.C.S. Pt. VII Subpt. B1(relating to indebtedness and borrowing), council may issue nondebt revenue bonds
   pursuant to the provisions of 53 Pa.C.S. Pt. VII Subpt. B.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12445. Rights within streets and rights-of-way
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12445. Rights within streets and rights-of-way
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12445. Rights within streets and rights-of-way (2023)
content:
(a) Rights within streets.--Council may consent to a person using city streets and other properties, whether the
      use is within, on or over the streets or public property in question, for transportation
      purposes or for the purpose of installing and maintaining pipes, wires, fibers, cables
      or any other utility or service medium.  Council may define a reasonable district within which all electric or telephone
      wires, cables or any other utility or service medium are to be placed underground.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12444. Validation and maintenance of certain records
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12444. Validation and maintenance of certain records
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12444. Validation and maintenance of certain records (2023)
content:
(a) Validation of records.--Except as otherwise provided by law, city records that are required to be recorded
      or copied shall be deemed valid if recorded or transcribed by any digital, photostatic,
      photographic, microphotographic, microfilm, microcard, miniature photographic, optical,
      electronic or other process that accurately reproduces the original and forms a durable
      medium for recording, storing and reproducing the original in accordance with standards,
      policies and procedures for the creation, maintenance, transmission or reproduction
      of images of records approved by the county or local government records committees,
      as applicable, and as otherwise provided by law.  Where recording in a specific book is required, except for minutes or the proceedings
      of council, the records may be recorded, transcribed or otherwise assembled in an
      appropriate book, disk or other medium approved by resolution of council, and all
      records recorded and assembled in any manner are validated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12442. Appropriation for nonprofit art corporation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12442. Appropriation for nonprofit art corporation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12442. Appropriation for nonprofit art corporation (2023)
content:
(a) Appropriation.--Council may appropriate money annually, of not more than an amount equal to one mill
      of the real estate tax, to any nonprofit art corporation for the conduct of its artistic
      and cultural activities.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12447. Charitable purposes
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12447. Charitable purposes
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12447. Charitable purposes (2023)
content:
(a) Creation of city bureau or agency.--Council may, by ordinance, create a city bureau or agency to receive, in trust, all
      property bestowed upon the bureau or agency for charitable purposes.  Council may control the property for the purposes of the trust.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 125. Taxation › Subchapter B. Levy and Collection › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12531.2. Certification of schedule

content:
For the purpose of delinquent tax collection and the filing of liens on property upon
   which the taxes, assessed and levied, have not been paid and have become delinquent,
   the city treasurer shall certify schedules of unpaid taxes.  The certification shall be made to the person designated by each taxing district
   for which the city treasurer collects taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 124. Corporate Powers›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12446. Emergency services
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 124. Corporate Powers › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12446. Emergency services
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12446. Emergency services (2023)
content:
(a) Provision of emergency services.--A city shall be responsible for ensuring that fire and emergency medical services
      are provided within the city by the means and to the extent determined by the city,
      including the appropriate financial and administrative assistance for these services.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 125. Taxation›Subchapter B. Levy and Collection›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12531.1. Exemptions from taxation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 125. Taxation › Subchapter B. Levy and Collection › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12531.1. Exemptions from taxation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12531.1. Exemptions from taxation (2023)
content:
Council may, by ordinance or resolution, exempt any individual whose total income
   from all sources is less than $12,000 per annum from any per capita or residence tax
   levied under this chapter.  This exemption shall not apply to real property taxes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 125. Taxation›Subchapter C. Sales of Real Estate for Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12546. Record of sales, purchase and resale

      may direct, a record of all the sales made pursuant to section 12542.1 (relating to
      public sale of property to satisfy tax claims).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 125. Taxation›Subchapter C. Sales of Real Estate for Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12543. Certification of schedules to city treasurer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 125. Taxation › Subchapter C. Sales of Real Estate for Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12543. Certification of schedules to city treasurer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12543. Certification of schedules to city treasurer (2023)
content:
At the request of the city treasurer, any person acting on behalf of the city who
   possesses a schedule of unpaid city taxes shall certify the schedule to the city treasurer
   along with the description of property against which the unpaid taxes were assessed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 125. Taxation›Subchapter C. Sales of Real Estate for Delinquent Taxes›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12552.1. Conduct of tax sales
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 125. Taxation › Subchapter C. Sales of Real Estate for Delinquent Taxes › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12552.1. Conduct of tax sales
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12552.1. Conduct of tax sales (2023)
content:
The procedures and requirements relating to the sale of property for delinquent taxes,
   including the advertisement for and the time and conduct of the sale, the payment
   of the purchase price, the distribution of proceeds, making the return and confirmation
   of sale and the delivery of deed, shall be governed by the act of July 7, 1947 (P.L.
   1368, No. 542),1known as the Real Estate Tax Sale Law, or the Municipal Claim and Tax Lien Law2as utilized by the city in accordance with section 12542.1 (relating to public sale
   of property to satisfy tax claims) and by any applicable rules of court governing
   procedures for tax sales.

In addition to all other powers granted by this part and other laws, a city shall

Council may, as provided by ordinance or the laws of this Commonwealth, license and
   provide for the collection of a license fee from all persons certified as being qualified
   to engage in the business of plumbing or house drainage.

content: (a) General rule.--Subject to subsection (b), a city may regulate transportation by motor vehicle.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12651. Farmers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12651. Farmers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12651. Farmers (2023)
content:
A city may not levy or collect a license fee from a farmer upon sales of the farmer's
   own produce in or about the streets of the city.  This section shall not restrict a city's power to regulate the conduct of a farmer's
   business.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12604. Power to regulate and license transient merchants
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12604. Power to regulate and license transient merchants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12604. Power to regulate and license transient merchants (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--With regard to transient merchants, a city shall have power, by ordinance, to regulate
      and license the transient merchant, including requiring that a license be procured
      prior to commencement of transient merchant activity.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12605. Regulation of special events
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12605. Regulation of special events
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12605. Regulation of special events (2023)
content:
(a) Special events.--In addition to other licensing and regulatory powers authorized by this chapter, council
      shall have the authority, by ordinance, to require a permit for and to reasonably
      regulate the conduct of a special event, which may include, but are not limited to,
      the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12653. Persons taking orders by samples
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12653. Persons taking orders by samples
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12653. Persons taking orders by samples (2023)
content:
A city may not levy or collect a license fee or mercantile tax upon a person taking
   orders for merchandise by sample from a dealer or merchant for persons who pay a license
   or mercantile tax at their primary places of business.  Nothing in this section shall authorize a person to sell by retail to persons other
   than dealers or merchants without payment of a license or permit fee.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12654. Commonwealth licenses
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12654. Commonwealth licenses
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12654. Commonwealth licenses (2023)
content:
This chapter shall not be construed to relieve a person from the duty of taking out
   a license or from the payment of any license tax or fee imposed or authorized by any
   other statute, nor shall any Commonwealth license tax or fee preempt the registration,
   licensure or regulatory powers of a city in accordance with this chapter, unless the
   preemption is expressly authorized.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A02. Report and investigation of public nuisance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A02. Report and investigation of public nuisance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A02. Report and investigation of public nuisance (2023)
content:
(a) Designation of department.--Council shall designate the department to which reports of the existence of a possible
      public nuisance shall be made.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12650. Regulation of parking lot and parking garage operators
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12650. Regulation of parking lot and parking garage operators
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12650. Regulation of parking lot and parking garage operators (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--For the purpose of protecting the public, a city may enact suitable ordinances regulating
      the business of operating for-profit parking lots and for-profit parking garages within
      the city.  Ordinances shall be consistent with 75 Pa.C.S. (relating to vehicles).  A city may require for-profit parking lots and for-profit parking garages to reserve
      areas exclusively for parking by handicapped individuals.  Nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the protections and prohibitions
      contained in section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (Public Law 101-336, 104 Stat. 327),1the act of October 27, 1955 (P.L. 744, No. 222),2known as the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, and Federal and State rules and regulations
      implementing those acts.  License and permit requirements may be imposed on for-profit parking lots and for-profit
      parking garages, and license or permit fees may be charged and collected from the
      operators of the parking lots and parking garages.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A03. Summary abatement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A03. Summary abatement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A03. Summary abatement (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--A city shall have the power to utilize summary abatement in accordance with this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A01. Definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A01. Definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A01. Definitions (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this chapter shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section unless the context clearly indicates otherwise:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A04. Prior notice of abatement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A04. Prior notice of abatement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A04. Prior notice of abatement (2023)
content:
(a) Abatement authority.--The department shall have the authority to abate a public nuisance with prior notice
      as provided by this section if, after inspecting the property or condition reported
      to be a public nuisance, subject to constitutional standards in a similar manner as
      provided in section 12308 (relating to powers of board of health), the department
      determines, as provided for in section 127A02(d)(1) (relating to report and investigation
      of public nuisance), that the public nuisance exists.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127. Real Estate Registry›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12704. Real estate registry
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127. Real Estate Registry › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12704. Real estate registry
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12704. Real estate registry (2023)
content:
(a) Registration requirement.--For the purpose of procuring accurate information on the ownership of all real estate,
      council may provide, by ordinance, for a real estate registry in accordance with the
      act of October 9, 2008 (P.L. 1400, No. 110),1known as the Uniform Municipal Deed Registration Act.  If required by the ordinance, every owner, subsequent purchaser, devisee or person
      acquiring title by partition, or otherwise, to real estate in the city shall furnish,
      at the designated city office, descriptions of their respective properties upon blanks
      to be furnished by the city and, at the same time, present their conveyance to be
      stamped by the designated city official or employee, without charge, as evidence of
      its registration.  A person who fails to register real estate as required by this chapter shall be
      liable for a penalty established by ordinance, with costs of suit, in the name and
      for the use of the city, as penalties for the violation of city ordinances are recoverable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A06. Appeal after notice and hearing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A06. Appeal after notice and hearing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A06. Appeal after notice and hearing (2023)
content:
(a) Hearing.--A city shall, by ordinance, provide a procedure by which an owner of the property
      who has been served with a notice pursuant to section 127A04(b)(1) or (2) (relating
      to prior notice of abatement) may request and have a timely hearing on the question
      of whether a public nuisance, in fact, exists.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12652. Insurance business
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 126. Licenses and License Fees › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12652. Insurance business
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12652. Insurance business (2023)
content:
A city may not levy or collect a license fee upon an insurance company or its agents
   or an insurance broker authorized to transact business under the laws of this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A07. Abatement by city after notice and statement of costs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A07. Abatement by city after notice and statement of costs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A07. Abatement by city after notice and statement of costs (2023)
content:
(a) Abatement by city after notice.--If a public nuisance has not been abated at the expiration of 30 days after notice
      has been provided or within additional time as the department or appeals board may
      grant, taking into consideration the provisions of section 127A06(c) (relating to
      appeal after notice and hearing), the department shall have the authority to enter
      upon the property for the purpose of abatement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A09. Salvage of material
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A09. Salvage of material
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A09. Salvage of material (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A08. Assistance in abatement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A08. Assistance in abatement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A08. Assistance in abatement (2023)
content:
In abating a public nuisance, the department may call upon any of the city departments
   or divisions for assistance, as shall be deemed necessary, or may abate the public
   nuisance by private contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 128. Eminent Domain›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12801. Exercise of eminent domain
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 128. Eminent Domain › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12801. Exercise of eminent domain
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12801. Exercise of eminent domain (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to all other purposes for which a city may exercise the power of eminent
      domain as authorized by this part or by other laws of this Commonwealth and subject
      to the duty to provide just compensation, a city may acquire property by eminent domain,
      including entering upon, appropriating, taking, using and occupying private lands
      and property for any of the following public purposes:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A05. Abatement by owner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A05. Abatement by owner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A05. Abatement by owner (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of owner.--Within 30 days after written notice has been provided pursuant to section 127A04(b)(1)
      or (2) (relating to prior notice of abatement), the owner shall remove and abate the
      nuisance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A10. Notice of assessment and appeal of charges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A10. Notice of assessment and appeal of charges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A10. Notice of assessment and appeal of charges (2023)
content:
(a) Notice of assessment.--Upon receipt of the statement of costs from the department, either for a summary abatement
      pursuant to section 127A03 (relating to summary abatement) or for an abatement with
      notice pursuant to section 127A04 (relating to prior notice of abatement), the city
      treasurer or other financial officer of the city designated by council shall, in accordance
      with section 127A04(b), give notice of the amount set forth in the statement of costs
      to the owner and lienholders of the property upon which the public nuisance has been
      abated.  The notice shall state that the city proposes to assess against the property the
      amount set forth in the notice and that objections to the proposed assessment must
      be made in writing and received by the designated officer within 20 days from the
      date of mailing the notice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 128. Eminent Domain›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12803. Title acquired
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 128. Eminent Domain › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12803. Title acquired
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12803. Title acquired (2023)
content:
Except as otherwise provided by law, if land or other real or personal property is
   acquired by a city in eminent domain proceedings or is acquired by gift, purchase
   or otherwise, the title obtained by the city shall be in fee simple absolute or like
   absolute ownership unless the parties agree otherwise in writing and the agreement
   expressly appears in a recorded deed affecting any real property acquired by the city
   or in the notice of condemnation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A11. Personal liability of owner
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A11. Personal liability of owner
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A11. Personal liability of owner (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding the right of the city to utilize in rem proceedings to pursue collection
   of the costs, fees and penalties in the statement of costs as a municipal claim, the
   person who is the owner of the property at the time of a summary abatement at which
   the notice required is given, or, in the case of an abatement pursuant to section
   127A04 (relating to prior notice of abatement), the person who was the owner of the
   property at the time notice of the existence of the public nuisance was given, shall
   be personally liable for the amount of the assessment, including all interest, other
   charges and, except as provided in section 127A10(g) (relating to notice of assessment
   and appeal of charges), civil penalties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A12. Administrative fee and civil penalties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 127A. Nuisance Abatement › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A12. Administrative fee and civil penalties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 127A12. Administrative fee and civil penalties (2023)
content:
Whenever a public nuisance is abated by the city, the statement of the costs of the
   public nuisance shall include the city's actual cost of abatement, plus an administrative
   fee, not to exceed 10%, and a civil penalty.  For the first abatement of a public nuisance upon any owner's property within the
   city in any two-year period, the civil penalty shall be $250.  For second and subsequent abatements upon any properties of any owner within the
   city during any two-year period, the civil penalty shall be $500.  The increased civil penalty shall be imposed and collected regardless of whether
   the second and subsequent public nuisances upon property or properties of an owner
   involve the same property or the public nuisances are of the same or different character.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12904. Improvements within laid-out streets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12904. Improvements within laid-out streets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12904. Improvements within laid-out streets (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--No permit shall be issued for any building within the lines of any street laid out
      pursuant to this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 128. Eminent Domain›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12824. Assessment awards
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 128. Eminent Domain › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12824. Assessment awards
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12824. Assessment awards (2023)
content:
In proceedings to assess damages and benefits, one of the following shall be awarded
   to or assessed against the owner of land and affected property:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12903. Effect of laying out street
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12903. Effect of laying out street
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12903. Effect of laying out street (2023)
content:
With regard to land not previously used by the city as a passageway for public travel,
   the laying out and locating of a street in accordance with this chapter shall not
   in and of itself do any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12917. Erection of improvements restricted
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12917. Erection of improvements restricted
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12917. Erection of improvements restricted (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Any ordinance widening or straightening any street shall fix the new line or lines.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12915. Power to open and alter streets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12915. Power to open and alter streets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12915. Power to open and alter streets (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--With regard to any street or any part of a street within city limits, a city may,
      with or without any petition of property owners, do any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12902. Laying out streets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12902. Laying out streets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12902. Laying out streets (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--A city may lay out streets by any of the following means:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 128. Eminent Domain›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12802. Restrictions as to certain property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 128. Eminent Domain › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12802. Restrictions as to certain property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12802. Restrictions as to certain property (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In addition to the restrictions made by other provisions of this part in particular
      cases or by any other provision of law, no city shall exercise the right of eminent
      domain against:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12916. Ordinances when no petition is presented
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12916. Ordinances when no petition is presented
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12916. Ordinances when no petition is presented (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An ordinance shall be enacted for the opening, widening, straightening, extending
      or vacating of any street without petition of property owners by the affirmative vote
      of a majority of the whole number of members of council, plus one.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12901. Map of streets
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12901. Map of streets
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12901. Map of streets (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council may authorize and approve a comprehensive map of city streets, which may be
      part of an official map adopted in accordance with the Municipalities Planning Code.1

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12930. Power to grade, pave and macadamize
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12930. Power to grade, pave and macadamize
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12930. Power to grade, pave and macadamize (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A city may grade, pave, macadamize or otherwise improve any street, and the sidewalks
      of the street when included as a part of the improvement, have them set with curbs
      and provide for drainage.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12918. Petition for opening
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12918. Petition for opening
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12918. Petition for opening (2023)
content:
(a) Presentment to council.--A petition may be presented to council for the opening, widening, straightening, altering,
      extending, vacating, establishing or reestablishing of the grade of any street.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12931. Payment of cost of improvement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12931. Payment of cost of improvement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12931. Payment of cost of improvement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The costs and expenses of the improvements done under section 12930 (relating to power
      to grade, pave and macadamize) shall be paid, in whole or in part, by the city or
      by the owners of real estate bounding and abutting the improvement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12919. Notice of petition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12919. Notice of petition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12919. Notice of petition (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--After a petition has been presented in accordance with section 12918 (relating to
      petition for opening) and council has determined the adequacy of the petition, but
      before final enactment of any ordinance enacted pursuant to the petition, notice shall
      be published in a newspaper of general circulation once a week for three consecutive
      weeks as required by section 10109 (relating to publication of notices), and handbills
      shall be posted in conspicuous places along the line of the proposed improvement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12922. Assessment of damages and benefits
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12922. Assessment of damages and benefits
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12922. Assessment of damages and benefits (2023)
content:
If necessary, in any proceedings to exercise one of the powers given in section 12915
   (relating to power to open and alter streets), viewers shall be appointed, damages
   awarded and benefits assessed as provided in 26 Pa.C.S. (relating to eminent domain)
   or as provided in this chapter for the assessment of benefits.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12950. Grade crossing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12950. Grade crossing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12950. Grade crossing (2023)
content:
(a) Railroad crossings.--A city constructing a street across a railroad shall construct the street above or
      below the grade of the railroad, unless permitted by the Pennsylvania Public Utility
      Commission to construct the street at grade.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12938. Preparation of streets for paving or repairing
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12938. Preparation of streets for paving or repairing
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12938. Preparation of streets for paving or repairing (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Council may provide, by ordinance, for the laying, renewing and repairing of all gas,
      water, steam or other pipes or conduits in any street before the paving, repaving
      or repairing of the street and for making the necessary connections with the pipes.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12955. Acquisition of unobstructed views
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12955. Acquisition of unobstructed views
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12955. Acquisition of unobstructed views (2023)
content:
Any city may acquire, by purchase or by the right of eminent domain, a free and unobstructed
   view down and across lands located at or near intersections or curves of streets,
   railroads or railways to assure a free and unobstructed view in all directions at
   the intersections or curves and to prevent the use of the lands over and across which
   the view was acquired for any purpose or in any manner which may interfere with or
   obstruct the vision of any person traveling upon any street within the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12985. Maintenance of streets forming boundaries
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12985. Maintenance of streets forming boundaries
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12985. Maintenance of streets forming boundaries (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A street on the boundary line between a city and another municipal corporation shall
      be maintained jointly by the city and the other municipal corporation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12939. Highways in cities
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12939. Highways in cities
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12939. Highways in cities (2023)
content:
(a) Power over highways.--Powers, rights and duties given to a city over its streets shall extend to highways
      to the extent that the city is legally responsible for them, pursuant to agreement
      or otherwise.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12988. Streets more than half of whose width is within city
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12988. Streets more than half of whose width is within city
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12988. Streets more than half of whose width is within city (2023)
content:
(a) Authority to improve entire street.--Whenever any street, more than one-half the width of which is within the limits of
      the city, shall divide the city from any other municipal corporation, the street may
      be improved by the city in the same manner as if the street were entirely located
      within the limits of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12970. Appropriation for connections with highways
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12970. Appropriation for connections with highways
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12970. Appropriation for connections with highways (2023)
content:
A city may, singly or jointly with other political subdivisions, appropriate money
   for the improvement of streets or roads beyond the limits of a city for the purpose
   of connecting improved streets in a city with a highway.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12960. Use of abutting lands for embankments, slopes, fills and culverts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12960. Use of abutting lands for embankments, slopes, fills and culverts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12960. Use of abutting lands for embankments, slopes, fills and culverts (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--In the grading of any street, a city may use so much of the lots and lands abutting
      on the street for the construction of embankments, slopes, fills and culverts as may
      be necessary for the completion of the improvement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12986. Streets, the center line of which is the boundary between city and another municipal corporation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12986. Streets, the center line of which is the boundary between city and another municipal corporation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12986. Streets, the center line of which is the boundary between city and another municipal corporation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A city may enter into a contract with a municipal corporation to provide for the grading,
      curbing, draining, paving and macadamizing of any street that constitutes the dividing
      line between the city and the municipal corporation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12989. Assessment for improvements on property outside limits where street entirely within city
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12989. Assessment for improvements on property outside limits where street entirely within city
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12989. Assessment for improvements on property outside limits where street entirely within city (2023)
content:
Whenever any street, entirely within the limits of any city, shall divide the city
   from any other municipal corporation, the property on the side of the street, within
   or outside the city, that abuts the street and benefits from the improvement may,
   for a depth of 150 feet from its center line, be assessed for any and all municipal
   improvements to or on the streets on which the property abuts in the same manner as
   the property would be assessed under the provisions of this part if it were entirely
   located within the limits of the city.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 129. Streets›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12975. Street closings and detours
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 129. Streets › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12975. Street closings and detours
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 12975. Street closings and detours (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--The following shall apply to the closing of a street to vehicular traffic:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13114. Recording of contract
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13114. Recording of contract
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13114. Recording of contract (2023)
content:
Any of the contracts provided for under this chapter may be recorded in the office
   of the recorder of deeds in the proper county.  The record shall be notice to all persons who might be affected by the contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 130. Sidewalks›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13002. Construction by cities upon failure of owner and collection of cost
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 130. Sidewalks › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13002. Construction by cities upon failure of owner and collection of cost
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13002. Construction by cities upon failure of owner and collection of cost (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Upon failure of any owner of property abutting any street to construct, pave, curb,
      repave, recurb or maintain any sidewalk, in accordance with the notice required in
      subsection (f), the city, itself or by contract, may complete the construction, paving,
      curbing, repaving, recurbing or maintenance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13101. Construction and maintenance of bridges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13101. Construction and maintenance of bridges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13101. Construction and maintenance of bridges (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Cities may locate, build and maintain bridges, wholly or partially within the city
      limits, along with the piers, abutments and approaches appurtenant to the bridges,
      to be used as public streets.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 130. Sidewalks›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13002.1. Ordinances
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 130. Sidewalks › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13002.1. Ordinances
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13002.1. Ordinances (2023)
content:
All reconstruction, repaving and recurbing of sidewalks may be included in the ordinance
   providing for the original construction, paving and curbing of sidewalks without the
   necessity for adopting a new ordinance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13102. Ordinance for location of bridges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13102. Ordinance for location of bridges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13102. Ordinance for location of bridges (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Cities may enact ordinances fixing the location and providing for the laying out and
      opening of the routes or locations for bridges, which shall be public streets.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 130. Sidewalks›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13003. Emergency repairs
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 130. Sidewalks › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13003. Emergency repairs
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13003. Emergency repairs (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any city may make emergency repairs to sidewalks, within its corporate limits, if
      an officer or designated individual representing the department in charge of repairs
      to sidewalks upon inspection determines that a substantial and immediate danger exists
      to public health, safety and welfare.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 130. Sidewalks›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13001. Power to lay out and grade sidewalks and compel construction of sidewalks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 130. Sidewalks › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13001. Power to lay out and grade sidewalks and compel construction of sidewalks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13001. Power to lay out and grade sidewalks and compel construction of sidewalks (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Any city may lay out, ordain and establish sidewalks, curbs, gutters and drains along
      any street, and may, with or without petition, require owners of property abutting
      any street to construct, pave, curb, repave and recurb the sidewalks and keep the
      sidewalks in good repair along their property at grades and under regulations and
      specifications as council may provide.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13110. Agreement for joint construction and maintenance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13110. Agreement for joint construction and maintenance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13110. Agreement for joint construction and maintenance (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The city may enter into an agreement with any political subdivision, public agency,
      public utility or any other person interested and by law authorized to enter into
      an agreement, or with any or all of them, for the laying out, construction, improvement
      and maintenance of any bridge and for the payment of any damages caused by the action.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part VI. Miscellaneous Provisions (Reserved) › PA ST T. 11 Pa.C.S.A., Pt. VI, Reserved

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13103. Right to appropriate property
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13103. Right to appropriate property
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13103. Right to appropriate property (2023)
content:
(a) Failure to agree on damages.--A city that has not agreed with an owner regarding damages done, or likely to be done,
      by the erection of the bridge may take and appropriate the lands and property necessary
      to erect the bridge.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13115. Power to construct boundary bridges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13115. Power to construct boundary bridges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13115. Power to construct boundary bridges (2023)
content:
Whenever a creek over which a bridge may be necessary shall be on the division line
   of a city and another municipality, the city may enter into an intergovernmental agreement
   pursuant to 53 Pa.C.S. Ch. 23 Subch. A (relating to intergovernmental cooperation) with the municipality for the construction
   and maintenance of a bridge and for apportionment of the costs.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities›Part V. Third Class Cities›Chapter 131. Bridges›PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13135. Acquisition of existing bridges
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 11 Pa.C.S.A. Cities › Part V. Third Class Cities › Chapter 131. Bridges › PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13135. Acquisition of existing bridges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 11 Pa.C.S.A. § 13135. Acquisition of existing bridges (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A city may purchase, condemn, maintain and use any public toll bridge crossing any
      river or stream within the limits of the municipality, together with the approaches
      and appurtenances to the toll bridge.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part I. General Provisions › Chapter 5. Small Business Council › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 503. Small Business Council

      Council.  The council shall do all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part I. General Provisions›Chapter 3. Economic Development Financing Strategy›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Oversight
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part I. General Provisions › Chapter 3. Economic Development Financing Strategy › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 304. Oversight

content:
Concurrent with the submission of the Governor's annual budget message, the department

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part I. General Provisions›Chapter 4. Pennsylvania Military Community Enhancement Commission›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 402. Establishment and membership
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part I. General Provisions › Chapter 4. Pennsylvania Military Community Enhancement Commission › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 402. Establishment and membership
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 402. Establishment and membership (2023)
content: (a) Establishment.--The commission is hereby established within the department.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part I. General Provisions›Chapter 5. Small Business Council›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Regulatory review
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part I. General Provisions › Chapter 5. Small Business Council › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Regulatory review
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 504. Regulatory review (2023)
content:
(a) Notification.--To the extent known to the secretary, the department shall, on a semiannual basis,
      provide the council with a list of regulations being proposed by all executive agencies
      which may affect small businesses in this Commonwealth.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part I. General Provisions›Chapter 4. Pennsylvania Military Community Enhancement Commission›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 404. Administrative assistance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part I. General Provisions › Chapter 4. Pennsylvania Military Community Enhancement Commission › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 404. Administrative assistance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 404. Administrative assistance (2023)
content:
The department shall provide appropriate administrative, legal and technical support
   as needed by the commission in order to accomplish its purpose.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part II. Economic Development Entities›Chapter 15. Pennsylvania-Ireland Trade Commission›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Pennsylvania-Ireland Trade Commission Fund
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part II. Economic Development Entities › Chapter 15. Pennsylvania-Ireland Trade Commission › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Pennsylvania-Ireland Trade Commission Fund
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 1503. Pennsylvania-Ireland Trade Commission Fund (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment and purposes.--The Pennsylvania-Ireland Trade Commission Fund is established as a nonlapsing fund
      within the State Treasury to accept financial assets to defray the administrative

content:

   chapter, or a requirement that one new job be created for a certain amount of funds
   loaned.  In establishing the minimum levels of job creation, the authority shall consider
   unemployment statistics, inflation, the authority's cash flow and the need to keep

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part III. Economic Development Programs › Chapter 32. Entertainment Economic Enhancement Program › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 3207. Carryover, carryback and assignment of tax credit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 3207. Carryover, carryback and assignment of tax credit (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If a recipient cannot use the entire amount of a tax credit for the taxable year in
      which the tax credit is first approved, the excess may be carried over to succeeding
      taxable years and used as a tax credit against the qualified tax liability of the
      recipient for those taxable years.  Each time the tax credit is carried over to a succeeding taxable year, the tax credit
      shall be reduced by the amount that was used as a credit during the immediately preceding
      taxable year.  The tax credit may be carried over and applied to succeeding taxable years for no
      more than three taxable years following the first taxable year for which the recipient
      was entitled to claim the tax credit.

   and tour expenses agreed to under section 3203(d)(4) (relating to procedure) for a

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 3903. Establishment (2023)
content:
There is established within the department a program to be known as the Water Supply
   and Wastewater Infrastructure Capitalization Program.  The program shall finance single-year or multiyear grants to municipalities and
   municipal authorities and loans to municipalities, municipal authorities, industrial
   development corporations and investor-owned water or wastewater enterprises for water
   projects which are approved by the authority, which, when completed, construct, expand
   or improve water and wastewater infrastructure and which are related to economic development.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part III. Economic Development Programs › Chapter 39. Water Supply and Wastewater Infrastructure Capitalization › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 3904. Award of grants
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 3904. Award of grants (2023)
content:
Upon being notified by the authority that a grant has been approved under64 Pa.C.S. § 1558(c)(relating to Water Supply and Wastewater Infrastructure Program) for an applicant,
   the department shall enter into a contract with the applicant.  The contract shall be for the amount approved by the authority, and if the grant
   provided for improvements on a site of a private facility that has or will be receiving
   additional economic development assistance or job creation tax credits from the Commonwealth,
   the contract shall include a provision that ensures that if the facility is closed
   or is sold within five years after the approval of the application, the Commonwealth
   shall request reimbursement of the grant and shall place a lien for that amount on
   the real property of that facility to remain on the real property until the Commonwealth
   receives reimbursement.  Upon entering into a contract with the applicant, the department shall award the
   grant for the amount specified in the contract.

content:

   National Commerce Act (Public Law 106-229,15 U.S.C. § 7001 et seq.), but does not modify, limit or supersede section 101(c) of the Electronic Signatures

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part IV. Commercial Protection›Chapter 53. Trade Secrets›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5303. Injunctive relief
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part IV. Commercial Protection › Chapter 53. Trade Secrets › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5303. Injunctive relief
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5303. Injunctive relief (2023)
content:
(a) Injunctions.--Actual or threatened misappropriation may be enjoined.  Upon application to the court, an injunction shall be terminated when the trade
      secret has ceased to exist, but the injunction may be continued for an additional
      reasonable period of time in order to eliminate commercial advantage that otherwise
      would be derived from the misappropriation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part IV. Commercial Protection›Chapter 53. Trade Secrets›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5306. Preservation of secrecy
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part IV. Commercial Protection › Chapter 53. Trade Secrets › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5306. Preservation of secrecy
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5306. Preservation of secrecy (2023)
content:
In any action under this chapter, a court shall preserve the secrecy of an alleged
   trade secret by reasonable means which may include, but are not limited to, granting
   protective orders in connection with discovery proceedings, holding in camera hearings,
   sealing the records of the action and ordering any person involved in the litigation
   not to disclose an alleged trade secret without prior court approval.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part IV. Commercial Protection›Chapter 53. Trade Secrets›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5304. Damages
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part IV. Commercial Protection › Chapter 53. Trade Secrets › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5304. Damages
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5304. Damages (2023)
content:
(a) Monetary damages.--Except to the extent that a material and prejudicial change of position prior to acquiring
      knowledge or reason to know of misappropriation renders a monetary recovery inequitable,
      a complainant is entitled to recover damages for misappropriation.  Damages can include both the actual loss caused by misappropriation and the unjust
      enrichment caused by misappropriation that is not taken into account in computing
      actual loss.  In lieu of damages measured by any other methods, the damages caused by misappropriation
      may be measured by imposition of liability for a reasonable royalty for a misappropriator's
      unauthorized disclosure or use of a trade secret.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part IV. Commercial Protection›Chapter 55. Legitimate Cannabis-Related Business›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5505. Access to information
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part IV. Commercial Protection › Chapter 55. Legitimate Cannabis-Related Business › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5505. Access to information
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5505. Access to information (2023)
content:
(a) Voluntary disclosures.--Section 1307 of the act of April 17, 2016 (P.L. 84, No. 16),1known as the Medical Marijuana Act, shall not prohibit the voluntary disclosure of
      any records or other information by a legitimate cannabis-related business, or a business
      associate to a financial institution or insurer, as necessary to obtain financial
      or insurance services to the extent not prohibited by and consistent with any applicable
      requirements of the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (Public Law 104-191, 110 Stat. 1936) privacy regulation as promulgated by the United States Department of Health and
      Human Services under45 CFR Pts. 160(relating to general administrative requirements), 162 (relating to administrative
      requirements) and 164 (relating to security and privacy) and16 CFR Pt. 313(relating to privacy of consumer financial information).

   after the misappropriation was discovered or by the exercise of reasonable diligence
   should have been discovered.

content:
(a) Notification by legitimate cannabis-related business.--If a legitimate cannabis-related business obtains financial or insurance services
      from a financial institution or insurer doing business in this Commonwealth, the business
      shall, within five business days, provide notice to the financial institution or insurer
      if a cannabis-related permit, registration or certification held by the business or
      its affiliates under Federal law, the laws of this Commonwealth or a law established
      by another state is suspended or revoked.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 5707. Maintenance of books and records (2023)
content:
An eligible financial institution that conducts a savings promotion program under
   this chapter shall maintain books and records relating to the conduct of the savings
   promotion program sufficient to facilitate an audit of the savings promotion program.  The financial institution shall keep a record of the names of winners of all savings
   promotion programs, which shall be available for inspection by the financial institution's
   customers.

      by this chapter, including, but not limited to, those pertaining to charges for service
      contracts, warranties, debt cancellation agreements, debt suspension agreements and
      insurance products not required by section 6241 (relating to insurance).

content:
License fees and fines that are received by the department under this chapter shall
   be deposited in the State Treasury to the credit of a special fund for the use of
   the department in administering this and other laws of this Commonwealth placed under
   its administration.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6226. Heavy commercial motor vehicle (2023)
content:
(a) Variable finance charge percentage rate.--Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, the finance charge percentage
      rate included in an installment sale contract for the sale of a heavy commercial motor
      vehicle may vary during the term of the contract pursuant to a formula or index set
      forth in the contract that is made readily available to and verifiable by the buyer
      and beyond the control of the holder of the contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter C. Installment Sale Contracts›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6224. Itemization

Costs and charges under sections 6222 (relating to contents) and 6242 (relating to
   other costs included in amount financed) shall be separately itemized in an installment
   sale contract as to their nature and amounts.

content:
(a) Installment seller.--An installment seller of a motor vehicle under an installment sale contract executed
      in this Commonwealth may not sell, transfer or assign the obligation represented by
      the contract to a person in this Commonwealth or elsewhere unless the person is licensed
      as a sales finance company under this chapter.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter C. Installment Sale Contracts›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6234. Waiver of statutory protection prohibited

content:

      of this chapter intended to protect a buyer of a motor vehicle.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part V. Consumer Credit › Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance › Subchapter C. Installment Sale Contracts › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6233. Prohibited charges
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6233. Prohibited charges (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as provided in subsections (b) and (c), a licensee may directly or indirectly
      charge, contract for, collect or receive from the buyer, in connection with the retail
      sale of a motor vehicle under an installment sale contract, insurance charges, other
      charges necessary or incidental to the sale of the motor vehicle, finance charges,
      refinance charges, late charges, recording and satisfaction fees, court costs, attorney
      fees and costs of retaking, repairing and storing a repossessed motor vehicle, which
      are disclosed as required by section 6222(5) (relating to contents).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter C. Installment Sale Contracts›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6235. Effect of license expiration, surrender and revocation on contracts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part V. Consumer Credit › Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance › Subchapter C. Installment Sale Contracts › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6235. Effect of license expiration, surrender and revocation on contracts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6235. Effect of license expiration, surrender and revocation on contracts (2023)
content:
(a) Effect.--The expiration, surrender or revocation of a license issued under this chapter to
      an installment seller or sales finance company does not impair or affect the obligation
      under an installment sale contract entered into lawfully or lawfully acquired by the
      licensee prior to the effective date of the expiration, surrender or revocation of
      the license.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter D. Costs and Charges›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6243. Finance charges

(a) General rule.--An installment seller licensed under this chapter may charge, contract for, receive

      the retail sale of a motor vehicle in this Commonwealth.

content:
(a) Right to prepay unpaid time balance.--Notwithstanding the provisions of an installment sale contract, a buyer may prepay
      at any time all or part of the unpaid time balance under the contract.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part V. Consumer Credit › Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance › Subchapter E. Repossession › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6254. Notice of repossession

      other than by legal process, the holder shall immediately furnish the buyer with a
      written notice of repossession.

content:
If repossession of a motor vehicle subject to an installment sale contract is effected
   other than by legal process, the buyer shall be liable for costs incurred by the holder

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter E. Repossession›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6253. Legal proceedings

content:

      or its collateral security is effected by legal process, the holder may commence legal
      proceedings immediately upon the buyer's default or breach of the contract.
