path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter E. Repossession›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6255. Personal property in repossessed motor vehicle
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part V. Consumer Credit › Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance › Subchapter E. Repossession › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6255. Personal property in repossessed motor vehicle
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6255. Personal property in repossessed motor vehicle (2023)
content:
A buyer may reclaim personal property left in the repossessed motor vehicle within
   30 days of the mailing of the notice under section 6254 (relating to notice of repossession).  If personal property is left in the motor vehicle after the 30-day time period,
   the holder may dispose of the personal property in any manner that it chooses.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter E. Repossession›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6261. Deficiency judgment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade › Part V. Consumer Credit › Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance › Subchapter E. Repossession › PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6261. Deficiency judgment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6261. Deficiency judgment (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--If the proceeds of a resale under section 6260 (relating to sale of motor vehicle
      after repossession) are not sufficient to defray the expenses regarding the repossessed
      motor vehicle, including the costs under section 6256 (relating to buyer's liability
      for costs), the net balance due on the installment sale contract and the amount of
      accrued late charges authorized by this chapter, the installment seller or holder
      may recover the deficiency from the buyer or from any person who has succeeded to
      the obligations of the buyer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 12 Pa.C.S.A. Commerce and Trade›Part V. Consumer Credit›Chapter 62. Motor Vehicle Sales Finance›Subchapter E. Repossession›PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6259. Redemption and termination of contract after repossession

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6259. Redemption and termination of contract after repossession (2023)
content:
(a) Retaining motor vehicle.--Unless the right of redemption is waived in a nonconsumer transaction under13 Pa.C.S. § 9624(c)(relating to waiver), if repossession of a motor vehicle subject to an installment
      sale contract is effected within or outside this Commonwealth other than by legal
      process, the holder shall retain the repossessed motor vehicle for a period of 15
      days after the mailing of the notice of repossession under section 6254 (relating
      to notice of repossession).

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 6274. Civil penalty by department (2023)
content:

content:

   a license under section 6218 (relating to revocation or suspension of license) or
   imposing a civil penalty under section 6274 (relating to civil penalty by department)

content:

      or information obtained through examinations relating to any activities regulated

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 12 Pa.C.S.A. § 9801. Assembled industrial plant doctrine abolished (2023)
content:

      plant doctrine or the integrated industrial mortgage doctrine, is abolished.  Whether personal property placed or installed in an industrial, commercial or other
      establishment is a fixture shall be determined by other law.

content:

content:

   no part of it shall be deemed to be impliedly repealed by subsequent legislation if
   such construction can reasonably be avoided.

Nothing in this title shall be construed to modify or supersede the provisions of
   42 Pa.C.S. Ch. 69 (relating to particular rights and immunities).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 11. General Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Use of singular and plural; gender (Reserved)
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 11. General Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Use of singular and plural; gender (Reserved)
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1106. Use of singular and plural; gender (Reserved) (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 12. General Definitions and Principles of Interpretation›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1203. Lease distinguished from security interest
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 12. General Definitions and Principles of Interpretation › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1203. Lease distinguished from security interest
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1203. Lease distinguished from security interest (2023)
content:
(a) Factual determination.--Whether a transaction in the form of a lease creates a lease or security interest
      is determined by the facts of each case.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 11. General Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Section captions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 11. General Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Section captions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1107. Section captions (2023)
content:
Notwithstanding1 Pa.C.S. § 1924(relating to construction of titles, preambles, provisos, exceptions and headings),
   section captions are part of this title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 11. General Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Construction of title to promote its purposes and policies; applicability of supplemental principles of law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 11. General Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Construction of title to promote its purposes and policies; applicability of supplemental principles of law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1103. Construction of title to promote its purposes and policies; applicability of supplemental principles of law (2023)
content:
(a) Liberal construction.--This title must be liberally construed and applied to promote its underlying purposes
      and policies, which are:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 11. General Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Scope of division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 11. General Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Scope of division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1102. Scope of division (2023)
content:
This division applies to a transaction to the extent that it is governed by another
   division of this title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 11. General Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Short titles
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 11. General Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Short titles
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1101. Short titles (2023)
content: (a) Title.--This title may be cited as the Uniform Commercial Code.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1304. Obligation of good faith
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1304. Obligation of good faith
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1304. Obligation of good faith (2023)
content:
Every contract or duty within this title imposes an obligation of good faith in its
   performance and enforcement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1303. Course of performance, course of dealing and usage of trade
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1303. Course of performance, course of dealing and usage of trade
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1303. Course of performance, course of dealing and usage of trade (2023)
content:
(a) Course of performance.--A “course of performance” is a sequence of conduct between the parties to a particular transaction that exists
      if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 11. General Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. (Reserved)
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 11. General Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. (Reserved)
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1105. (Reserved) (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Territorial applicability; parties' power to choose applicable law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Territorial applicability; parties' power to choose applicable law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1301. Territorial applicability; parties' power to choose applicable law (2023)
content:
(a) Agreement;  reasonable relation requirement.--Except as otherwise provided in this section, when a transaction bears a reasonable
      relation to this Commonwealth and also to another state or nation, the parties may
      agree that the law either of this Commonwealth or of such other state or nation shall
      govern their rights and duties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1302. Variation by agreement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1302. Variation by agreement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1302. Variation by agreement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (b) or elsewhere in this title, the effect
      of provisions of this title may be varied by agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1308. Performance or acceptance under reservation of rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1308. Performance or acceptance under reservation of rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1308. Performance or acceptance under reservation of rights (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as set forth in subsection (b), a party that with explicit reservation of rights
      performs or promises performance or assents to performance in a manner demanded or
      offered by the other party does not thereby prejudice the rights reserved.  The words “without prejudice,” “under protest” and the like are sufficient.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1309. Option to accelerate at will
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1309. Option to accelerate at will
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1309. Option to accelerate at will (2023)
content:
A term providing that one party or that party's successor in interest may accelerate
   payment or performance or require collateral or additional collateral “at will” or when the party “deems itself insecure,” or words of similar import, means that the party has power to do so only if that
   party in good faith believes that the prospect of payment or performance is impaired.  The burden of establishing lack of good faith is on the party against which the
   power has been exercised.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2102. Scope; certain security and other transactions excluded from division (2023)
content:
(a) Scope.--Unless the context otherwise requires, and except as provided in subsection (c), this
      division applies to transactions in goods and, in the case of a hybrid transaction,
      this division applies to the extent provided in subsection (b).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1310. Subordinated obligations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1310. Subordinated obligations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1310. Subordinated obligations (2023)
content:
An obligation may be issued as subordinated to performance of another obligation of
   the person obligated, or a creditor may subordinate its right to performance of an
   obligation by agreement with either the person obligated or another creditor of the
   person obligated.  Subordination does not create a security interest as against either the common debtor
   or a subordinated creditor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1306. Waiver or renunciation of claim or right after breach
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1306. Waiver or renunciation of claim or right after breach
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1306. Waiver or renunciation of claim or right after breach (2023)
content:
A claim or right arising out of an alleged breach may be discharged in whole or in
   part without consideration by agreement of the aggrieved party in a signed record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1307. Prima facie evidence by third-party documents
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1307. Prima facie evidence by third-party documents
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1307. Prima facie evidence by third-party documents (2023)
content:
A document in due form purporting to be a bill of lading, a policy or certificate
   of insurance, an official weigher's or inspector's certificate, a consular invoice
   or any other document authorized or required by the contract to be issued by a third
   party is prima facie evidence of its own authenticity and genuineness and of the facts
   stated in the document by the third party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Seals inoperative
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Seals inoperative
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2203. Seals inoperative (2023)
content:
The affixing of a seal to a record evidencing a contract for sale or an offer to buy
   or sell goods does not constitute the record a sealed instrument and the law with
   respect to sealed instruments does not apply to such a contract or offer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2104. Definitions: “merchant”; “between merchants”; “financing agency” (2023)
content:
The following words and phrases when used in this division shall have the meanings
   given to them in this section:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 1. General Provisions›Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1305. Remedies to be liberally administered
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 1. General Provisions › Chapter 13. Territorial Applicability and General Rules › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1305. Remedies to be liberally administered
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 1305. Remedies to be liberally administered (2023)
content:
(a) Administration.--The remedies provided by this title must be liberally administered to the end that
      the aggrieved party may be put in as good a position as if the other party had fully
      performed, but neither consequential or special damages nor penal damages may be had
      except as specifically provided in this title or by other rule of law.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Short title of division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Short title of division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2101. Short title of division (2023)
content: This division shall be known and may be cited as theUniform Commercial Code, Article 2, Sales.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Goods to be severed from realty: recording
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Goods to be severed from realty: recording
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2107. Goods to be severed from realty: recording (2023)
content:
(a) Minerals and structures.--A contract for the sale of minerals or the like (including oil and gas) or a structure
      or its materials to be removed from realty is a contract for the sale of goods within
      this division if they are to be severed by the seller but until severance a purported
      present sale thereof which is not effective as a transfer of an interest in land is
      effective only as a contract to sell.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation”; “hybrid transaction”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation”; “hybrid transaction”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2106. Definitions: “contract”; “agreement”; “contract for sale”; “sale”; “present sale”; “conforming” to contract; “termination”; “cancellation”; “hybrid transaction” (2023)
content:
(a) “Contract”, “agreement”, “sale”.--In this division unless the context otherwise requires “contract” and “agreement”
      are limited to those relating to the present or future sale of goods.  “Contract for sale” includes both a present sale of goods and a contract to sell
      goods at a future time.  A “sale” consists in the passing of title from the seller to the buyer for a price
      (section 2401).  A “present sale” means a sale which is accomplished by the making of the contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Definitions and index of definitions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Definitions and index of definitions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2103. Definitions and index of definitions (2023)
content:
(a) Definitions.--The following words and phrases when used in this division shall have, unless the
      context clearly indicates otherwise, the meanings given to them in this subsection:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Final expression: parol or extrinsic evidence
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Final expression: parol or extrinsic evidence
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2202. Final expression: parol or extrinsic evidence (2023)
content:
Terms with respect to which the confirmatory memoranda of the parties agree or which
   are otherwise set forth in a record intended by the parties as a final expression
   of their agreement with respect to such terms as are included therein may not be contradicted
   by evidence of any prior agreement or of a contemporaneous oral agreement but may
   be explained or supplemented:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2201. Formal requirements; statute of frauds (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in this section a contract for the sale of goods for
      the price of $500 or more is not enforceable by way of action or defense unless there
      is a record sufficient to indicate that a contract for sale has been made between
      the parties and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought or by the party's
      authorized agent or broker.  A record is not insufficient because it omits or incorrectly states a term agreed
      upon but the contract is not enforceable under this subsection beyond the quantity
      of goods shown in the record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Firm offers
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Firm offers
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2205. Firm offers (2023)
content:
An offer by a merchant to buy or sell goods in a signed record which by its terms
   gives assurance that it will be held open is not revocable, for lack of consideration,
   during the time stated or if no time is stated for a reasonable time, but in no event
   may such period of irrevocability exceed three months;  but any such term of assurance
   on a form supplied by the offeree must be separately signed by the offeror.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Modification, rescission and waiver
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Modification, rescission and waiver
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2209. Modification, rescission and waiver (2023)
content:
(a) Consideration unnecessary for modification.--An agreement modifying a contract within this division needs no consideration to be
      binding.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 21. Short Title, General Construction and Subject Matter › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2105. Definitions: transferability; “goods”; “future” goods; “lot”; “commercial unit” (2023)
content:
(a) “Goods”.--“Goods” means all things (including specially manufactured goods) which are movable
      at the time of identification to the contract for sale other than the money in which
      the price is to be paid, investment securities (Division 8) and things in action.  “Goods” also includes the unborn young of animals and growing crops and other identified
      things attached to realty as described in section 2107 (relating to goods to be severed
      from realty;  recording).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2210. Delegation of performance; assignment of rights (2023)
content:
(a) Delegation of performance.--A party may perform his duty through a delegate unless otherwise agreed or unless
      the other party has a substantial interest in having his original promisor perform
      or control the acts required by the contract.  No delegation of performance relieves the party delegating of any duty to perform
      or any liability for breach.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Formation in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Formation in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2204. Formation in general (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A contract for sale of goods may be made in any manner sufficient to show agreement,
      including conduct by both parties which recognizes the existence of such a contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. General obligations of parties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. General obligations of parties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2301. General obligations of parties (2023)
content:
The obligation of the seller is to transfer and deliver and that of the buyer is to
   accept and pay in accordance with the contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2207. Additional terms in acceptance or confirmation (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A definite and seasonable expression of acceptance or a written confirmation which
      is sent within a reasonable time operates as an acceptance even though it states terms
      additional to or different from those offered or agreed upon, unless acceptance is
      expressly made conditional on assent to the additional or different terms.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 22. Form, Formation and Readjustment of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Offer and acceptance in formation of contract

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2206. Offer and acceptance in formation of contract (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Unless otherwise unambiguously indicated by the language or circumstances:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2304. Price payable in money, goods, realty or otherwise
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2304. Price payable in money, goods, realty or otherwise
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2304. Price payable in money, goods, realty or otherwise (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The price can be made payable in money or otherwise.  If it is payable in whole or in part in goods each party is a seller of the goods
      which he is to transfer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2303. Allocation or division of risks
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2303. Allocation or division of risks
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2303. Allocation or division of risks (2023)
content:
Where this division allocates a risk or a burden as between the parties “unless otherwise
   agreed,” the agreement may not only shift the allocation but may also divide the risk
   or burden.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2306. Output, requirements and exclusive dealings (2023)
content:
(a) Quantity measured by output or requirements.--A term which measures the quantity by the output of the seller or the requirements
      of the buyer means such actual output or requirements as may occur in good faith,
      except that no quantity unreasonably disproportionate to any stated estimate or in
      the absence of a stated estimate to any normal or otherwise comparable prior output
      or requirements may be tendered or demanded.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2305. Open price term

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2305. Open price term (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The parties if they so intend can conclude a contract for sale even though the price
      is not settled.  In such a case the price is a reasonable price at the time for delivery if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2302. Unconscionable contract or clause

content:
(a) Finding and authority of court.--If the court as a matter of law finds the contract or any clause of the contract

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2307. Delivery in single lot or several lots
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2307. Delivery in single lot or several lots
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2307. Delivery in single lot or several lots (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed all goods called for by a contract for sale must be tendered
   in a single delivery and payment is due only on such tender but where the circumstances
   give either party the right to make or demand delivery in lots the price if it can
   be apportioned may be demanded for each lot.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2308. Absence of specified place for delivery (2023)
content: Unless otherwise agreed:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Options and cooperation respecting performance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Options and cooperation respecting performance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2311. Options and cooperation respecting performance (2023)
content:
(a) Specifying particulars of performance.--An agreement for sale which is otherwise sufficiently definite (section 2204(c))
      to be a contract is not made invalid by the fact that it leaves particulars of performance
      to be specified by one of the parties.  Any such specification must be made in good faith and within limits set by commercial
      reasonableness.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Warranty of title and against infringement; obligation of buyer against infringement

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2312. Warranty of title and against infringement; obligation of buyer against infringement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to subsection (b) there is in a contract for sale a warranty by the seller

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2313. Express warranties by affirmation, promise, description or sample (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Express warranties by the seller are created as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2318. Third party beneficiaries of warranties express or implied (2023)
content:
The warranty of a seller whether express or implied extends to any natural person
   who is in the family or household of his buyer or who is a guest in his home if it
   is reasonable to expect that such person may use, consume or be affected by the goods
   and who is injured in person by breach of the warranty.  A seller may not exclude or limit the operation of this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2320. C.I.F. and C. & F. terms (2023)
content:
(a) Definitions.--The term C.I.F. means that the price includes in a lump sum the cost of the goods
      and the insurance and freight to the named destination.  The term C. & F. or C.F. means that the price so includes cost and freight to the
      named destination.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2309. Absence of specific time provisions; notice of termination (2023)
content:
(a) Shipment, delivery or other action.--The time for shipment or delivery or any other action under a contract if not provided
      in this division or agreed upon shall be a reasonable time.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2317. Cumulation and conflict of warranties express or implied (2023)
content:
Warranties whether express or implied shall be construed as consistent with each other
   and as cumulative, but if such construction is unreasonable the intention of the parties
   shall determine which warranty is dominant.  In ascertaining that intention the following rules apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2314. Implied warranty: merchantability; usage of trade
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2314. Implied warranty: merchantability; usage of trade
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2314. Implied warranty: merchantability; usage of trade (2023)
content:
(a) Sale by merchant.--Unless excluded or modified (section 2316), a warranty that the goods shall be merchantable
      is implied in a contract for their sale if the seller is a merchant with respect to
      goods of that kind.  Under this section the serving for value of food or drink to be consumed either
      on the premises or elsewhere is a sale.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2319. F.O.B. and F.A.S. terms
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2319. F.O.B. and F.A.S. terms
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2319. F.O.B. and F.A.S. terms (2023)
content:
(a) Definition of F.O.B.--Unless otherwise agreed the term F.O.B. (which means “free on board”) at a named
      place, even though used only in connection with the stated price, is a delivery term
      under which:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2316. Exclusion or modification of warranties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2316. Exclusion or modification of warranties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2316. Exclusion or modification of warranties (2023)
content:
(a) Construction of words or conduct limiting warranties.--Words or conduct relevant to the creation of an express warranty and words or conduct
      tending to negate or limit warranty shall be construed wherever reasonable as consistent
      with each other;  but subject to the provisions of this division on parol or extrinsic
      evidence (section 2202) negation or limitation is inoperative to the extent that such
      construction is unreasonable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2323. Form of bill of lading required in overseas shipment; “overseas”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2323. Form of bill of lading required in overseas shipment; “overseas”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2323. Form of bill of lading required in overseas shipment; “overseas” (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Where the contract contemplates overseas shipment and contains a term C.I.F., C.
      & F. or F.O.B. vessel, the seller unless otherwise agreed must obtain a negotiable
      bill of lading stating that the goods have been loaded on board or, in the case of
      a term C.I.F. or C. & F., received for shipment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2322. Delivery “ex-ship”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2322. Delivery “ex-ship”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2322. Delivery “ex-ship” (2023)
content:
(a) Definition.--Unless otherwise agreed a term for delivery of goods “ex-ship” (which means from
      the carrying vessel) or in equivalent language is not restricted to a particular ship
      and requires delivery from a ship which has reached a place at the named port of destination
      where goods of the kind are usually discharged.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 24. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2402. Rights of creditors of seller against sold goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 24. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2402. Rights of creditors of seller against sold goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2402. Rights of creditors of seller against sold goods (2023)
content:
(a) Priority of buyer over unsecured creditors.--Except as provided in subsections (b) and (c), rights of unsecured creditors of
      the seller with respect to goods which have been identified to a contract for sale
      are subject to the rights of the buyer to recover the goods under this division (section
      2502 (relating to right of buyer to goods on insolvency of seller) and section 2716
      (relating to right of buyer to specific performance or replevin)).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2325. “Letter of credit” term; “confirmed credit”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2325. “Letter of credit” term; “confirmed credit”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2325. “Letter of credit” term; “confirmed credit” (2023)
content:
(a) Failure to furnish letter.--Failure of the buyer seasonably to furnish an agreed letter of credit is a breach
      of the contract for sale.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 24. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2403. Power to transfer; good faith purchase of goods; “entrusting”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 24. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2403. Power to transfer; good faith purchase of goods; “entrusting”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2403. Power to transfer; good faith purchase of goods; “entrusting” (2023)
content:
(a) Transfer of title.--A purchaser of goods acquires all title which his transferor had or had power to
      transfer except that a purchaser of a limited interest acquires rights only to the
      extent of the interest purchased.  A person with voidable title has power to transfer a good title to a good faith
      purchaser for value.  When goods have been delivered under a transaction of purchase the purchaser has
      such power even though:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2328. Sale by auction
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2328. Sale by auction
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2328. Sale by auction (2023)
content:
(a) Sale in lots.--In a sale by auction if goods are put up in lots each lot is the subject of a separate
      sale.

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Insurable interest in goods; manner of identification of goods

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2501. Insurable interest in goods; manner of identification of goods (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The buyer obtains a special property and an insurable interest in goods by identification
      of existing goods as goods to which the contract refers even though the goods so identified
      are nonconforming and he has an option to return or reject them.  Such identification can be made at any time and in any manner explicitly agreed
      to by the parties.  In the absence of explicit agreement identification occurs as follows:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 23. General Obligation and Construction of Contract›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2326. Sale on approval and sale or return; rights of creditors

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2326. Sale on approval and sale or return; rights of creditors (2023)
content:

content: (a) Sale on approval.--Under a sale on approval unless otherwise agreed:

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Right of buyer to goods on repudiation, failure to deliver or insolvency of seller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2502. Right of buyer to goods on repudiation, failure to deliver or insolvency of seller (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to subsections (b) and (c) and even though the goods have not been shipped
      a buyer who has paid a part or all of the price of goods in which he has a special
      property under the provisions of section 2501 (relating to insurable interest in goods;
      manner of identification of goods) may on making and keeping good a tender of any
      unpaid portion of their price recover them from the seller if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Manner of tender of delivery by seller
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Manner of tender of delivery by seller
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2503. Manner of tender of delivery by seller (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Tender of delivery requires that the seller put and hold conforming goods at the
      disposition of the buyer and give the buyer any notification reasonably necessary
      to enable him to take delivery.  The manner, time and place for tender are determined by the agreement and this division,
      and in particular:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Rights of financing agency
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Rights of financing agency
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2506. Rights of financing agency (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A financing agency by paying or purchasing for value a draft which relates to a
      shipment of goods acquires to the extent of the payment or purchase and in addition
      to its own rights under the draft and any document of title securing it any rights
      of the shipper in the goods including the right to stop delivery and the right of
      the shipper to have the draft honored by the buyer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2508. Cure by seller of improper tender or delivery; replacement (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Where any tender or delivery by the seller is rejected because nonconforming and
      the time for performance has not yet expired, the seller may seasonably notify the
      buyer of his intention to cure and may then within the contract time make a conforming
      delivery.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 24. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2401. Passing of title; reservation for security; limited application of section
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 24. Title, Creditors and Good Faith Purchasers › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2401. Passing of title; reservation for security; limited application of section
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2401. Passing of title; reservation for security; limited application of section (2023)
content:
Each provision of this division with regard to the rights, obligations and remedies
   of the seller, the buyer, purchasers or other third parties applies irrespective of
   title to the goods except where the provision refers to such title.  Insofar as situations are not covered by the other provisions of this division and
   matters concerning title become material the following rules apply:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2510. Effect of breach on risk of loss
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2510. Effect of breach on risk of loss
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2510. Effect of breach on risk of loss (2023)
content:
(a) Tender of nonconforming goods.--Where a tender or delivery of goods so fails to conform to the contract as to give
      a right of rejection the risk of their loss remains on the seller until cure or acceptance.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Effect of tender by seller; delivery on condition
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Effect of tender by seller; delivery on condition
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2507. Effect of tender by seller; delivery on condition (2023)
content:
(a) Effect of tender by seller.--Tender of delivery is a condition to the duty of the buyer to accept the goods,
      and unless otherwise agreed, to his duty to pay for them.  Tender entitles the seller to acceptance of the goods and to payment according to
      the contract.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Preserving evidence of goods in dispute
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Preserving evidence of goods in dispute
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2515. Preserving evidence of goods in dispute (2023)
content: In furtherance of the adjustment of any claim or dispute:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2512. Payment by buyer before inspection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2512. Payment by buyer before inspection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2512. Payment by buyer before inspection (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Where the contract requires payment before inspection nonconformity of the goods
      does not excuse the buyer from so making payment unless:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2509. Risk of loss in absence of breach
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2509. Risk of loss in absence of breach
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2509. Risk of loss in absence of breach (2023)
content: (a) Seller to ship by carrier.--Where the contract requires or authorizes the seller to ship the goods by carrier:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2601. Rights of buyer on improper delivery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2601. Rights of buyer on improper delivery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2601. Rights of buyer on improper delivery (2023)
content:
Subject to the provisions of this division on breach in installment contracts (section
   2612) and unless otherwise agreed under the sections on contractual limitations of
   remedy (sections 2718 and 2719), if the goods or the tender of delivery fail in any
   respect to conform to the contract, the buyer may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. When documents deliverable on acceptance; when on payment
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. When documents deliverable on acceptance; when on payment
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2514. When documents deliverable on acceptance; when on payment (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed documents against which a draft is drawn are to be delivered
   to the drawee on acceptance of the draft if it is payable more than three days after
   presentment;  otherwise only on payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2604. Options of buyer as to salvage of rightfully rejected goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2604. Options of buyer as to salvage of rightfully rejected goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2604. Options of buyer as to salvage of rightfully rejected goods (2023)
content:
Subject to the provisions on perishables in section 2603 (relating to duties of merchant
   buyer as to rightfully rejected goods) if the seller gives no instructions within
   a reasonable time after notification of rejection the buyer may store the rejected
   goods for the account of the seller or reship them to him or resell them for the account
   of the seller with reimbursement as provided in section 2603.  Such action is not acceptance or conversion.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2511. Tender of payment by buyer; payment by check
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2511. Tender of payment by buyer; payment by check
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2511. Tender of payment by buyer; payment by check (2023)
content:
(a) Tender of payment condition to delivery.--Unless otherwise agreed tender of payment is a condition to the duty of the seller
      to tender and complete any delivery.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2607. Effect of acceptance; notice of breach; burden of establishing breach after acceptance; notice of claim or litigation to person answerable over
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2607. Effect of acceptance; notice of breach; burden of establishing breach after acceptance; notice of claim or litigation to person answerable over
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2607. Effect of acceptance; notice of breach; burden of establishing breach after acceptance; notice of claim or litigation to person answerable over (2023)
content: (a) Payment for accepted goods.--The buyer must pay at the contract rate for any goods accepted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2605. Waiver of objections of buyer by failure to particularize
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2605. Waiver of objections of buyer by failure to particularize
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2605. Waiver of objections of buyer by failure to particularize (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The failure of the buyer to state in connection with rejection a particular defect
      which is ascertainable by reasonable inspection precludes him from relying on the
      unstated defect to justify rejection or to establish breach:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2611. Retraction of anticipatory repudiation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2611. Retraction of anticipatory repudiation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2611. Retraction of anticipatory repudiation (2023)
content:
(a) When allowable.--Until the next performance is due by the repudiating party he can retract his repudiation
      unless the aggrieved party has since the repudiation cancelled or materially changed
      his position or otherwise indicated that he considers the repudiation final.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Duties of merchant buyer as to rightfully rejected goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Duties of merchant buyer as to rightfully rejected goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2603. Duties of merchant buyer as to rightfully rejected goods (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Subject to any security interest in the buyer (section 2711(c) ), when the seller
      has no agent or place of business at the market of rejection a merchant buyer is under
      a duty after rejection of goods in his possession or control to follow any reasonable
      instructions received from the seller with respect to the goods and in the absence
      of such instructions to make reasonable efforts to sell them for the account of the
      seller if they are perishable or threaten to decline in value speedily.  Instructions are not reasonable if on demand indemnity for expenses is not forthcoming.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2602. Manner and effect of rightful rejection
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2602. Manner and effect of rightful rejection
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2602. Manner and effect of rightful rejection (2023)
content: (a) Time and notice of rejection.--Rejection of goods must be within a reasonable time after their delivery or tender.  It is ineffective unless the buyer seasonably notifies the seller.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2612. “Installment contract”; breach
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2612. “Installment contract”; breach
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2612. “Installment contract”; breach (2023)
content:
(a) Definition of “installment contract”.--An “installment contract” is one which requires or authorizes the delivery of goods
      in separate lots to be separately accepted, even though the contract contains a clause
      “each delivery is a separate contract” or its equivalent.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2608. Revocation of acceptance in whole or in part
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2608. Revocation of acceptance in whole or in part
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2608. Revocation of acceptance in whole or in part (2023)
content:
(a) Grounds for revocation.--The buyer may revoke his acceptance of a lot or commercial unit whose nonconformity
      substantially impairs its value to him if he has accepted it:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2609. Right to adequate assurance of performance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2609. Right to adequate assurance of performance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2609. Right to adequate assurance of performance (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A contract for sale imposes an obligation on each party that the expectation of
      the other of receiving due performance will not be impaired.  When reasonable grounds for insecurity arise with respect to the performance of
      either party the other may in writing demand adequate assurance of due performance
      and until he receives such assurance may if commercially reasonable suspend any performance
      for which he has not already received the agreed return.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2613. Casualty to identified goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2613. Casualty to identified goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2613. Casualty to identified goods (2023)
content:
Where the contract requires for its performance goods identified when the contract
   is made and the goods suffer casualty without fault of either party before the risk
   of loss passes to the buyer, or in a proper case under a “no arrival, no sale” term
   (section 2324) then:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 25. Performance›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2513. Right of buyer to inspection of goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 25. Performance › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2513. Right of buyer to inspection of goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2513. Right of buyer to inspection of goods (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Unless otherwise agreed and subject to subsection (c), where goods are tendered
      or delivered or identified to the contract for sale, the buyer has a right before
      payment or acceptance to inspect them at any reasonable place and time and in any
      reasonable manner.  When the seller is required or authorized to send the goods to the buyer, the inspection
      may be after their arrival.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2606. What constitutes acceptance of goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2606. What constitutes acceptance of goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2606. What constitutes acceptance of goods (2023)
content: (a) General rule.--Acceptance of goods occurs when the buyer:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2610. Anticipatory repudiation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2610. Anticipatory repudiation
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2610. Anticipatory repudiation (2023)
content:
When either party repudiates the contract with respect to a performance not yet due
   the loss of which will substantially impair the value of the contract to the other,
   the aggrieved party may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2701. Remedies for breach of collateral contracts not impaired
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2701. Remedies for breach of collateral contracts not impaired
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2701. Remedies for breach of collateral contracts not impaired (2023)
content:
Remedies for breach of any obligation or promise collateral or ancillary to a contract
   for sale are not impaired by the provisions of this division.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2702. Remedies of seller on discovery of insolvency of buyer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2702. Remedies of seller on discovery of insolvency of buyer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2702. Remedies of seller on discovery of insolvency of buyer (2023)
content:
(a) Right to refuse or stop delivery.--Where the seller discovers the buyer to be insolvent he may refuse delivery except
      for cash including payment for all goods theretofore delivered under the contract
      and stop delivery under this division (section 2705).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703. Remedies of seller in general
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703. Remedies of seller in general
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2703. Remedies of seller in general (2023)
content:
Where the buyer wrongfully rejects or revokes acceptance of goods or fails to make
   a payment due on or before delivery or repudiates with respect to a part or on the
   whole, then with respect to any goods directly affected and, if the breach is of the
   whole contract (section 2612), then also with respect to the whole undelivered balance,
   the aggrieved seller may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2706. Resale by seller including contract for resale
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2706. Resale by seller including contract for resale
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2706. Resale by seller including contract for resale (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Under the conditions stated in section 2703 (relating to remedies of seller in general),
      the seller may resell the goods concerned or the undelivered balance thereof.  Where the resale is made in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner the
      seller may recover the difference between the resale price and the contract price
      together with any incidental damages allowed under the provisions of this division
      (section 2710), but less expenses saved in consequence of the breach by the buyer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2616. Procedure on notice claiming excuse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2616. Procedure on notice claiming excuse
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2616. Procedure on notice claiming excuse (2023)
content:
(a) Right of buyer to terminate or modify contract.--Where the buyer receives notification of a material or indefinite delay or an allocation
      justified under section 2615 (relating to excuse by failure of presupposed conditions)
      he may by written notification to the seller as to any delivery concerned, and where
      the prospective deficiency substantially impairs the value of the whole contract under
      the provisions of this division relating to breach of installment contracts (section
      2612), then also as to the whole:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2614. Substituted performance
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2614. Substituted performance
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2614. Substituted performance (2023)
content:
(a) Manner of delivery.--Where without fault of either party the agreed berthing, loading, or unloading facilities
      fail or an agreed type of carrier becomes unavailable or the agreed manner of delivery
      otherwise becomes commercially impracticable but a commercially reasonable substitute
      is available, such substitute performance must be tendered and accepted.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2615. Excuse by failure of presupposed conditions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 26. Breach, Repudiation and Excuse › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2615. Excuse by failure of presupposed conditions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2615. Excuse by failure of presupposed conditions (2023)
content:
Except so far as a seller may have assumed a greater obligation and subject to section
   2614 (relating to substituted performance):

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2704. Right of seller to identify goods to contract notwithstanding breach or to salvage unfinished goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2704. Right of seller to identify goods to contract notwithstanding breach or to salvage unfinished goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2704. Right of seller to identify goods to contract notwithstanding breach or to salvage unfinished goods (2023)
content:
(a) Identification and resale of goods.--An aggrieved seller under section 2703 (relating to remedies of seller in general)
      may:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2709. Action for the price
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2709. Action for the price
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2709. Action for the price (2023)
content:
(a) When allowable.--When the buyer fails to pay the price as it becomes due the seller may recover,
      together with any incidental damages under section 2710 (relating to incidental damages
      of seller), the price of:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Remedies of buyer in general; security interest of buyer in rejected goods
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Remedies of buyer in general; security interest of buyer in rejected goods
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2711. Remedies of buyer in general; security interest of buyer in rejected goods (2023)
content:
(a) Cancellation and additional remedies.--Where the seller fails to make delivery or repudiates or the buyer rightfully rejects
      or justifiably revokes acceptance then with respect to any goods involved, and with
      respect to the whole if the breach goes to the whole contract (section 2612 (relating
      to “installment contract”;  breach) ), the buyer may cancel and whether or not he
      has done so may in addition to recovering so much of the price as has been paid:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2707. “Person in the position of a seller”
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2707. “Person in the position of a seller”
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2707. “Person in the position of a seller” (2023)
content: (a) Definition.--A “person in the position of a seller” includes:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 2. Sales›Chapter 27. Remedies›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2705. Stoppage by seller of delivery in transit or otherwise
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 2. Sales › Chapter 27. Remedies › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2705. Stoppage by seller of delivery in transit or otherwise
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 2705. Stoppage by seller of delivery in transit or otherwise (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--The seller may stop delivery of goods in the possession of a carrier or other bailee
      when he discovers the buyer to be insolvent (section 2702) and may stop delivery of
      carload, truckload, planeload or larger shipments of express or freight when the buyer
      repudiates or fails to make a payment due before delivery, or if for any other reason
      the seller has a right to withhold or reclaim the goods.
