      the bank has the following obligations in executing the order:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A2. Issue and Acceptance of Payment Order›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A212. Liability and duty of receiving bank regarding unaccepted payment order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A2. Issue and Acceptance of Payment Order › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A212. Liability and duty of receiving bank regarding unaccepted payment order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A212. Liability and duty of receiving bank regarding unaccepted payment order (2023)
content:
If a receiving bank fails to accept a payment order that it is obliged by express
   agreement to accept, the bank is liable for breach of the agreement to the extent
   provided in the agreement or in this division but does not otherwise have any duty
   to accept a payment order or, before acceptance, to take any action, or refrain from
   taking action, with respect to the order except as provided in this division or by
   express agreement.  Liability based on acceptance arises only when acceptance occurs as stated in section
   4A209 (relating to acceptance of payment order), and liability is limited to that
   provided in this division.  A receiving bank is not the agent of the sender or beneficiary of the payment order
   it accepts or of any other party to the funds transfer, and the bank owes no duty
   to any party to the funds transfer except as provided in this division or by express
   agreement.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A3. Execution of Sender's Payment Order by Receiving Bank›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A304. Duty of sender to report erroneously executed payment order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A3. Execution of Sender's Payment Order by Receiving Bank › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A304. Duty of sender to report erroneously executed payment order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A304. Duty of sender to report erroneously executed payment order (2023)
content:
If the sender of a payment order that is erroneously executed as stated in section
   4A303 (relating to erroneous execution of payment order) receives notification from
   the receiving bank that the order was executed or that the sender's account was debited
   with respect to the order, the sender has a duty to exercise ordinary care to determine,
   on the basis of information available to the sender, that the order was erroneously
   executed and to notify the bank of the relevant facts within a reasonable time, not
   exceeding 90 days, after the notification from the bank was received by the sender.  If the sender fails to perform that duty, the bank is not obliged to pay interest
   on any amount refundable to the sender under section 4A402(d) (relating to obligation
   of sender to pay receiving bank) for the period before the bank learns of the execution
   error.  The bank is not entitled to any recovery from the sender on account of a failure
   by the sender to perform the duty stated in this section.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A4. Payment›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A402. Obligation of sender to pay receiving bank
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A4. Payment › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A402. Obligation of sender to pay receiving bank
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A402. Obligation of sender to pay receiving bank (2023)
content:
(a) Scope of section.--This section is subject to sections 4A205 (relating to erroneous payment orders) and
      4A207 (relating to misdescription of beneficiary).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A4. Payment›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A404. Obligation of beneficiary's bank to pay and give notice to beneficiary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A4. Payment › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A404. Obligation of beneficiary's bank to pay and give notice to beneficiary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A404. Obligation of beneficiary's bank to pay and give notice to beneficiary (2023)
content:
(a) Obligation.--Subject to sections 4A211(e) (relating to cancellation and amendment of payment order)
      and 4A405(d) and (e) (relating to payment by beneficiary's bank to beneficiary), if
      a beneficiary's bank accepts a payment order, the bank is obliged to pay the amount
      of the order to the beneficiary of the order.  Payment is due on the payment date of the order, but if acceptance occurs on the
      payment date after the close of the funds-transfer business day of the bank, payment
      is due on the next funds-transfer business day.  If the bank refuses to pay after demand by the beneficiary and receipt of notice
      of particular circumstances that will give rise to consequential damages as a result
      of nonpayment, the beneficiary may recover damages resulting from the refusal to pay
      to the extent the bank had notice of the damages, unless the bank proves that it did
      not pay because of a reasonable doubt concerning the right of the beneficiary to payment.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A4. Payment›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A401. Payment date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A4. Payment › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A401. Payment date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A401. Payment date (2023)
content:
“Payment date”of a payment order means the day on which the amount of the order is payable to the
   beneficiary by the beneficiary's bank.  The payment date may be determined by instruction of the sender but cannot be earlier
   than the day the order is received by the beneficiary's bank and, unless otherwise
   determined, is the day the order is received by the beneficiary's bank.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A3. Execution of Sender's Payment Order by Receiving Bank›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A305. Liability for late or improper execution or failure to execute payment order
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A3. Execution of Sender's Payment Order by Receiving Bank › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A305. Liability for late or improper execution or failure to execute payment order
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A305. Liability for late or improper execution or failure to execute payment order (2023)
content:
(a) Liability for improper execution resulting in delay in payment.--If a funds transfer is completed but execution of a payment order by the receiving
      bank in breach of section 4A302 (relating to obligations of receiving bank in execution
      of payment order) results in delay in payment to the beneficiary, the bank is obliged
      to pay interest to either the originator or the beneficiary of the funds transfer
      for the period of delay caused by the improper execution.  Except as provided in subsection (c), additional damages are not recoverable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A502. Creditor process served on receiving bank; setoff by beneficiary's bank
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A502. Creditor process served on receiving bank; setoff by beneficiary's bank
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A502. Creditor process served on receiving bank; setoff by beneficiary's bank (2023)
content:
(a) Definition.--As used in this section, the term “creditor process” means levy, attachment, garnishment, notice of lien, sequestration or similar process
      issued by or on behalf of a creditor or other claimant with respect to an account.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A3. Execution of Sender's Payment Order by Receiving Bank›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A301. Execution and execution date
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A3. Execution of Sender's Payment Order by Receiving Bank › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A301. Execution and execution date
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A301. Execution and execution date (2023)
content:
(a) Execution.--A payment order is “executed” by the receiving bank when it issues a payment order
      intended to carry out the payment order received by the bank.  A payment order received by the beneficiary's bank can be accepted but cannot be
      executed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A504. Order in which items and payment orders may be charged to account; order of withdrawals from account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A504. Order in which items and payment orders may be charged to account; order of withdrawals from account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A504. Order in which items and payment orders may be charged to account; order of withdrawals from account (2023)
content:
(a) Priority among obligations paid from account.--If a receiving bank has received more than one payment order of the sender or one
      or more payment orders and other items that are payable from the sender's account,
      the bank may charge the sender's account with respect to the various orders and items
      in any sequence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A4. Payment›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A406. Payment by originator to beneficiary; discharge of underlying obligation
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A4. Payment › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A406. Payment by originator to beneficiary; discharge of underlying obligation

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A501. Variation by agreement and effect of funds-transfer system rule
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A501. Variation by agreement and effect of funds-transfer system rule
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A501. Variation by agreement and effect of funds-transfer system rule (2023)
content:
(a) Variation by agreement.--Except as otherwise provided in this division, the rights and obligations of a party
      to a funds transfer may be varied by agreement of the affected party.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 4A. Funds Transfers›Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A505. Preclusion of objection to debit of customer's account
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 4A. Funds Transfers › Chapter 4A5. Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A505. Preclusion of objection to debit of customer's account
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 4A505. Preclusion of objection to debit of customer's account (2023)
content:
If a receiving bank has received payment from its customer with respect to a payment
   order issued in the name of the customer as sender and accepted by the bank and the
   customer received notification reasonably identifying the order, the customer is precluded
   from asserting that the bank is not entitled to retain the payment unless the customer
   notifies the bank of the customer's objection to the payment within one year after
   the notification was received by the customer.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Short title of division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5101. Short title of division (2023)

content:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5107. Confirmer, nominated person and adviser
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5107. Confirmer, nominated person and adviser
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5107. Confirmer, nominated person and adviser (2023)
content:
(a) Rights and obligations of a confirmer.--A confirmer is directly obligated on a letter of credit and has the rights and obligations
      of an issuer to the extent of its confirmation.  The confirmer also has rights against and obligations to the issuer as if the issuer
      were an applicant and the confirmer had issued the letter of credit at the request
      and for the account of the issuer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Consideration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Consideration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5105. Consideration (2023)
content:
Consideration is not required to issue, amend, transfer or cancel a letter of credit,
   advice or confirmation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5113. Transfer by operation of law
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5113. Transfer by operation of law
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5113. Transfer by operation of law (2023)
content:
(a) Undisclosed successor.--A successor of a beneficiary may consent to amendments, sign and present documents
      and receive payment or other items of value in the name of the beneficiary without
      disclosing its status as a successor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5109. Fraud and forgery
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5109. Fraud and forgery
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5109. Fraud and forgery (2023)
content:
(a) Fraud and forgery generally.--If a presentation is made that appears on its face strictly to comply with the terms
      and conditions of the letter of credit, but a required document is forged or materially
      fraudulent, or honor of the presentation would facilitate a material fraud by the
      beneficiary on the issuer or applicant:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5112. Transfer of letter of credit
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5112. Transfer of letter of credit
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5112. Transfer of letter of credit (2023)
content:
(a) Transfer generally.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5113 (relating to transfer by operation of
      law), unless a letter of credit provides that it is transferable, the right of a beneficiary
      to draw or otherwise demand performance under a letter of credit may not be transferred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Issuer's rights and obligations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Issuer's rights and obligations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5108. Issuer's rights and obligations (2023)
content:
(a) Duty to honor, dishonor.--Except as otherwise provided in section 5109 (relating to fraud and forgery), an issuer
      shall honor a presentation that, as determined by the standard practice referred to
      in subsection (e), appears on its face strictly to comply with the terms and conditions
      of the letter of credit.  Except as otherwise provided in section 5113 (relating to transfer by operation
      of law) and unless otherwise agreed with the applicant, an issuer shall dishonor a
      presentation that does not appear so to comply.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5111. Remedies
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5111. Remedies
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5111. Remedies (2023)
content:
(a) Wrongful dishonor or repudiation before presentation.--If an issuer wrongfully dishonors or repudiates its obligation to pay money under
      a letter of credit before presentation, the beneficiary, successor or nominated person
      presenting on its own behalf may recover from the issuer the amount that is the subject
      of the dishonor or repudiation.  If the issuer's obligation under the letter of credit is not for the payment of
      money, the claimant may obtain specific performance or, at the claimant's election,
      recover an amount equal to the value of performance from the issuer.  In either case, the claimant may also recover incidental but not consequential damages.  The claimant is not obligated to take action to avoid damages that might be due
      from the issuer under this subsection.  If, although not obligated to do so, the claimant avoids damages, the claimant's
      recovery from the issuer must be reduced by the amount of damages avoided.  The issuer has the burden of proving the amount of damages avoided.  In the case of repudiation the claimant need not present any document.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Formal requirements
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Formal requirements
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5104. Formal requirements (2023)
content:
A letter of credit, confirmation, advice, transfer, amendment or cancellation may
   be issued in any form that is a signed record.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5110. Warranties
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5110. Warranties
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5110. Warranties (2023)
content: (a) Warranties generally.--If its presentation is honored, the beneficiary warrants:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Issuance, amendment, cancellation and duration
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Issuance, amendment, cancellation and duration
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5106. Issuance, amendment, cancellation and duration (2023)
content:
(a) Issuance;  revocability.--A letter of credit is issued and becomes enforceable according to its terms against
      the issuer when the issuer sends or otherwise transmits it to the person requested
      to advise or to the beneficiary.  A letter of credit is revocable only if it so provides.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5117. Subrogation of issuer, applicant and nominated person
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5117. Subrogation of issuer, applicant and nominated person
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5117. Subrogation of issuer, applicant and nominated person (2023)
content:
(a) Subrogation rights of issuer.--An issuer that honors a beneficiary's presentation is subrogated to the rights of
      the beneficiary to the same extent as if the issuer were a secondary obligor of the
      underlying obligation owed to the beneficiary and of the applicant to the same extent
      as if the issuer were the secondary obligor of the underlying obligation owed to the
      applicant.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5116. Choice of law and forum
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5116. Choice of law and forum
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5116. Choice of law and forum (2023)
content:
(a) Express choice of law.--The liability of an issuer, nominated person or advisor for action or omission is
      governed by the law of the jurisdiction chosen by an agreement in the form of a record
      signed by the affected parties or by a provision in the person's letter of credit,
      confirmation or other undertaking.  The jurisdiction whose law is chosen need not bear any relation to the transaction.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5118. Security interest of issuer or nominated person
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5118. Security interest of issuer or nominated person
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5118. Security interest of issuer or nominated person (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--An issuer or nominated person has a security interest in a document presented under
      a letter of credit to the extent that the issuer or nominated person honors or gives
      value for the presentation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 71. General›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Short title of division
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 71. General › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Short title of division
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7101. Short title of division (2023)
content:
This division shall be known and may be cited as the Uniform Commercial Code--Documents
   of Title.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5114. Assignment of proceeds
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5114. Assignment of proceeds
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5114. Assignment of proceeds (2023)
content:
(a) Definition.--As used in this section, the term “proceeds of a letter of credit” means the cash, check, accepted draft or other item of value paid or delivered upon
      honor or giving of value by the issuer or any nominated person under the letter of
      credit.  The term does not include a beneficiary's drawing rights or documents presented
      by the beneficiary.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5115. Statute of limitations
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5115. Statute of limitations
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5115. Statute of limitations (2023)
content:
An action to enforce a right or obligation arising under this division must be commenced
   within one year after the expiration date of the relevant letter of credit or one
   year after the cause of action accrues, whichever occurs later.  A cause of action accrues when the breach occurs, regardless of the aggrieved party's
   lack of knowledge of the breach, except that, in the event of a fraud or forgery adversely
   affecting the aggrieved party, a cause of action accrues on the earlier of the date
   on which the fraud or forgery was discovered by the aggrieved party or the date on
   which the fraud or forgery could have been discovered by the aggrieved party by the
   exercise of reasonable diligence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 71. General›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Reissuance in alternative medium
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 71. General › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Reissuance in alternative medium
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7105. Reissuance in alternative medium (2023)

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 71. General›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. Negotiable and nonnegotiable document of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 71. General › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. Negotiable and nonnegotiable document of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7104. Negotiable and nonnegotiable document of title (2023)
content:
(a) Negotiable.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (c), document of title is negotiable if,
      by its terms, the goods are to be delivered to the bearer or to the order of a named
      person.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7201. Person that may issue a warehouse receipt; storage under bond
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7201. Person that may issue a warehouse receipt; storage under bond
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7201. Person that may issue a warehouse receipt; storage under bond (2023)
content: (a) Issuer.--A warehouse receipt may be issued by any warehouse.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 71. General›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7102. Definitions and index of definitions

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7102. Definitions and index of definitions (2023)
content:
(a) Division 7 definitions.--The following words and phrases when used in this division shall have, unless the
      context clearly indicates otherwise, the meanings given to them in this subsection:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 71. General›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7103. Relation of division to treaty or statute
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 71. General › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7103. Relation of division to treaty or statute
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7103. Relation of division to treaty or statute (2023)
content:
(a) Hierarchy.--This division is subject to any treaty or statute of the United States or a regulatory
      statute of this Commonwealth to the extent the treaty, statute or regulatory statute
      is applicable.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7203. Liability for nonreceipt or misdescription
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7203. Liability for nonreceipt or misdescription
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7203. Liability for nonreceipt or misdescription (2023)
content:
A party to or purchaser for value in good faith of a document of title, other than
   a bill of lading, that relies upon the description of the goods in the document may
   recover from the issuer damages caused by the nonreceipt or misdescription of the
   goods, except to the extent that:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 5. Letters of Credit›Chapter 51. Letters of Credit›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Scope
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 5. Letters of Credit › Chapter 51. Letters of Credit › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Scope
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 5103. Scope (2023)
content:
(a) Applicability of division.--This division applies to letters of credit and to certain rights and obligations arising
      out of transactions involving letters of credit.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Duty of care; contractual limitation of warehouse's liability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Duty of care; contractual limitation of warehouse's liability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7204. Duty of care; contractual limitation of warehouse's liability (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of care.--A warehouse is liable for damages for loss of or injury to the goods caused by its
      failure to exercise care with regard to the goods that a reasonably careful person
      would exercise under similar circumstances.  Unless otherwise agreed, the warehouse is not liable for damages that could not
      have been avoided by the exercise of that care.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7206. Termination of storage at warehouse's option
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7206. Termination of storage at warehouse's option
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7206. Termination of storage at warehouse's option (2023)
content:
(a) Payment and removal.--A warehouse, by giving notice to the person on whose account the goods are held and
      any other person known to claim an interest in the goods, may require payment of any
      charges and removal of the goods from the warehouse at the termination of the period
      of storage fixed by the document of title or, if a period is not fixed, within a stated
      period not less than 30 days after the warehouse gives notice.  If the goods are not removed before the date specified in the notice, the warehouse
      may sell them pursuant to section 7210 (relating to enforcement of warehouse's lien).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202. Form of warehouse receipt; effect of omission
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202. Form of warehouse receipt; effect of omission
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7202. Form of warehouse receipt; effect of omission (2023)
content: (a) Form.--A warehouse receipt need not be in any particular form.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 71. General›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7106. Control of electronic document of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 71. General › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7106. Control of electronic document of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7106. Control of electronic document of title (2023)
content:
(a) Establishment.--A person has control of an electronic document of title if a system employed for evidencing
      the transfer of interests in the electronic document reliably establishes that person
      as the person to which the electronic document was issued or transferred.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7205. Title under warehouse receipt defeated in certain cases
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7205. Title under warehouse receipt defeated in certain cases
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7205. Title under warehouse receipt defeated in certain cases (2023)
content:
A buyer in ordinary course of business of fungible goods sold and delivered by a warehouse
   that is also in the business of buying and selling such goods takes the goods free
   of any claim under a warehouse receipt even if the receipt is negotiable and has been
   duly negotiated.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Liability for nonreceipt or misdescription; “said to contain”; “shipper's weight, load and count”; improper handling
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Liability for nonreceipt or misdescription; “said to contain”; “shipper's weight, load and count”; improper handling
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7301. Liability for nonreceipt or misdescription; “said to contain”; “shipper's weight, load and count”; improper handling (2023)
content:
(a) Liability.--A consignee of a nonnegotiable bill of lading which has given value in good faith,
      or a holder to which a negotiable bill has been duly negotiated, relying upon the
      description of the goods in the bill or upon the date shown in the bill, may recover
      from the issuer damages caused by the misdating of the bill or the nonreceipt or misdescription
      of the goods, except to the extent that the bill indicates that the issuer does not
      know whether any part or all of the goods in fact were received or conform to the
      description, such as in a case in which the description is in terms of marks or labels
      or kind, quantity or condition or the receipt or description is qualified by “contents
      or condition of contents of packages unknown,” “said to contain,” “shipper's weight,
      load and count” or words of similar import, if that indication is true.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7210. Enforcement of warehouse's lien (2023)
content: (a) Sale.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Through bills of lading and similar documents of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Through bills of lading and similar documents of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7302. Through bills of lading and similar documents of title (2023)
content:
(a) Liability of issuer.--The issuer of a through bill of lading or other document of title embodying an undertaking
      to be performed in part by a person acting as its agent or by a performing carrier
      is liable to any person entitled to recover on the bill or other document for any
      breach by the other person or the performing carrier of its obligation under the bill
      or other document.  However, to the extent that the bill or other document covers an undertaking to
      be performed overseas or in territory not contiguous to the continental United States
      or an undertaking including matters other than transportation, this liability for
      breach by the other person or the performing carrier may be varied by agreement of
      the parties.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7207. Goods must be kept separate; fungible goods

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7207. Goods must be kept separate; fungible goods (2023)
content: (a) Separation.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Lien of carrier

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7307. Lien of carrier (2023)
content: (a) Establishment.--

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Altered bills of lading
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Altered bills of lading
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7306. Altered bills of lading (2023)
content:
An unauthorized alteration or filling in of a blank in a bill of lading leaves the
   bill enforceable according to its original tenor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Tangible bills of lading in a set
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Tangible bills of lading in a set
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7304. Tangible bills of lading in a set (2023)
content:
(a) Prohibition.--Except as customary in international transportation, a tangible bill of lading may
      not be issued in a set of parts.  The issuer is liable for damages caused by violation of this subsection.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Destination bills
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Destination bills
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7305. Destination bills (2023)
content:
(a) Location.--Instead of issuing a bill of lading to the consignor at the place of shipment, a carrier,
      at the request of the consignor, may procure the bill to be issued at destination
      or at any other place designated in the request.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Diversion; reconsignment; change of instructions
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Diversion; reconsignment; change of instructions
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7303. Diversion; reconsignment; change of instructions (2023)
content:
(a) Proper instruction.--Unless the bill of lading otherwise provides, a carrier may deliver the goods to a
      person or destination other than that stated in the bill or may otherwise dispose
      of the goods, without liability for misdelivery, on instructions from:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7403. Obligation of bailee to deliver; excuse
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 74. citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7403. Obligation of bailee to deliver; excuse (2023)
content:
(a) Delivery.--A bailee shall deliver the goods to a person entitled under a document of title if
      the person complies with subsections (b) and (c) unless and to the extent that the
      bailee establishes any of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7208. Altered warehouse receipts
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 72. Warehouse Receipts: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7208. Altered warehouse receipts
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7208. Altered warehouse receipts (2023)
content:
If a blank in a negotiable tangible warehouse receipt has been filled in without authority,
   a good-faith purchaser for value and without notice of the lack of authority may treat
   the insertion as authorized.  Any other unauthorized alteration leaves any tangible or electronic warehouse receipt
   enforceable against the issuer according to its original tenor.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7401. Irregularities in issue of receipt or bill or conduct of issuer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7401. Irregularities in issue of receipt or bill or conduct of issuer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7401. Irregularities in issue of receipt or bill or conduct of issuer (2023)
content:
The obligations imposed by this division on an issuer apply to a document of title
   even if:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Duty of care; contractual limitation of carrier's liability
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Duty of care; contractual limitation of carrier's liability
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7309. Duty of care; contractual limitation of carrier's liability (2023)
content:
(a) Standard.--A carrier that issues a bill of lading, whether negotiable or nonnegotiable, shall
      exercise the degree of care in relation to the goods which a reasonably careful person
      would exercise under similar circumstances.  This subsection shall not affect any statute, regulation or rule of law that imposes
      liability upon a common carrier for damages not caused by its negligence.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7402. Duplicate document of title; overissue
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7402. Duplicate document of title; overissue
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7402. Duplicate document of title; overissue (2023)
content:
A duplicate or any other document of title purporting to cover goods already represented
   by an outstanding document of the same issuer does not confer any right in the goods,
   except as provided in the case of tangible bills of lading in a set of parts, overissue
   of documents for fungible goods, substitutes for lost, stolen or destroyed documents
   or substitute documents issued pursuant to section 7105 (relating to reissuance in
   alternative medium).  The issuer is liable for damages caused by its overissue or failure to identify
   a duplicate document by a conspicuous notation.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 73. Bills of Lading: Special Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7308. Enforcement of carrier's lien

      a holder to which a negotiable document of title has been duly negotiated acquires
      thereby all of the following:

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7404. No liability for good faith delivery pursuant to document of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 74. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: General Obligations › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7404. No liability for good faith delivery pursuant to document of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7404. No liability for good faith delivery pursuant to document of title (2023)
content:
A bailee that in good faith has received goods and delivered or otherwise disposed

The indorsement of a tangible document of title issued by a bailee does not make the

content:
A collecting bank or other intermediary known to be entrusted with documents of title
   on behalf of another or with collection of a draft or other claim against delivery
   of documents warrants by the delivery of the documents only its own good faith and
   authority even if the collecting bank or other intermediary has purchased or made
   advances against the claim or draft to be collected.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 76. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7601. Lost, stolen or destroyed documents of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7601. Lost, stolen or destroyed documents of title (2023)
content:
(a) Court orders.--If a document of title is lost, stolen or destroyed, a court may order delivery of
      the goods or issuance of a substitute document, and the bailee may, without liability
      to any person, comply with the order.  If the document was negotiable, a court may not order delivery of the goods or issuance
      of a substitute document without the claimant's posting security unless it finds that
      any person that may suffer loss as a result of nonsurrender of possession or control
      of the document is adequately protected against the loss.  If the document was nonnegotiable, the court may require security.  The court may also order payment of the bailee's reasonable costs and attorney fees
      in any action under this subsection.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7603. Conflicting claims; interpleader (2023)
content:
If more than one person claims title to or possession of the goods, the bailee is
   excused from delivery until the bailee has a reasonable time to ascertain the validity
   of the adverse claims or to commence an action for interpleader.  The bailee may assert an interpleader either in defending an action for nondelivery
   of the goods or by original action.

content:
The transferee of a negotiable tangible document of title has a specifically enforceable
   right to have its transferor supply any necessary indorsement, but the transfer becomes
   a negotiation only as of the time the indorsement is supplied.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8112. Creditor's legal process
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8112. Creditor's legal process

content:
(a) Interest of debtor in certificated security.--The interest of a debtor in a certificated security may be reached by a creditor only
      by actual seizure of the security certificate by the officer making the attachment
      or levy, except as otherwise provided in subsection (d).  However, a certificated security for which the certificate has been surrendered

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8111. Clearing corporation rules
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8111. Clearing corporation rules

content:
A rule adopted by a clearing corporation governing rights and obligations among the
   clearing corporation and its participants in the clearing corporation is effective
   even if the rule conflicts with this title and affects another party who does not
   consent to the rule.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 75. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Negotiation and Transfer›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7509. Adequate compliance with commercial contract

content:
Whether a document of title is adequate to fulfill the obligations of a contract for
   sale, a contract for lease, or the conditions of a letter of credit is determined
   by Division 2 (relating to sales), 2A (relating to leases) or 5 (relating to letters
   of credit).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title›Chapter 76. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Miscellaneous Provisions›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7602. Judicial process against goods covered by negotiable document of title
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 7. Warehouse Receipts, Bills of Lading and Other Documents of Title › Chapter 76. Warehouse Receipts and Bills of Lading: Miscellaneous Provisions › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7602. Judicial process against goods covered by negotiable document of title
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 7602. Judicial process against goods covered by negotiable document of title (2023)
content:
Unless a document of title was originally issued upon delivery of the goods by a person
   that did not have power to dispose of them, a lien does not attach by virtue of any
   judicial process to goods in the possession of a bailee for which a negotiable document
   of title is outstanding unless possession or control of the document is first surrendered
   to the bailee or the document's negotiation is enjoined.  The bailee may not be compelled to deliver the goods pursuant to process until possession
   or control of the document is surrendered to the bailee or to the court.  A purchaser of the document for value without notice of the process or injunction
   takes free of the lien imposed by judicial process.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8116. Securities intermediary as purchaser for value
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8116. Securities intermediary as purchaser for value
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8116. Securities intermediary as purchaser for value (2023)
content:
A securities intermediary that receives a financial asset and establishes a security
   entitlement to the financial asset in favor of an entitlement holder is a purchaser
   for value of the financial asset.  A securities intermediary that acquires a security entitlement to a financial asset
   from another securities intermediary acquires the security entitlement for value if
   the securities intermediary acquiring the security entitlement establishes a security
   entitlement to the financial asset in favor of an entitlement holder.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 81. Short Title and General Matters›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8113. Statute of frauds inapplicable

content:
A contract or modification of a contract for the sale or purchase of a security is
   enforceable whether or not there is a writing signed or record authenticated by a
   party against whom enforcement is sought, even if the contract or modification is
   not capable of performance within one year of its making.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8202. Issuer's responsibility and defenses; notice of defect or defense
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8202. Issuer's responsibility and defenses; notice of defect or defense (2023)
content:
(a) Terms included in certificated security.--Even against a purchaser for value and without notice, the terms of a certificated
      security include terms stated on the certificate and terms made part of the security
      by reference on the certificate to another instrument, indenture or document or to
      a constitution, statute, ordinance, rule, regulation, order or the like, to the extent
      the terms referred to do not conflict with terms stated on the certificate.  A reference under this subsection does not of itself charge a purchaser for value
      with notice of a defect going to the validity of the security, even if the certificate
      expressly states that a person accepting it admits notice.  The terms of an uncertificated security include those stated in any instrument,
      indenture or document or in a constitution, statute, ordinance, rule, regulation,
      order or the like, pursuant to which the security is issued.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8207. Rights and duties of issuer with respect to registered owners (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Before due presentment for registration of transfer of a certificated security in
      registered form or of an instruction requesting registration of transfer of an uncertificated
      security, the issuer or indenture trustee may treat the registered owner as the person
      exclusively entitled to vote, receive notifications and otherwise exercise all the
      rights and powers of an owner.

title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 82. Issue and Issuer › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8209. Issuer's lien
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8209. Issuer's lien (2023)
content:
A lien in favor of an issuer upon a certificated security is valid against a purchaser
   only if the right of the issuer to the lien is noted conspicuously on the security
   certificate.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8302. Rights of purchaser (2023)
content:
(a) Rights acquired by purchaser.--Except as otherwise provided in subsections (b) and (c), a purchaser of a certificated
      or uncertificated security acquires all rights in the security that the transferor
      had or had power to transfer.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8304. Indorsement (2023)
content:
(a) Blank and special indorsement.--An indorsement may be in blank or special.  An indorsement in blank includes an indorsement to bearer.  A special indorsement specifies to whom a security is to be transferred or who has
      power to transfer it.  A holder may convert a blank indorsement to a special indorsement.

content:
(a) Instruction originated by appropriate person.--If an instruction has been originated by an appropriate person but is incomplete in
      any other respect, any person may complete it as authorized and the issuer may rely
      on it as completed, even though it has been completed incorrectly.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8307. Purchaser's right to requisites for registration of transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 83. Transfer of Certificated and Uncertificated Securities › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8307. Purchaser's right to requisites for registration of transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8307. Purchaser's right to requisites for registration of transfer (2023)
content:
Unless otherwise agreed, the transferor of a security on due demand shall supply the
   purchaser with proof of authority to transfer or with any other requisite necessary
   to obtain registration of the transfer of the security, but, if the transfer is not
   for value, a transferor need not comply unless the purchaser pays the necessary expenses.  If the transferor fails within a reasonable time to comply with the demand, the
   purchaser may reject or rescind the transfer.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8407. Authenticating trustee, transfer agent and registrar
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8407. Authenticating trustee, transfer agent and registrar
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8407. Authenticating trustee, transfer agent and registrar (2023)
content:
A person acting as authenticating trustee, transfer agent, registrar or other agent
   for an issuer in the registration of a transfer of its securities, in the issue of
   new security certificates or uncertificated securities or in the cancellation of surrendered
   security certificates has the same obligation to the holder or owner of a certificated
   or uncertificated security with regard to the particular functions performed as the
   issuer has in regard to those functions.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8403. Demand that issuer not register transfer
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8403. Demand that issuer not register transfer
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8403. Demand that issuer not register transfer (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A person who is an appropriate person to make an indorsement or originate an instruction
      may demand that the issuer not register transfer of a security by communicating to
      the issuer a notification that identifies the registered owner and the issue of which
      the security is a part and provides an address for communications directed to the
      person making the demand.  The demand is effective only if it is received by the issuer at a time and in a
      manner affording the issuer reasonable opportunity to act on it.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8502. Assertion of adverse claim against entitlement holder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8502. Assertion of adverse claim against entitlement holder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8502. Assertion of adverse claim against entitlement holder (2023)
content:
An action based on an adverse claim to a financial asset, whether framed in conversion,
   replevin, constructive trust, equitable lien or other theory, may not be asserted
   against a person who acquires a security entitlement under section 8501 (relating
   to securities account;  acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary)
   for value and without notice of the adverse claim.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8501. Securities account; acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8501. Securities account; acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8501. Securities account; acquisition of security entitlement from securities intermediary (2023)
content:
(a) Definition of “securities account”.--“Securities account”means an account to which a financial asset is or may be credited in accordance with
      an agreement under which the person maintaining the account undertakes to treat the
      person for whom the account is maintained as entitled to exercise the rights that
      comprise the financial asset.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8503. Property interest of entitlement holder in financial asset held by securities intermediary
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8503. Property interest of entitlement holder in financial asset held by securities intermediary
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8503. Property interest of entitlement holder in financial asset held by securities intermediary (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--To the extent necessary for a securities intermediary to satisfy all security entitlements
      with respect to a particular financial asset, all interests in that financial asset
      held by the securities intermediary are held by the securities intermediary for the
      entitlement holders, are not property of the securities intermediary and are not subject
      to claims of creditors of the securities intermediary, except as otherwise provided
      in section 8511 (relating to priority among security interests and entitlement holders).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 84. Registration›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8406. Obligation to notify issuer of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 84. Registration › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8406. Obligation to notify issuer of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8406. Obligation to notify issuer of lost, destroyed or wrongfully taken security certificate (2023)
content:
If a security certificate has been lost, apparently destroyed or wrongfully taken
   and the owner fails to notify the issuer of that fact within a reasonable time after
   the owner has notice of it and the issuer registers a transfer of the security before
   receiving notification, the owner may not assert against the issuer a claim for registering
   the transfer under section 8404 (relating to wrongful registration) or a claim to
   a new security certificate under section 8405 (relating to replacement of lost, destroyed
   or wrongfully taken security certificate).

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8504. Duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8504. Duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8504. Duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--A securities intermediary shall promptly obtain and thereafter maintain a financial
      asset in a quantity corresponding to the aggregate of all security entitlements it
      has established in favor of its entitlement holders with respect to that financial
      asset.  The securities intermediary may maintain those financial assets directly or through
      one or more other securities intermediaries.

content:

      (relating to duty of securities intermediary to maintain financial asset) through
      8508 (relating to duty of securities intermediary to change entitlement holder's position
      to other form of security holding) is the subject of another statute, regulation or
      rule, compliance with that statute, regulation or rule satisfies the duty.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8510. Rights of purchaser of security entitlement from entitlement holder
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8510. Rights of purchaser of security entitlement from entitlement holder
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8510. Rights of purchaser of security entitlement from entitlement holder (2023)
content:
(a) Action based on adverse claim to financial asset or security entitlement.--In a case not covered by the priority rules in Division 9 (relating to secured transactions)
      or the rules stated in subsection (c), an action based on an adverse claim to a financial
      asset or security entitlement, whether framed in conversion, replevin, constructive
      trust, equitable lien or other theory, may not be asserted against a person who purchases
      a security entitlement, or an interest therein, from an entitlement holder if the
      purchaser gives value, does not have notice of the adverse claim and obtains control.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9105. Control of electronic copy of record evidencing chattel paper (2023)
content:
(a) General rule;  control of electronic copy of record evidencing chattel paper.--A purchaser has control of an authoritative electronic copy of a record evidencing
      chattel paper if a system employed for evidencing the assignment of interests in the
      chattel paper reliably establishes the purchaser as the person to which the authoritative
      electronic copy was assigned.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Chapter 91. General Provisions›Subchapter A. Short Title, Definitions and General Concepts›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9107. Control of letter-of-credit right
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Chapter 91. General Provisions › Subchapter A. Short Title, Definitions and General Concepts › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9107. Control of letter-of-credit right
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9107. Control of letter-of-credit right (2023)
content:
A secured party has control of a letter-of-credit right to the extent of any right
   to payment or performance by the issuer or any nominated person if the issuer or nominated
   person has consented to an assignment of proceeds of the letter of credit under section
   5114(c) (relating to recognition of assignment of proceeds) or otherwise applicable
   law or practice.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 8. Investment Securities›Chapter 85. Security Entitlements›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8511. Priority among security interests and entitlement holders
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 8. Investment Securities › Chapter 85. Security Entitlements › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8511. Priority among security interests and entitlement holders
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 8511. Priority among security interests and entitlement holders (2023)
content:
(a) General rule.--Except as otherwise provided in subsections (b) and (c), if a securities intermediary
      does not have sufficient interests in a particular financial asset to satisfy both
      its obligations to entitlement holders who have security entitlements to that financial
      asset and its obligation to a creditor of the securities intermediary who has a security
      interest in that financial asset, the claims of entitlement holders other than the
      creditor have priority over the claim of the creditor.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9207. Rights and duties of secured party having possession or control of collateral (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of care when secured party in possession.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (d), a secured party shall use reasonable
      care in the custody and preservation of collateral in the secured party's possession.  In the case of chattel paper or an instrument, reasonable care includes taking necessary
      steps to preserve rights against prior parties unless otherwise agreed.

path: Pennsylvania Statutes›Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code›Division 9. Secured Transactions›Subchapter B. Rights and Duties›PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9207. Rights and duties of secured party having possession or control of collateral
title: PA Statutes › Pennsylvania Statutes › Title 13 Pa.C.S.A. Commercial Code › Division 9. Secured Transactions › Subchapter B. Rights and Duties › PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9207. Rights and duties of secured party having possession or control of collateral
citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9207. Rights and duties of secured party having possession or control of collateral (2023)
content:
(a) Duty of care when secured party in possession.--Except as otherwise provided in subsection (d), a secured party shall use reasonable
      care in the custody and preservation of collateral in the secured party's possession.  In the case of chattel paper or an instrument, reasonable care includes taking necessary
      steps to preserve rights against prior parties unless otherwise agreed.

citation: PA Stat § PA ST 13 Pa.C.S.A. § 9206. Security interest arising in purchase or delivery of financial asset (2023)
content:
(a) Security interest when person buys through securities intermediary.--A security interest in favor of a securities intermediary attaches to a person's security
